Agartala.x: Agartala, the capital city of Tripura, is the second-largest city in North-Eastern India after Guwahati. It is on the banks of the Haora River, near the Bangladesh border, about 90 km (55 mi) east of Bangladesh's capital Dhaka. Agartala is the third international internet gateway after Mumbai and Chennai.

see.d: Built by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya during 1899-1901, this is a two-storey mansion, with mixed type of architecture with three high domes, the central one being 86 feet high.
It handles the largest number of visitors to and from neighbouring Bangladesh.
The main place of worship for the Muslims of Tripura, this imposing mosque bears testimony to the devotion and piety of a remarkable individual.
Famous not only from the pilgrim's point of view, this temple is also a remarkable architectural feat with its octagonal base and its impressive pradhakshin patha round the sanctum.
The idol of Lord Krishna was installed by Krishnananda Sevayet of Laxmi Narayan temple in the 1970s.
The last king of Tripura founded this in 1947.

do.d: Inaugurated in 2003, it is a happy hub for people of all ages looking to get away from the city.
A park with lush greenery and an abundance of flowers, home to children and young people looking for a peaceful getaway.

Agonda.x: Agonda is a beach area in the southernmost Canacona taluka of the Indian state of Goa.

see.d: An old fort built by a Hindu king named for Lord Rama, after a few battles, it was eventually taken over by the Portuguese.

Agra.x: Agra, a city around 200 km from Delhi, is home to two UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal and the Agra Fort. There are also many other buildings and tombs from Agra's days of glory as the capital of the Mughal Empire, as well as the abandoned city of Fatehpur Sikri outside town, itself a World Heritage Site. Besides these three World Heritage Sites, the city has little else to recommend it.

Ahmedabad.x: Ahmedabad is the seventh largest city in India with a population of 8.5 million. Although it is the commercial hub of one of the most prosperous states of India, Gujarat, it's not the state capital, which is its twin city of Gandhinagar, 30 km (19 mi) to the north. Ahmedabad is a good example of contrast between the materialistic attitude and the spirituality of self-renunciation.

Ahmednagar.x: Ahmednagar, officially Ahilyanagar, has more than 500 years history traced back to 1490, with find traces of Nizamshahi, Shah Jahan and Peshwas until the British took over Ahmednagar.

see.d: Built by Ahmed Nizam Shah in 1490, this is an oval-shaped fort, which features 18-m-high walls, supported by 22 bastions.
10 km east of the city, on a hill 215-245 m (700-800 feet) above the city level and on the left of the Ahmednagar-Shevgaon road stands the tomb of the Nizamshahi Minister, Salabat Khan II,…
A fine black stone mausoleum with a domed roof, within which glitter golden Quranic inscriptions, holds the tomb of Ahmed Nizam Shah, founder and 'faujdar' of Ahmednagar.
The museum has a rich collection of tanks used during different periods.
Shani-Shinganapur lies 6km off Ghodegaon- an important market place along Ahmednagar-Aurangabad Road. Ghodegaon is 35 km from Ahmednagar. The village has no doors.
Greatest Literature in Marathi - Jnyaneswari was written here by Sant Jnyaneshwar'. Newasa Phata on Nagar Aurangabad Road, 40 km from Ahmednagar.

Ajmer.x: Ajmer, in Rajasthan, western India, is very popular as a gateway to Pushkar, and an important Islamic pilgrimage site, the shrine of the Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti.

see.d: Emperor Akbar's royal residence, now serves as a museum, which houses an excellent collection of Mughal and Rajput armour, and some fine sculptures.
The dam built by the grand father of Emperor Prithviraj Chouhan in Ajmer. Daulat Bag is an enormous park by the side of Ana Sagar and is a nice place to relax.
Must go to Pushkar to visit this amazing Brahma Temple near Pushkar Lake, go shopping in the narrow but ethnic and colourful lanes of the marketplace, eat traditional foods as well as…
The Dargah is a major pilgrimage centre of Muslim religion and holds a special place in the life of the Sufi saint Khwaja Moin Uddin Chisty(RA).
Only if it is rainy season and you don't have old members in your group.
A Jain place on the outskirts (Kishangarh bypass). This is a good place to visit, has a very big temple and offer authentic Jain food (You have to check the meal hours in advance, they are…

Aksa.x: Aksa is a popular beach vacation spot at Malad close to Malvani, Mumbai.

Alappuzha.x: The city of Alappuzha, also known as Alleppey, is situated in Kerala. Alappuzha is the smallest district in Kerala with a long coastline and many lagoons and backwaters. It is often called the Venice of the East due to the canals that connect it to Kerala's famous snaking backwaters.

see.d: This temple is very calm and quiet temple. Allepey has a very small Jain population.
This is a 9th century black granite statue of the Buddha, locally known as Karumadi Kuttan. This statue is protected by the Archeological survey of India.
A good destination for a day trip, it is about 16 km north of Alappuzha town. This area also has the Mahadeva temple and Arthunkal church.
Alleppey has a high percentage of Christians. St. Mary’s Church (Champakulam) is believed to be one of the seven churches established by St. Thomas.
This temple was built in the 15th century. Of interest here is an extremely distinctive Paal-Payasam (a sweet milk dessert made out of rice, with jaggery, in milk).

do.d: A fairly large, flat and clean beach. An old pier, which was at one point used for trade and had three railway lines, still stands.
Ayurveda centre. It is run by a traditional family of ayurvedic doctors. The hospital and spa are constructed in Kerala traditional architecture style but contains a modern facility.
- Alappuzha is known for its Snake Boat races. Held on the second Saturday of August, the competition is named after Jawaharlal Nehru who inaugurated the event in 1952.
Try Kainakkary, a short distance from Viluakkuthara.

Aligarh.x: Aligarh, a city in the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh, is famous for its locks as well as the Aligarh Muslim University.

see.n: Ibn Sina Academy of Medieval Medicine and Sciences
see.d: Museum on Indian heritage and Library on History of Medieval Medicine

Aluva.x: Aluva, formerly Alwaye, is the second largest town in Greater Kochi agglomeration and an important commercial town in Kerala. The town is famous for its festivals, large river banks and temples. Many of Kochinites (people of Kochi, as popularly known) do prefer to live in Aluva, while working in Ernakulam, considering quiet cityscape, waterfront facility and presence of large commercial areas.

see.d: Once the summer palace of Travancore Royal family, today it's one of the largest archeological palaces in Kerala.
The Marthanada Varma Bridge is considered as icon of the town. Though nothing special about this bridge, this bridge was the first bridge laid across the mighty Periyar.
The Shiva temple of Aluva is one of the most famous Shiva temples in south India. Legend says, the idol (Lingam) has risen out of the sand of the river bank, naturally.
Uliyanoor Temple is a historical Temple believed to have been built By Perunthachan

do.n: CIAL Golf Course and Country Club
do.d: A golf course managed by the Airport themselves. Not very amateur friendly but seasoned players can enjoy the place. A restaurant exists too

Alwar.x: Alwar, a city of 460,000 people (2018) in Rajasthan, is surrounded by the Aravalli Hills. It was one of the various princely states of Rajputana during the British times.

see.d: One of the few forts built in Rajasthan prior to the rise of the Mughals. Permission from the superintendent of police is required prior to visiting (however this is easy to get).
A famous TapoBhumi of Raja BhartriHari
At former city palace.
A place where "Pandvas" stayed at the time of agyatvaas. There is a Hanuman temple which have the unique Hanuman idol (in the form of relax). It is placed in the middle of Sariska jungle.

do.d: It is a lake constructed by King of Alwar.
One of the most famous national parks in India designated as a tiger reserve.
A decent lake named Siliserh lake along with government hotel (RTDC hotel) also named as Silliserh Hotel with restaurant and boarding facility except during rainy season boating facility is…

Ambala.x: Ambala is a city in Haryana in North India.

see.d: One of the oldest airbases in the world, the home base of Jaguar Squadron.
Christian cemetery on same road.

do.d: A popular place for running, yoga and other forms of exercise.

Kochi.x: Kochi, formerly Cochin, is a cosmopolitan city in Kerala (Keralam) with a bustling commercial port. Kochi is the financial and commercial capital of Kerala and, with a population of more than 2.1 million (2011), the biggest conurbation in the state.

Alipurduar.x: Alipurduar, a town on the east bank of Kaljani River in North Bengal, acts as a stopover to the surrounding tourist attractions in Alipurduar district.

Adilabad.x: Surrounded by a variety of landscapes, the city of Adilabad in the Indian state of Telangana is a fine base to explore the sights of the surrounding area.

see.d: These waterfalls, highest in Telangana, are some 30 km out of town. They are a popular day trip, not only from Adilabad but even from Hyderabad.
21 km out of town, this temple complex has all the architectural treats of the Jain temple style. In it, you'll find stone inscriptions in prakrit, including 10 ślokas, or verses.

Amaravati.x: Amaravati or Amaravathi is the capital of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, on the banks of the Krishna River, opposite Vijayawada (Bezawada) and northeast of Guntur. Once the capital of the Satavahana dynasty and a major Buddhist centre in ancient times, Amaravati has become a cautionary tale in urban planning in the 21st century, where a change in state administration put a megaproject into a halt, with a series of legal battles for a few years. Nonetheless, Amaravati, Guntur and Vijayawada together constitute the Capital Region (CR) of Andhra Pradesh, the modern heart of the state since 2014.

see.d: The ruins of an ancient Buddhist site, probably built in phases between the third century BCE and about 250 CE.
Serves Lord Amareswara, has a history of about 2,000 years.
This tall statue of the Buddha in a meditative (Dhyana) position was completed in 2015 to celebrate the Buddhist heritage of the city in ancient times.
One of the eight sacred places of Lord Vishnu in India. It is also known for being one of the eight mahakshetras Narasimha in India.
Built across the river Krishna connecting this city with Vijayawada, Prakasam Barrage has created a panoramic lake.
on the banks of river Krishna with a vast sandy beach for recreation and leisure. The famous Someswara Swamy temple is situated here.

Adichunchanagiri Hills.x: Adichunchanagiri Hills, is a tourist place near Nagamangala town in Mandya (district), Karnataka State, India.

do.d: It is a pleasant drive from Nagamangala to Adichunchanagiri Hills. Small villages like Tolali,Anchebuhalli and Doodajilla are on the way.
Riverside temple

Ambika Kalna.x: Ambika Kalna, or simply Kalna, is a town in the Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal, India. Situated on the western bank of the Bhagirathi River, it is also called the Temple City for the number of old temples found here. The town got its name from the deity Ma Ambika (incarnation of Goddess Kali) of Siddheswari Temple.

see.d: The temple complex of Nava Kailash consists of 108 Shiva Temples built in aat - chala style. The temple are arranged in two concentric circles.
The Nava Kailash complex is flanked on either side by two pancha ratna (five-pinnacled) temples. The Jalesvar Temple lies on the west.
The Nava Kailash complex is flanked on either side by two pancha ratna (five-pinnacled) temples. The Ratneshwar Temple lies on the east.
Kalna is known for its terracotta temples and the Pratapeswar Temple definitely stands out among the numerous temples of Kalna.
Just north of the Pratapeswar Temple is the Ras Mancha. The octagonal structure has triple arched entrance on all three sides and at the centre is a hexagonal pavilion crowned with a dome.
Built in 1739, the Lalji Temple is the oldest temple in the Rajbari Complex. It was built by Braja Kishori Devi, the wife of Maharaja Jagat Ram. It houses the idol of Radha – Krishna.

Ambikapur.x: Ambikapur is the northern city of Chhattisgarh. It is also the headquarters of Surguja District and Surguja Division.

see.d: It is a white, two-storey palace. This palace is open for public only on the day of Dussehra every year.

Ambernath.x: Ambernath is a suburb near Thane, in the North Konkan region of western Maharashtra.

Amravati.x: Amravati, also known as Amraoti, a city in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra, is believed to be the city of Lord Indra, the king of all gods. The city boasts of historical temples of Goddess Amba, Lord Shri Krishna and Shri Venkateshwara.

see.d: This temple is in the heart of Amravati city. It is believed that Shri Krishna abducted Rukmini from this temple, and married her.
1 km away from Dasturnagar Square on the Malkhed Railway Road. Built in the year 1888 on a small spring called Kali Nadi, this small reservoir was built to supply drinking water to Amravati…
it lies on Badnera road. It has very calm surrounding. Gives mental piece & relief.
Located in the heart of the city at Rallies Plot. This temple has beautiful idols of Lord Krishna and Radha, Lord Ram and Sita, Lord Ganesh, Lord Shiva and Rani Satiji.
This temple has beautiful idols of Lord Krishna and Radha. There is also an idol of Shri Sant Jalaram Bappa. There is a small park for children behind this temple.
This was built to deliver a clean and fresh water supply to Amravati Camp. There is a small garden with a zoo here. People usually come here during weekends and enjoy boating.

Amritsar.x: Amritsar is a city in the state of Punjab, India. It is the holiest city in Sikhism. Amritsar is one of the largest cities in the Indian state of Punjab and is the spiritual and cultural centre of the Sikh religion.

see.d: The site of the 1919 Amritsar massacre, turned into a park memorial. On April 13 of that year, British Indian Army soldiers opened fire on an unarmed gathering of men, women and children.
A large 1760 fort that is being turned into a tourist spot with several museums and performances. The fort was built of bricks and lime by Gujjar Singh Bhangi and armed with 25 cannons.
This is a beautiful garden. A tribute to Guru Ram Das, the founder of the city. Famed as the summer palace of the Maharaja Ranjit Singh (Ranjit Singh Panorama?), it has now been converted…
Subhas Chandra Bose (Netaji) was an important leader in the Indian struggle for independence. He led the Indian National Army and formed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind in exile.

see.n: Summer Palace of Maharaja Ranjit Singh'
see.d: The palace houses a museum, exhibiting oil paintings, miniatures, coins and weapons from the Sikh period.
This is a great viewpoint over the city and the nearby Golden Temple. It is standing in another Gurdwara, namely the one of Baba Atal Rai Sahib Ji.

do.d: Despite visiting Amritsar and Golden temple several times, visitors find Heritage Walk experience extremely enjoyable and informative.
As you move through narrow path of old city and some other heritage buildings, you can see stalls selling everything from jootis to roasted sweet potatoes.

Anand.x: Anand is a medium-sized city in Central Gujarat, popularly known as the "milk capital of India."

see.d: Asia's largest dairy.

do.d: There are many cinemas in the city.

Anantapur.x: Anantapur is a city in Andhra Pradesh in India with historic forts and temples.

see.d: The Clock Tower is a historic structure at the centre of Anantapur town, built in memory of martyrs of the Indian freedom movement by the initiative of M.
to see ancient architecture.
7 km from town. Built by ISKON in 2008.
This is holy place both for Hindus and Muslims. All the temples are located at one place (Shirdi Sai Baba, Ayyappa, Ganesh & Hanuman Temples)
It's a peaceful place and very famous.

do.d: An outdoor restaurant.

Anantnag.x: Anantnag is a city in India, and the second largest city in the Kashmir Valley. Its district headquarters has the largest number of tourist spots in the Kashmir valley.

see.d: This Kashmiri Hindu temple is an important and protected archeological site. The ruins remain impressive with its decorations and construction.
With terraced lawns, cascading fountains, and paint-box-bright flowerbeds, they are most charming for tourists.

Ankola.x: Ankola is a small town in Uttara Kannada.

Annavaram.x: Annavaram is a temple town in central Andhra Pradesh, famous for the Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Vari temple located on a hillock. The town itself is on the banks of the Pampa River.

Aranmula.x: Aranmula is a city in Kerala in India.

see.d: During Onam.
A school of traditional art founded by French artist Louba Schild. It imparts training in the traditional arts like Kathakali, classical dances, classical music, as well as Kalaripayattu.

Aruvankadu.x: Aruvankadu, is a small town located in the Nilgiris of Tamil Nadu in India between Coonoor and Ooty, at distances 5 km and 12 km respectively. It houses the Cordite Factory, one of the 40 Indian Ordnance Factories, and one of the oldest, established in 1903. It is also the place where Robert Hanbury Brown, a British astronomer and physicist was born.

Arcot.x: Arcot is an historic town in the northern part of Tamil Nadu, the southernmost state in India.

see.n: Kathiyavadi Panchapandavar Ancient Jain Hill and Caves

Asansol.x: Asansol is the headquarters of the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal. It is at the centre of a major industrial area and the second largest urban agglomeration in the state.

see.d: This stone temple is built over a platform with a Bengal hut-shaped roof and arched entrance. The temple dates to about the 14th century CE.
A small shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali, it is the oldest temple of Asansol.
Operated by Steel Authority of India (SAIL), the IISCO Steel Plant is one of the major steel plants in West Bengal.

do.d: You can watch all newly released movies here. Good cinema hall; one of the biggest with a seating capacity of almost 1800.
A beautiful park on the banks of the Damodar River. A cast iron statue of Nehru, casted by IISCO, is in the park. There is an eatery in the park.
A picnic spot with a lake for boating and beautiful garden of flowers.
There are facilities for paddle boating and a few rides for children. Nice place to spend the evening.

Attingal.x: Attingal is a town in Thiruvananthapuram District, Kerala State, India. It is the second biggest town in Thiruvananthapuram District. Headquarters of Chiyrinkil Taluk.

Aurangabad.x: Aurangabad, now known officially as Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, is a city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It sees a lot of international tourist traffic due to its proximity to the two UNESCO World Heritage Sites, namely Ajanta and Ellora caves. Aurangabad, a dream destination of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, founded in 1610, is known today as one of the four important cities in Maharashtra.

see.d: This is a fine piece of architecture, is presented in the most unembellished manner.
A replica of the Taj Mahal, the Bibi-ka-Maqbara is the only example of the Mughal architecture of its kind in the Deccan plateau.

see.n: History Museum - Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University
see.d: It has on display a good number of ancient Indian paintings, coins, fabrics, arms, artifacts, etc.
This is a 17th-century water mill. The name has been derived from the mill that crushed grain for the pilgrims.
As the name suggests, this museum is dedicated to the great warrior of Maharashtra - Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. A number of exhibits associated with Lord Shivaji are on display.
an old historic monument now converted into museum houses a variety of ancient Indian pottery, dresses, remains of local palaces and antiques of daily use.

do.d: This is a beautiful landscaped garden, with good variety of trees and shrubs. There is a small aquarium inside the garden, however the biggest attraction is the Siddharth Garden Zoo, with a…

Mithila.x: Mithila, also called Tirhut, Tirabhukti and Mithilanchal, is the northern region of Bihar, India.

Perinthalmanna.x: Perinthalmanna , or Perintalmanna, is in Malappuram District, in the Malabar region in Kerala, India. Perintalmanna is known as the hospital city of Kerala.

see.d: Temple town of Malabar. This little town was the erstwhile capital of Walluvanad, a kingdom that existed from about 500 AD till the British Era.
Thanakursi Narasimha Kshethram.
Birthplace of E.M.S. Namboodiripad, famous political leader of Kerala.

Arsikere.x: Arsikere is in Hassan district, India.

Andul.x: Andul is a town west of Howrah city, in the Howrah district of southern West Bengal.

see.d: A palace built by Raja Rajnarayan Bahadur in 1834. His family now owns a cinema hall and a local market as well.
A temple dedicated to Siddheswari Shankari Mata, the patron goddess of Andul. It was founded in 1772 by Bhairavicharan Vidyasagar.

do.n: Durga Puja of Dutta Chowdhury family
do.d: Among the oldest in Bengal, the Durga Puja was started by Kashiswar Dutta Chowdhury around 400 years ago.

Anakapalle.x: Anakapalle or Anakapalli is a suburb west of Visakhapatnam in northern Andhra Pradesh.

see.d: It offers architectural remnants of the Buddhist period, one of the earliest of its class in Southern India.
A popular pilgrimage site among locals. The name "Panchadharla" is derived from the five jets of water coming out of the five fountains that receive water supply from a natural perennial…
A bird sanctuary with a unique and endangered forest.

Ariyalur.x: Ariyalur is a town in southern Tamil Nadu.

Chola Nadu.x: Chola Nadu consists of the Kaveri Delta, the homeland of the Chola dynasty in Tamil Nadu.

Auroville.x: Auroville is a small town 6 km north of Pondicherry, in the Viluppuram district of Tamil Nadu. This town was a vision of The Mother from Sri Aurobindo Ashram at Pondicherry as it's an international town. She envisioned a town where unity will be celebrated and all will have a spiritual vocation.

see.d: Meaning "Temple of the Mother" in Sanskrit, this is the geographical and spiritual heart of Auroville.
Walking distance from the Auroville Bus Stop on ECR (East Coast Road), Auro Beach is considered one of the best beaches on India's Eastern Coastline although it is still very polluted.
Run by the inhabitants.
Radiating from Matri Mandir, are four "zones" of the City Area: the "Residential Zone", "Industrial Zone", "Cultural (& Educational) Zone" and "International Zone".
A beautiful building with a Dalai Lama seat.
A beautiful building in a green surroundings.

do.d: 9AM to 4:30PM (with a break from noon to 2PM).

Awadh.x: Awadh is the central region of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, known as the granary of India. It is the centre of various period films of Bollywood and modern films.

Ayodhya.x: Ayodhya is an ancient city in the Awadh region of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. Ayodhya is one of the major holy cities of Hinduism. It has a central role in the ancient Indian epic, the Ramayana, whose protagonist Lord Rama believed to be Lord Vishnu incarnated on Earth as the prince of Ayodhya.

see.d: The colossal temple in Ayodhya, built on the supposed birthplace of Rama. Although visited by pilgrims throughout the year, this sacred place attracts devotees from all over India and…
Tomb and still one of the highest buildings in Faizabad.
Gulab Bari translates to "garden of roses" and this tomb of the 16th century ruler of the Kingdom of Oudh, Shuja-ud-Daula, has both a magnificent mausoleum and a rose garden.
This is where Rama's brother Lakshmana is said to have voluntarily given up his life-an act called samadhi. Another version says that he gave up living after he broke a vow.
A former Buddhist vihara (cave with cells) that became a Hindu temple. It is dotted with little shrines and if you stand on the topmost terrace you get a splendid view of Ayodhya, one that…
The legendary Korean queen Heo Hwang-ok, also known as Suriratna, is believed according to the Samguk yusa to have been an Indian princess from Ayuta, nowadays identified with Ayodhya.

do.n: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar International Sports Stadium
do.d: A multi-purpose stadium with a capacity of 30,000.
Constitutes a circular journey of 28 miles made once a year on the occasion of Akshainaumi, which is completed within 24 hours.
The enactment of the story of Lord Rama is believed to have been started by great Saint Tulsidas. The Ramcharitmanas, written by him till today forms the basis of Ram Lila performances.
Ayodhya, the holy city of the sacred pilgrim centre of Hindus plays host to the Ram Navmi Festival in the month of April.
This mela celebrates the playful spirit of the deities. On the third day of the second half of Shravan, images of the deities (specially of Rama, Lakshman and Sita) are placed in swings in…

Badami.x: Badami, formerly Vatapi, is a city in the Bagalkot district of Northern Karnataka, in Southern India. It is a historical place.

see.d: The main attractions of Badami are its caves. There are four main caves. The first one, dedicated to Shiva, was excavated by the Chalukyas in 550 AD. The second one is dedicated to Vishnu.
A cluster of sandstone shrines dedicated to the deity Bhutanatha, built between the 7th and 11th century CE.
Contains sculptures of various era from the region. To the left of it starts the footpath going up 300 stairs leading to the Lower and Upper Shivalayas.
When facing the museum, walk through the gate on your left and follow the path up the 300 stairs or so.
This temple is the oldest one of the town. It is built on a flat rock and offers a nice view on Badami.

do.d: With all the cliffs surrounding the town, Badami is a nice spot for climbing, not least since the sandstone is flattering to the hands.

Baijnath.x: Baijnath is a town in Himachal Pradesh, India. Its temple is one of twelve jyortilingas in India, and sees a large number of visitors each year.

see.d: A famous temple where Shiva is worshipped as a lingam of light.

Bakreshwar.x: Bakreshwar is a pilgrimage centre in the central region of West Bengal.

see.d: There is a warm water pool for bathing.

Balasore.x: Balasore or Baleshwar is a city in the North Coast of Odisha. It is full of mixed cultures, and is greatly influenced by Odia, Bengali and Marwari cultures. It's also an industrial hub with some major and numerous small-scale industries.

Ballia.x: Ballia is in Uttar Pradesh province of India. Ballia is an ancient city. Many great saints and sages of India had their ashrams in Ballia, including 'Valmiki', 'Bhrigu', 'Durvasa', 'Parashara muni' and 'Jamadagni.' Ballia was a part of the Kosala Kingdom in ancient times.

do.d: Dadri Mela is the second largest cattle fair of India. The fair starts on the full moon of the month of Kartik (October–November) with a holy dip in the Ganges River.

Bandel.x: Bandel is a former Portuguese colony at the Hooghly River, in the Hooghly district of West Bengal.

see.d: One of the oldest churches in West Bengal, standing as a memorial to the Portuguese settlement in Bengal. It is dedicated to Our Lady of the Rosary.
The birthplace of Bengali novelist Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (1874–1938). He had written several novels and short stories, and most of them were translated into other languages and even…
The temple is known for its architecture and environment, and was built in 2003 on the philosophy of Yogiraj Shyamacharan Lahiri. It is open to all visitors regardless of creed and caste.
A medieval mosque in Saptagram, built in 1529, and it happens to be the only medieval remains of the flourishing port.

Dakshin Dinajpur.x: Dakshin Dinajpur is a district of West Bengal, India. Its history dates back to Pala and Sena times and has a unique cultural heritage.

see.d: Many antique collections including coins, inscriptions, sculptures, terracotta, ornamental stones, etc. of ancient ages are preserved here.
An archaeological site with structures from the Maurya Empire to the Pala Empire.
Kali Puja is being observed here every Friday following the Rash Purnima. A fair is organised for three days.
A brick-built structure built as early as the 14th century. It is a square, roofless mausoleum enclosing the grave of Molla Ataruddin, also known as Shah Ata.
A large number of migratory birds flock to this place during winter.
A small forest with an exquisite picnic spot. There's a small hut with drinking water facilities. Permission is required from Hili Block Development Officer (BDO) to visit the area.

Ballari.x: Ballari, previously Bellary, is a historical city, known for the medieval fort high on a hill overlooking the city. The city of 410,000 (2011) is now a steel hub of South India.

see.d: This is a big fort sitting on a huge monolithic rock mountain at the center of the city. There is only one way upwards mainly consisting of a rocky trail and steps.
This is a 350-year-old temple of the Goddess Durga, which is held in high regard. You can visit it in the mornings or evenings when the aarti (a worshiping ritual) takes place.
It is the quiet heaven in the middle of the bustle hardly known by anyone but the spiritual. This temple was established by the migrant traders in the city about 50 years ago.
This hill has been said to look like the face of a sleeping human.

see.n: Neolethic art on boulders near Sanganakallu
see.d: The exact location is not very clear, but you can ask the locals there to guide you. The said hills are most probably called Hiregudda or Kupgal hill.
This beautiful shrine which has 14 Stations of the Cross separately erected outside and a Bible Museum on the ground floor is an architectural landmark in the City of Ballari.

do.d: Visit the exhibition-cum-tradefair which is setup for around two months in the Municipal high school grounds. It has interesting amusement rides and games for both kids and adults.

Badanaguppe.x: Badanaguppe is a small scenic village in Chamarajangar district of Karnataka state, India.

see.d: Cute little building with green pillars and red roof.

do.d: The road opposite the railway station is suitable for a picnic trip. There are green farms and big trees in this direction.

Bally.x: Bally is a laid-back town north of Howrah city, in the Howrah district of southern West Bengal. It is home to the Belur Math, headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission.

see.d: A riverfront temple complex belonging to the Daw family of Jorasanko. Built by Purna Chandra Daw in 1790, the temple complex consists of a navaratna (nine-pinnacled) temple, six Shiva…
A multi-span extradosed bridge, named after a disciple of Swami Vivekananda. It was built in 2007 to reduce congestion on Vivekananda Setu upstream.
A long rail-cum-road bridge, commonly known as Bally Bridge (বালি ব্রিজ Bāli Brij). It was built in 1932 as Willingdon Bridge, and later renamed after Swami Vivekananda.
The original shrine of Belur Math until the present one is constructed. It has the hallowed memories of Swami Vivekananda and other disciples of Ramakrishna.
A museum.
Contains the remains of the seven disciples of Ramakrishna.

Azimganj.x: Azimganj, a heritage town in Murshidabad, is the district's main railway hub.

see.d: The temple complex houses four temples of "Do chala" or 'Bangla' style of architecture, hence the name "Char Bangla".
Just north of the Char Bangla Complex, the Gangeshwar Temple follows the Jor Bangla style of architecture and also has rich terracotta ornamentation.
This octagonal temple lacks terracotta ornamentation but it is largely compensated by beautiful stucco work, It was built by Tarasundari (daughter of Rani Bhabani) in 1755.
The temple follows the do-chala style architecture. The linga housed inside the temple has five faces and hence the name.

Ausgram.x: Ausgram is a rural area in the Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal, India. It is an off-the-beaten-path destination that provides an essence of the Rarh culture prevalent in the region, with open fields, mud huts, trails of red soil and Baul music.

see.d: Set up in a rustic open setting, the ashram provides a traditional Baul music experience throughout the year.
A forested area with remains of an age-old watchtower. It is said to be a favourite spot for hunting bears (ভালুক bhāluk) of the Rajas of Bardhaman.
A historical park built on a lake by Maharaja Kirtichand at around 1710. It is said that his wife from Rajasthan felt the lack of Rajasthani architecture and culture in Bengal, and the…
An abandoned airfield used by the United States Army Air Forces during the Burma Campaign (1944-1945) of World War II.
A 350-year-old mansion that you can find in some Bengali movies. Now mostly in shambles, the palace was built by Parameshwar Roy, a Dewan of the Bardhaman Raj, for his sons.
An archaeological site. According to legend, the main mound at Pandu Rajar Dhibi is associated with King Pandu mentioned in the epic Mahabharata, hence the name.

Ballavpur.x: Ballavpur is a village near Santiniketan, in the Birbhum district of West Bengal.

see.d: A picturesque river north and west of Santiniketan, which meets the Bakreshwar River in Labhpur. Several tourists gather at the riverside to take pictures and/or videos of the river.
A private community museum, which documents the history of the Santal tribe. Most of the collections were donated by the local residents, and others sourced from the Santal-majority areas…
India's only nature art museum with an impressive indoor display of natural sculptures in driftwood, and dry wood and a sprawling open-air garden of natural rock sculptures.

Baidyabati.x: Baidyabati is a town on the western bank of the Hooghly River, in the Hooghly district of West Bengal.

see.d: Residence of Madhusudan Gupta, the first anatomist of British India. When he became an anatomist, it was considered taboo to dissect a corpse in India.
One of the many canals dug by the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) for irrigation.
A holy ghat along the Hooghly River and a part of the Tarakeswar Yatra (July-August), when pilgrims collect sacred Ganges water from Nimai Tirtha Ghat to offer it to Shiva in Tarakeswar,…

Bamanpukur.x: Bamanpukur is in Nadia, West Bengal.

see.d: A high mound spread over a sprawling area of . The mound is named after King Vallala Sena, of the Sena dynasty, who ruled Bengal in the late 12th century CE.
A tomb of Chand Kazi, a Muslim devotee of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and an example of communal harmony in early modern times. He was entombed in a 500-year-old tree.

Balagarh.x: Balagarh is a town in the Hooghly district of West Bengal.

see.d: Literally the "Auspicious Island".
Literally the "Green Island", it consists of a group of four cottages that belong to the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation (WBTDCL).
A famous Kali temple, surrounded by some smaller temples, with a lake in front of the complex. Built in 1813 by Bireshwar Mustafi, the three-storey temple consists of 25 pinnacles.

Badarpur.x: Badarpur is a town in the Barak Valley region of Assam.

see.d: A historic Mughal-era military fortification located along the south bank of the Barak River.

Bangalore.x: Bangalore, officially called Bengaluru, is the largest city in southern India and the capital of the state of Karnataka. A cosmopolitan city, Bangalore was developed around what was once a mud fort of a feudal lord. The city has a population of nearly 13 million (2025), making it India's fourth-largest city.

do.d: Gopalan Mall, Mysore Road; Gopalan Mall, Near Jayadeva Hospital, Bannerghatta Road ; Gopalan Mal;, Old Madras Road, Near Baiyappanhalli Metro Station
A club membership (around ₹500/year) is typically required for entrance. Foreign film series and cultural events.

Bankura.x: Bankura is the headquarters of its namesake Bankura district of West Bengal. Bankura town is an important stopover for most of the tourist destinations in the district.

see.d: The temple is dedicated to Shiva, also called Ekteswar. It was built by the Rajas of Bishnupur. The temple was built of laterite but had subsequent additions of sandstone and brick.
A large temple ascribed to the Rajas of Bishnupur. It is a remarkably solid and tall temple made of brick.

Bardez.x: Bardez is a municipality of 237,000 people (2011) in North Goa.

see.d: An architectural museum by reputed architect Gerard da Cunha, that "encapsulates for posterity the phenomenal outcome of the amalgamation of eastern and western architectural styles"
It has a gallery on Christian art named the Xavier Xandev Museum art.

Bardhaman.x: Bardhaman or Barddhaman, also known as Burdwan, is the headquarters of the namesake Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal. It is the largest agricultural centre in the state, located in what has been traditionally called the "granary of Bengal". It is a major transport centre with rail and road connections all around.

see.d: Founded in 1994, the Science Centre aims at promoting the amazing facts and mechanisms of science through various models and displays.
Literally "rose garden", Golapbag is a botanical garden built in 1883 by Raja Bijoy Chand Mahtab.
Originally a botanical garden, Ramnabagan became a deer park with spotted deer in 1978. It was declared a wildlife sanctuary by 1981.
Built by Burdwan Development Authority (BDA), the clock tower resembles the Big Ben of London.
Officially known as Bijoy Toran (বিজয় তোরণ Bijaẏ Toraṇ), literally the "victory gate".
A bridge on the Damodar River connecting Bardhaman to Bankura and Arambagh. It was built in 1978.

do.d: One of the most famous natural attractions in the city. It is surrounds by an artificial lake, which was dug way back in 1691 by Raja Krishnaram Ray.
Named after the famous scientist Meghnad Saha, the planetarium came up in 1994 with the major instruments being gifted from Japan. The planetarium has a capacity of 90.
Literally "primary ghat", Sadarghat provides an amazing view of the Damodar River. A lot of people arrive at the sandy area to enjoy picnic.
It was built somewhere between 1890 and 1894. It preserves the legacy of Lala Bansogopal Nandey. It was handed over to the Bardhaman Municipality in 25 May 1984.

Bareilly.x: Bareilly is a city in Uttar Pradesh in India. Home to some 1 million people, Bareilly ranks seventh-largest metropolis in Uttar Pradesh. It is a crowded, hectic city where pedestrians compete with cars and rickshaws on what are quite narrow and congested streets.

see.d: The collection of the museum includes prehistorical stone sculptures, goddess heads of Mauryan era, and a chariot of Gupta period.
The main centre of Naga Sanyasins belonging to the Shiva order of Anand Akhara.
This is the oldest temple in town.
A beautiful Lord Radha Krishna Swaroop temple established in the 1960s with a big AC hall & music fountain, big garden

do.d: A big amusement park including an amphitheater, a 7 Days Restaurant and a water park named Boond.
One of the few well forested areas in Uttar Pradesh, 70 km away from the city centre. The reserve has its own tourist lodges.

Baripada.x: Baripada is a historic town in Mayurbhanj district of Odisha (formerly known as Orissa). This is the district headquarters of Mayurbhanj. It is known for its Jaganath Temple and the palaces of the Bhnaja Deo family.

see.d: The famous Jagannath Temple Rathyatra in Baripada is considered to be second best after that of Puri.
Palaces of the Maharaja of Mayurbhanj District. One of the Palaces has been converted in to a Govt. College.
The Jwalamukhi Temple displaying splendid colourful glass work.
Towering gateway
Opened in 2021 the 54,000-square-foot museum exhibits the restored narrow-gauge steam and diesel engines and old coaches of the Mayurbhanj State Railway.
Remains of an ancient fort, which once served as the capital of the Bhanja dynasty of the Mayurbhanj estate. The ruins consisted of three temples, excavated ruins and fortification walls.

Barnala.x: Barnala is a city in Punjab.

Bathinda.x: Bathinda is a city in Punjab, India known for its ancient fort, its deep ties to Sikh history and its role as a major agricultural and transport hub in southern Punjab.

see.d: Constructed by Raja Dab during the period 90-110 AD.
Grain Market, Bhatinda

Barpali.x: Barpali , or Barapali. This small town have given birth to great Oriya poet Gangadhar Meher. The nearest airport is Bhubaneswar and Raipur of Chhattisgarh.

Bargarh.x: Bargarh is a town and a municipality in Bargarh district in the state of Odisha, India. It is the administrative headquarters of Bargarh District.

Baranti.x: Baranti or Boronti is a small, quiet and scenic place in the Purulia district of West Bengal. There is a 1 km long irrigation project dam, between two small hillocks, Muradi Hill and Baranti Hill. You can get a grand view of Baranti Lake.

Basar.x: Basar (also called Basara) is in northwest Telangana.

see.d: The principal attraction of the town. The temple is one of the few that is dedicated to Saraswati, the Hindu Goddess of education.

Banethi.x: Banethi is a small and remote village hill station in the state of Himachal Pradesh, developed by the British Empire in 1905. at an altitude of 1323 m. The town is 56 km from Kumarhatti and 17 km from Nahan and 79 km from Chandigarh.

Barkur.x: Barkur or Barkoor is a historical place in Udupi district of Karnataka state, India. Most of the ancient structures at Barkur are in ruins.

Barabar and Nagarjuni Hill Caves.x: The Barabar Hill Caves in Magadha region of Bihar state are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India.

Barrackpore.x: Barrackpore or Barrackpur is a cantonment town in North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal. The oldest cantonment of India, Barrackpore was the birthplace of the Indian Rebellion of 1857, and is popular among Kolkata residents for its restaurants serving the Kolkata biryani.

see.d: One of the many museums in India that preserve and display materials associated with Mahatma Gandhi. This one particularly focuses on Bengal and Odisha.
The former riverside suburban residence of the Governor-General of India and later the Viceroy of India. It was built in 1823 by then-Governor-General Lord Hastings.
Wife of viceroy Lord Canning, Charlotte Canning was a painter and a naturalist. She spent her time in Barrackpore indulging in her passions.
Originally a residence of Rastraguru Surendranath Banerjee, who used to live here for a considerable period of time.
A Hindu navaratna (nine-pinnacled) heritage temple with a striking resemblance to the Dakshineswar Kali Temple.
Built in 1831. One of the best in terms of architecture amongst the churches built during the British period.

Bansberia.x: Bansberia is a town and a municipality in the Hooghly district of West Bengal, India.

see.d: The dargah contains the mortal remains of Zafar Khan, a commander of the Delhi Sultan Feroze Shah. He defeated the local Hindu king and established the Turkish rule in Bengal.
A Hindu temple dedicated to Hangseshwari, a form of Goddess Kali and an incarnation of Devi. It was built between 1799 and 1814.
Unlike its neighbour Hangeshwari the Ananta Basudev Temple follows the typical Bengal temple architecture of ek-ratna, single pinnacle. The pinnacle of Anantabasudev Temple is octagonal.
An old holy place for the Hindus. Here the Hooghly River divides into three branches. The branches are Hooghly, Jamuna and Saraswati.

Barak Valley.x: The Barak Valley, a region at the southern fringes of Assam, consists of Cachar, Hailakandi and Sribhumi districts. Culturally close to Sylhet, the valley is home to Bhuban Hills, tea gardens and the former capital of the old Cachari kingdom of Khaspur.

Barakar.x: Barakar is a town in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal along the Barakar River, at the border to Jharkhand. Known for the Begunia complex of Odisha-style temples, Barakar may look like an Odia industrial town at first glance.

see.d: It consists of four 13th-century temples built in the rekha deula style of Odisha. They are dedicated to Ganesha, Kali, Durga and Siddheshvari respectively.

Baneswar.x: Baneswar is a town in Cooch Behar, North Bengal.

see.d: According to a popular belief, the legendary Raja Banasura, an ardent devotee of Shiva had made the latter agree to come down to earth.
A brick-built structure with an unusual octagonal shape and a dome on top of it, the temple is an example of British architectural influence.

Berhampore.x: Berhampore, a colonial-era town on the Hooghly River, is the headquarters of the Murshidabad district of West Bengal.

see.d: The former royal palace of the Cossimbazar royal family, turned into a heritage property.
ThisThe place is known as Boro Rajbari and belongs to the Nandi family. It is totally in ruins, and the interiors are not accessible.
The Old English Cemetery contains several tombs and graves, including the tomb of Mary Hastings, wife of Warren Hastings and that of her infant daughter.
The Dutch Cemetery of Cossimbazar dates back to the early 18th century. The oldest grave is of Daniel Van der Muyl, who died in 1721. The cemetery has 47 tombs, most of them obelisks.
A heritage Christian cemetery protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Many important British residents and military personnel lived in Berhampore were buried in this cemetery.
It was constructed in 1758 by Khoja Petros Arathoon. The church closed down after its last sermon in 1860, but was reopened in 2005.

do.d: A great place to (re)discover love.
Watch theatre.
Watch documentary films.
The central ground of Berhampore, as part of the fortified British cantonment. It is surrounded by various bungalows and barracks, all of which are now used as government offices.

Belgaum.x: Belgaum or Belgaon, officially Belagavi, is a city in Northwestern Karnataka, neighbouring to the state of Goa and Maharashtra, deeply embroiled in claims over this district. The winter capital of Karnataka, Belgaum is a city with a special history; often nicknamed "Kundanagari" which takes the name of a popular sweet made in Belgaum. There is a large minority with links to Goa and Maharashtra.

see.d: A large lake in front of the fort.
A fort on a mountain ridge amidst dense evergreen forest.
Largely identical in design to Bangalore's Vidhana Soudha, the winter session of the Karnataka Legislature is held here.
A splendid Jain temple, built by the Ratta dynasty in c. 1204 under the guidance of a Jain monk.
A ruined Jain temple near Kamal Basadi.

Benaulim.x: Benaulim is a village with 13,000 people (2011) on the beach in Goa. A popular seaside resort in South Goa district, it is renowned for its balmy weather, golden sands, and palm-fringed beaches. It also houses the Don Bosco Animation Centre.

see.d: Ethnographic museum dedicated to rural and agrarian life in Goa.
Houses a large exhibition of historical industrial and household appliances.

Bethuadahari Wildlife Sanctuary.x: Bethuadahari Wildlife Sanctuary is in the Nadia district of West Bengal, India. It is at 24 km (15 mi) from Krishnanagar.

Betla National Park.x: Betla National Park is in Jharkhand, India.

Bettiah.x: Bettiah is a city in Bihar in India.

see.d: The torch of freedom movement started here by Mahatma Gandhi in 1924. The Satyagrah Andolan started from here as well.

do.d: A dense forest and a holiday spot in the periphery. According to mythology it was the residence of Sita, wife of lord Rama, with Luv and Kush, her sons, for years in the Valmiki ashram.

Betul.x: Betul is a city in Madhya Pradesh in India.

see.d: It has the dummy of most popular tourist place of India like Vaishno Devi, artificial lakes. And it has chipkali mandir(Lizard Temple).
Must to see, but be careful while going there with wild animals.
Must to see, but be careful while going there with wild animals.
One can reach here by bus. It is spread over an area of 63 acres. People of every religion can come here. From a spiritual point of view, this ashram helps people a lot.
Historical landmark in Borgaon Or Sergarh, Madhya Pradesh

do.d: There are many temples, Muktagiri one of them. This is a Jain tirtha sthan.

Beypore Beach.x: Beypore or Beypur is a small beach town and port in the state of Kerala, India. It is in Kozhikode District.

see.d: A beautiful beach which holds the main attraction here.
If you love Malabar cost marine life, you should visit here during early mornings. You can see the busy life of fishermen. Also wide variety of fishes.
Beypore Port historically had trade links with Europe, Arabia and other ports on the Indian coast.
An ancient port which have regular services to Lakshadweep islands.
Huge fishing boats and several other types of vessels carrying sand and other material can be seen together here.
15 minutes from the town centre is a place called Dolphin's Point, where one can see dolphins playing in the sea of an early morning.

do.d: The Beypore Pulimoott is a 1-km walkway into the sea. The walk is beautifully tiled and insufficiently lighted. Extremely crowded except in the early morning.
Board your vehicle into the Jankar and cross the Chaliyar river to the village of Chaliyam. You can drive one km into the sea on Chaliyar pulimoott road.

Bhadravathi.x: Bhadravathi is a city in Central Karnataka, India. It is around 25 km from Shivamogga city. It got its name as it is situated on river bank of Bhadra.

see.d: A dam located south of the city.
A very refreshing and spiritual place where Adi guru Shankara Charya enlightened.
Place where the rivers Bhadra and Thunga join.
This temple was built by the Veera Narasimha, the grandson of Vishnuvardhana belonging to Hoysala Dynasty in the 13th century A.D.

Bhagalpur.x: Bhagalpur is a city and a district at the Ganges River, in the Anga region of Mithila, Bihar. Bhagalpur is the distorted form of Bhagdatpuram (meaning city of Good Luck) as it was called during the flourishing of the Anga Kingdom, and has been the seat of power since Bhagalpur also known as Silk City.

see.d: It is an important pilgrimage centre for Jains.
It is an ancient Shiva Temple on the bank of Ganges.
It is an important religious center for Hindus from where holy water of Ganges is carried and offered at Deoghar.
One of the most popular place of Muslims.
It is supposed to have concurrent to Patliputra or Patna. Bhagdattpuram fin the gods to churn the ocean to procure amrit.
Ancient cave sculptures from Emperor Ashoka's reign, from 274 to 232 BC are found in the neighbourhood and at Sultangunj, 20 km west of Bhagalpur,

do.d: The religious festival of "Vish-hari Puja" or "the worship of the Snake Queen" or "Manasa Devi, said to be a daughter of lord Shiva and Queen of Snakes" traces its roots back hundreds of…

Bharatpur.x: Bharatpur is a city in Rajasthan state in India, best known for the Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary, an important way station for many types of migratory birds including the rare Siberian Crane. This is a city with great history ruled by jats and has a distinct place in jat history. The town has its share of fort, temple, mosque and several gateways.

see.d: Built in by Jat ruler Maharaja Suraj Mal in the 18th century. It's one of the few forts in India not conquered by the British, despite them laying siege to it for six weeks in 1805.
It was built by Raja Jawahar Singh in 1765 to commemorate his victory over the Mughals at the Battle of Delhi (1764)
It is also known as Ghana, is a world famous sanctuary developed by Maharaja of Bharatpur. It is also one of the few Natural UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India.
Built by Maharaja Balwant Singh in 1845.
The main mosque of Bharatpur. Built by Hindu Jat rulers. Sandstone structure.
400 years old temple.

Bhavnagar.x: Bhavnagar is a city in the Saurashtran peninsula of Gujarat, India, known as an industrial hub excelling in salt and jewellery production, and is associated with Mahatma Gandhi, who went to university here. It is located off the coast of the Gulf of Cambay in the Arabian Sea. It was the seat of the Babnagar Burn Kingdom of the Rajput Dynasty, which is said to have begun in the late 13th century.

see.d: It is a modern construction, but don't miss visiting it.
White marble temple built on hill, gives Aerial View of City. Crafting work on marble stone is pretty good.

do.d: One of the multiplex in Bhavnagar.
Spiritual Study Centre where more than 500 true seeker are doing their sadhana.
The people of Bhavnagar are some of the friendliest in India. Mixing with them will be a memorable experience. Look for people playing Cross and Circle game in public places.

Bhedaghat.x: Bhedaghat is a city in the Narmada Valley of Madhya Pradesh, India.

see.d: Situated atop a hillock and approached by a long flight of steps, the Chusat Yogini Temple commands a singularly beautiful view of the Narmada flowing through the jagged Marble Rocks.
The Narmada, making its way through the Marble Rocks, narrows down and then plunges in a waterfall known as Dhuandhar or the "Smoke Cascade".
The perpendicular magnesium limestone rocks fringe the crystal clear placid waters of the Narmada providing a fascinating site. Boating facilities are available between November-May.
The soapstone revealed by the Narmada provides occupation to families of carvers of gods and goddesses, lingas, crosses, madonnas, ashtrays and trinket boxes.

Bhilai.x: Bhilai is a major city in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh. It is also referred as Steel City because of steel plant by Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL).

Bhatpara.x: Bhatpara is a heritage town in North 24 Parganas.

see.d: It consists of two nine-pinnacled temples and two five-pinnacled temples.

Begusarai.x: Begusarai is a city of 250,000 people (2011) in the Mithila region of Bihar.

see.d: Contains rare and endangered migratory birds and has a large oxbow lake.

Bhandarej.x: Bhandarej also known as Bhandrey is in the Dausa District of Rajasthan. Located in this small village are many remnants of monuments and temples. It also a gateway to several wildlife sanctuaries.

see.d: (1732 AD) Hindu-style five-storey stepwell is believed to connect to the Palace by a secret tunnel.
Built in the 11th century. This palace was converted to a hotel, it retains its splendour and is an important site to visit.

Bekal.x: Bekal is a small town, known for the nearby seaside Bekal Fort, in Kasaragod District, Northern Kerala, India.

see.d: Sprawling fortress offering sweeping sea views, preserved battlement walls, gates & tunnels.
There are three beautiful temples in this area.
A family entertainment park complete with amusement park, food court, DJ stage, gaming zone, etc. It also provides space for cultural events and destination weddings.

Bhilwara.x: Bhilwara is a city of 510,000 people (2022) in Rajasthan in India.

do.d: The park is home to a variety of local wildlife. The sunsets here in the natural surroundings are pretty.

Bharuch.x: Bharuch, formerly Broach, is a city in South Gujarat.

Bhimbetka.x: Bhimbetka is a UNESCO World Heritage site in Madhya Pradesh, India.

Bhimtal.x: Bhimtal is a small town in the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, India. Its main attraction is Bhimtal Lake, surrounded by wooded hills. The town is also a useful base for visiting Sattal, Naukuchiatal and other places in the Kumaon region.

see.d: The main attraction of Bhimtal. The lake is surrounded by wooded hills and has boating facilities.
A Shiva temple on the eastern side of Bhimtal Lake. The present temple is associated with the 17th century. Local traditions connect the shrine with Bhima and the Pandavas.
The dam at the southern end of Bhimtal Lake.

Bhojpur.x: Bhojpur is a city in Madhya Pradesh in India. It is a destination of historical importance.

see.d: King Bhoj founded Bhojpur in the early medieval period, between 1010 and 1053 AD, and the temple has played a significant role in establishing Bhojpur's reputation across India.

Bhongir.x: Bhongir or Bhuvanagiri is a town 47 km from Hyderabad in the Telangana state of India. Its biggest attraction is Bhongir Fort standing atop of monolithic hill.

see.d: A fort on a huge, isolated, monolithic rock at a commanding height of 610 metres above sea level.

Bhopal.x: Bhopal is the capital of Madhya Pradesh, India. Despite earning the sobriquet the "Chernobyl of India" for its industrial disaster in 1984, Bhopal is an important city of Central India.

see.d: One of the largest mosques in the country.
A very beautiful place with an ancient Shwetambar Jain temple on the hill. You can see a beautiful view of Bhopal from this Takeri.
Bharat Bhavan is a world-famous art complex and museum.
Regional Museum of Natural History, Bhopal is a branch of the National Museum of Natural History, New Delhi, it is the center of an informal environment education, whose main purpose is to…
Another impressive museum, the Museum of Man created by the government of Madhya Pradesh, showcases how the people of the state live in their natural form, what they cultivate, the kind of…
A museum of tribal culture. The exhibits depict the ways of living of various tribes across India.

Bhubaneswar.x: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, lies on the banks of the River Kuakhai which is part of the Mahanadi River delta. Together with Konark and Puri, it forms the Swarna Tribhuja or Golden Triangle of Odisha tourism. This city makes an ideal starting point for the traveller who wishes to explore the magnificence of Kalinga architecture, worship at its grand temples or enjoy the beaches of Puri.

see.d: The 10th or 11th-century temple of Bhubaneswar has been described as "the truest fusion of dream and reality".
Built in 996 CE, the Muktesvara Temple marks an important transition point between the early and the later phases of the Kalinga architecture.
Dating to 650 AD this is the oldest surviving temple in Bhubaneswar, and possibly Odisha.
This temple got its name from a red-gold sandstone used, which is called Rajarani locally. It is an abandoned temple and has no presiding deity.
This 13th-century temple is on the eastern side of Bindu Saravar. It is dedicated to Lord Krishna. Krishna along with Balaram and Subhadra are worshipped out here.
Bhaskareswar Temple is located east of the Rajarani Temple and lies on the opposite side of the road and is surrounded by open space.

do.d: The planetarium is named after the famous Odia astrologer Samanta Chandra Sekhar Mahapatra, who was popularly known as Pathani Samanta.

Bhuj.x: Bhuj is a city in the Kutch district of the Gujarat state of India.

see.d: The literal translation of Aaina Mahal is an apt one. A beautiful palace now renovated after the massive earthquake in 2001.
A fort made by ancient rulers to protect the city. Now it is open for common public to see. A sure shot favorite if photography is your interest.
The cenotaphs of rulers is a picturesque place. Featured in Bollywood movies, the place and garden around it makes a nice time.
A 450-year-old artificial lake built during the reign of the Jadeja Dynasty, the lake is quite a site to sit and chill out while roaming around it.
The palace of rulers of Kutch region. Maharao Pragmalji initiated the creation of this palace. This Gothic styled structure is a must visit. Opens at 10AM.
The museum is located on the scenic bank of lake Hamirsar and has the largest collection of inscriptions from the period of Western Satrap rule during the early centuries CE.

do.d: The three-day Rann Utsav is held every year during the full moon night in the month of December at Bhuj and goes around the district with a grand finale.

Bidar.x: Bidar is a city in the Indian state of Karnataka, west of Hyderabad. Once a citadel of Badri Shahi and Bahmani empire Bidar still houses the remains of a gigantic fort along with a couple of tomb complexes.

see.d: Built in 1427 when Sultan Alla-Ud Din Bahman of the Bahmanid Dynasty shifted his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar. There are over 30 monuments inside fort.
An ancient madrasa (Islamic college) built by the Bahamani empire around 1460 AD. It bears testimony to the scholarly genius of Mahmud Gawan, who first came to Delhi as a Persian trader…
It is believed that Lord Sri Rama, on the way to Ayodhya from Lanka after defeating Ravana, visited this place and that resulted in the temple which would wash off his act of killing Ravana…
The temple virtually runs into a cave waterbody and is one of the unique in the world. The water in the cave will guide the pilgrims to the idol.
This is a Sikh historical shrine. One of the most popular south Indian historical gurudwaras amongst the Sikh community all over India.
Situated 53 km away from the city of Bidar, Manik Prabhu Temple is a unique architectural beauty and a major spiritual and religious centre.

Bihar.x: Bihar is a state in the plains of India. The state is bounded by Uttar Pradesh to its west, West Bengal to its east, Jharkhand to its south and Nepal to its north. Bihar is one of India's poorest states, with stark social inequality.

Biharinath.x: Biharinath in the Bankura district of West Bengal is the second highest hill in South Bengal. It is 451 m (1,480 ft) high. The tourist spot is at the foot of the hill, near Biharinath temple.

see.d: You can climb, take along a local guide (tip him) in order that you are not lost.
This is most famous Shiva temple in the western part of Bengal and for some ways beyond the state. Millions of pilgrims throng there throughout the year.
You can walk down through the country paths towards the river

Bihar Sharif.x: Bihar Sharif is a town of 300,000 people (2011) in Bihar, India. It is east of the Paimar River, a tributary of the Ganges (Ganga) River. The old centre of town has examples of medieval Islamic architecture, such as the Bukhari Mosque.

see.d: Celebrated widely.
Named after a Muslim saint of 14th century.
Sacred place for the Jain community. Famous for beautiful temples of God Mahavir.
A beautiful ancient tomb constructed on top of the rocky hill. Nearby are the ruins, which are believed to be ruins of Jarasandh Jail.
The scene around the temple is very calm and beautiful.

Bikaner.x: Bikaner is a city in north-west Rajasthan, India.

see.d: A jewel in the Thar Desert, the palace is built on the embankment of a lake. Built by H.H. Maharaja Sir Ganga Singhji of Bikaner, this Grand Heritage property is spread over 6000 acres.
An ornate two-storied Jain temple with vibrantly adorned paintings with gold leaf patterns. Marble pillars bearing floral arabesques, multi colored walls and floors appeal to the senses.
The fort was built by Raja Rai Singh, the sixth ruler of Bikaner who reigned from 1571 to 1612. It is a fort of the Bikaner royal family.
Located at Deshnok, 32 kilometres from Bikaner. This is a temple of a local deity, "Karni Mata". It is believed that the "Karni Mata" used to take care of the Rajputana family.
The Laxmi Niwas Palace is a former residential palace of the king of the former Bikaner state, Maharajah Ganga Singh in Bikaner in the Indian state of Rajasthan.
Lalgarh is another fort of the Rajputana family. Some of the Rajputana kings used to stay here. You will see the royal story of the Rajputana family.

Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh).x: Bilaspur is the second-largest city in Chhattisgarh, India after the capital, Raipur.

Bina.x: Bina is an emerging city in Central Madhya Pradesh, India.

Bir.x: Bir is a town in the eastern end of the Kangra Valley in Himachal Pradesh with a friendly, relaxed Indian population and a large Tibetan (Khampa) community. It is home to several educational institutions, monasteries, and nonprofit organizations (NGOs). It is becoming a popular off-the-beaten-path destination for meditation courses, volunteering, and ecotourism.

see.d: An eco-campus for compassionate living, set on a hill with breathtaking views overlooking Bir and the Kangra Valley, offering programs in sustainable living and contemplative practice, and…
A Karma Kagyü Tibetan Buddhist Monastery located in woodlands between Bir and Baijnath, headed by the 12th Tai Situ Rinpoche and also host of frequent visits from Mingyur Rinpoche.

do.d: Fun Museum with 1hr of Mind bending fun with illusions. Interactive & immersive experience. Optical and sensory illusions and augmented reality.

Birbhum.x: Birbhum, the "Land of Red Soil", is known for its rich culture, vibrant religion and picturesque nature.

Kolkata/East.x: East Kolkata comprises the new areas on the eastern side of the metropolis that have been growing since the 1990s. It houses the IT hub of Kolkata, shopping emporia, amusement parks and splurge hotels. Eco Park and Science City are major attractions.

see.d: Despite being a major landfill site where the solid waste are dumped, more than 40% of the green vegetables in the city's markets come from here, being a prominent example of peri-urban…
A luxury residential building, consisting of two tower blocks and a structure called "Deya" connecting the two.
An industrial complex and the centre of leather-tanning business of the metropolis, fondly known as chormonogorī (চর্মনগরী, literally "Skin City").
An arch monument in New Town and one of the most iconic structures in Kolkata. The structure consists of a single ring supported by two parabolic arches from four sides of the Narkelbagan…
A pedestrian zone, stretched from Infinity Benchmark to RDB Boulevard. Opened in September 2023 with a vibe of New York's famous intersection, this cyberpunky area has become a hangout spot…
An exhibition containing models depicting the daily life of rural Bengal.

do.d: Four screens for films.
Hosts the annual West Bengal State Handicrafts Fair.
Site of the annual Kolkata Book Fair that takes place from the last week of January to the first week of February. It is the largest book fair in Asia and is a significant event in the city.
A permanent trade fair complex. Fairs of different kinds are held at regular intervals.
Hosts Durga Puja and trade fairs.

Bijapur.x: There is more than one place called Bijapur:

Bhimavaram.x: Bhimavaram is a small colourful city in central Andhra Pradesh, with a population of about 1.5 lakh or 150 thousand.

Bhiwani.x: Bhiwani is a city of almost 200,000 people (2011) in the Northern Indian state of Haryana.

see.d: A small zoo with around 10 types of animals, including hippos, gharials, and peafowl. Takes 30 minutes to one hour to see them all.
The architectural showpiece of the town, shaped as a hexagonal pyramid with large white stars adorning the sides.

Bogmalo.x: Bogmalo is a small beach-side village in South Goa. Despite its small size, Bogmalo has a range of accommodation and places to eat. It is situated in a small bay, with around a mile of curving sandy beach, which is generally very quiet.

see.d: a military aviation museum focused on the history of the Indian Naval Air Arm. Displays the history of Indian's Naval Airforce right from the Independence.

Bokaro Steel City.x: Bokaro Steel City is a city in Jharkhand and one of the most important industrial cities in the Eastern Region. Population of the urban area is more than 1,000,000 with area above than 200 km2. The city is very well planned and systematic, with wide 4- to 6-lane roads across the city, a good sewage system, 24-hour electricity supply and the greenest environment in the region.

see.d: It is an important social, cultural and religious meeting place for people from the south.
A village in Chas Block famous for 75 foot (23 m) high tower.
Has a collection of over 40,000 books (including some valuable manuscript) that meets the reading requirements of the people in the township.
One of the largest steel mills in the country, with an output capacity of more than five million tonnes of salable steel.
This is the home of the oldest thermal power plant in Asia, started in 1952 in collaboration with USA and West Germany by the then Prime Minister of the country Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.
A town famous for Chandrapura Thermal Power Station, a unit of Damodar Valley Corporation.

Bundi.x: Bundi, in eastern Rajasthan, rates highly in terms of attractions; the city is famous for the Taragarh fort which towers over the city, and its more than 50 sunken step-wells used to draw clean water before the modern water mains were installed.

see.n: Rani Ki Ji Baori (Queen's Step Well)
see.d: The most famous step well in Bundi, it was built in 1699 by the spurned queen. It is 46 metres deep and includes 200 steps.
The largest in Bundi. Though slightly overgrown, it is well worth a visit for the spectacular carvings on the numerous steps leading down to the water level.
Constructed between 1871 and 1875, these are 2 step wells that have been extensively refurbished.
Built in the 16th century, this is one of the most famous forts in Rajasthan due to its intricate structures and a highly-regarded painting gallery.

see.n: Garh (Bundi) Palace and Chitrashala - Ummed Mahal
see.d: These adjacent structures are must-sees and include some of the most amazing paintings in India.
A smaller palace built on a dam wall; Rudyard Kipling stayed here.

do.d: A 307 km² park. Animals that live in the park include leopard, sambhar, wild boar, chinkara, sloth bear, Indian wolf, hyena, jackal, and Fox.

Canacona.x: Canacona is a city in the South Goa district in the extreme south of Goa. It includes touristy beaches such as Palolem, Patnem and Agonda.

Cauvery Basin.x: Cauvery Basin is a region in the south of Karnataka State.

Thrissur.x: Thrissur (originally Thirusivaperoor, formerly Trichur) is a popular city and district in the central part of Kerala in Southern India. It is known as the cultural capital of Kerala, with numerous cultural institutions, art centers, museums, etc.

see.d: Established in 1976 at Ayyanthole where Sri. Ramavarma Appanthampuran who lived the Kumarapuram Palace. This is also a cultural museum.
It has the best collection of wood carvings, metal sculptures and ancient jewelers of the Cochin dynasty.

see.n: Basilica of Our Lady of Dolours
see.d: The Roman Catholic Minor Basilica built in 1875 is locally called Puthen Palli. The long steeple is visible from anywhere in the town. The chapel has 15 altars.
Named as Vadakkekara Palace, was reconstructed in Kerala-Dutch style in 1795 by Sri.
It is a major attraction for children and students with a variety of animals. There is a special building which houses snakes.
This hillock has been converted by the tourism department as an amusement park. While grown ups relish the scenic splendor from the hill top. Children can relax and play to their hearts.

Bordi.x: Bordi is in North Konkan in Maharashtra.

Bongaigaon.x: Bongaigaon is an important town (pop: 93,650) in the eastern part of Assam, India. The largest clan of Rashbongshi people in Bongaigaon district is Halua across all Rashbongshi dominated villages.

see.d: It is in the middle of the city. From the highest point of the hill you can see a beautiful view of the whole city. There is also a nice Shiv temple on the highest point.
It is a famous temple for religious in Western Assam.
It is 15 km away from Bongaigaon city towards the east, covering an area around 20 km².
It is a popular tourist attraction near Abhayapuri about 15 km from Bongaigaon. It attracts thousands of local and foreign tourists every season.

do.d: Vast wildlife sanctuary, home to protected species such as Bengal tigers, elephants & rhinos.
The best-preserved relics of the architecture of the Buddhist period.
The best-preserved relics of the architecture of the Salasthambha period are the remains of the five rock-cut caves at Jogighopa on the bank of the Brahmaputra in the district of…

Burhanpur.x: Burhanpur is a city in Madhya Pradesh, India. It is located on the eastern bank of Tapti river and is the capital of Burhanpur district. A city with not many tourists, Burhanpur is a city rich in history.

see.d: The only railway station in Burhanpur. Trains arrive and leave the station regularly.
Syedi Abdul Qadir Hakimuddin (1665-1730 AD) is the holy dawoodi bohra saint who is buried in Burhanpur, India. His grave is visited by pilgrims from all over the world.

Bramhapuri.x: Brahmapuri is in Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.

Brahmavar.x: Brahmavar is in Udupi district. It lies to the immediate north of the city of Udupi.

see.d: Barkur is a historic cluster of 3 villages where you can find the ruins of many forts, among them Simhasanagudde, Vijayanagara fort, and Nandana fort.
An estuary around 20 km away from Udupi town, you can see the sea on one side of the road and the river on the other.

Byndoor.x: Byndoor is the northernmost taluka of Udupi district, spanning from the coast to the foothills of the western ghats. The Kollur Mookambika temple is located around 28 km from the town of Byndoor.

see.d: Reached only by trekking to the deep jungle. The name "Arishna" refers to the orange-yellow colour created by sunrays falling on the water droplets around the waterfall.
1 km from the Mookambika temple. Popular with trekkers and river lovers.
Adi Sri Shakthi Mookambika Temple sits atop this mountain and is believed to be the real abode of Devi from where Adi Shankara re-established it at foothills at Kollur.
Famous for Vidyadana, temple trust running several schools, & sponsoring midday meal program for surrounding schools. Devi Mookambika is famous for Vidya (education).
Kundapur-Kollur- Shimoga road. A World Wildlife Fund project, and a home for an endangered species, the lion-tailed monkey.
Devotees take a holy dip here at a spot one km from the Mookambika temple. There are rocks in the river and very good photographic opportunities.

do.d: The Annual Festival is held in March or April for nine days. Daily worship and special processions are held. At noon, Shatha Rudrabhishekha will be performed.

Bundelkhand.x: Bundelkhand is a geographical and cultural region of India, divided between the states of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. See: Northern Bundelkhand — the north-western part of the region in Uttar Pradesh Eastern Madhya Pradesh — covers the south-eastern part of the region in Madhya Pradesh Northern Madhya Pradesh is sometimes considered part of Bundelkhand as well.

Bolpur.x: Bolpur is a major commercial centre in the Birbhum district of West Bengal, on the north bank of the Ajay River. Although the city is best known for the nearby Santiniketan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Bolpur has managed to develop its own charm.

see.d: An old and popular Kali temple.
The museum showcases some aspects of the life of Rabindranath Tagore, other than railways.
The old zamindar palace that belonged to Bhuban Mohan Sinha, who gave his of land to Debendranath Tagore, the founder of present-day Santiniketan.

do.d: Hosts some Santiniketan events.
A beautiful park with an elevated view of the Sahibganj Loop.

Buxa Tiger Reserve.x: Buxa Tiger Reserve, also known as Buxa National Park, is a forested area in the Dooars of West Bengal. It is a habitat for tigers, Asian elephants and other mammals plus a variety of birds, amphibians and reptiles.

see.d: A fort at an altitude of on the Sinchula Range guarding the most important of the eleven routes into Bhutan.
A beautiful picnic spot at the Jayanti River that provides an excellent view of the hills of Bhutan.
This is a museum inside Buxa tiger reserve.

Chaibasa.x: Chaibasa is a small but important town in West Singhbhum, Jharkhand. The town is peaceful and known for its natural beauty — green all around, especially during monsoon.

see.d: A highly popular natural spring approximately 2 km from Chaibasa. This unique site is known for water owing directly from tree roots, creating a distinctive waterfall effect.
A scenic cascade found in Indikuri Dalki.

Budge Budge.x: Budge Budge is a town in the South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, along the Hooghly River.

see.d: One of the relics of the now-abandoned Chinese settlement of Achipur, the first recorded Chinatown in India. Many Chinese Kolkatans still flock to the temple around the Chinese New Year.
The grave of the first recorded Chinese settler in India, also known as Yang Tai Chow.
A memorial dedicated to the people who were killed in the Japanese steamship Komagata Maru in 1914.
The precursor to the new Budge Budge railway station, now partly in shambles. However, it is famous for its association with Swami Vivekananda.

Braj.x: Braj is a region of India between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers, in southwestern Uttar Pradesh.

Chakdaha.x: Chakdaha, a town in the Nadia district of West Bengal, is the birthplace of woman cricketer Jhulan Goswami, popularly known as the "Chakdaha Express".

see.d: Simurali was originally developed as a feeder port to Kolkata in the British period. However, the port was later abandoned as the Hooghly River later changed its course.
A 17th-century terracotta temple, and one of the earliest and rarest surviving examples of the classic char-chala (four-sloped roofs meeting at a pinnacle) style of Bengal temple…

Chandannagar.x: Chandannagar, formerly Chandernagore, is a small city in the Hooghly district of West Bengal, India. Situated along the banks of the river Hooghly, the city has been able to maintain a separate identity different from all other cities and abide by her own characteristics. The "City of Liberty" has always attracted people from all over the world due to her indescribable beauty.

see.d: The French Cemetery contains 150 tombs and is located on the Grand Trunk Road opposite Lal Dighi (a large lake).
Built by Sri Harihar Seth, and donated to the people of Chandannagar. This building still serves as a theatre hall and a library. It was first of its kind in the entire locality.
One of the original two gates that were constructed on 14 July 1937 as the gateways to the French colony of Chandernagore.
A meditation centre.
Locally known as Joṛā Ghāṭ (জোড়া ঘাট, literally "twin ghats"), this memorial is dedicated to Dourgachorone Roquitte (দুর্গাচরণ রক্ষিত Durgācaraṇ Rakṣit), the first Indian to receive the…
One of the oldest and finest museums in the entire region. It boasts a beautiful collection of French antiques which are difficult to find anywhere else in the world, including the cannons…

do.d: Operated by the municipal corporation.
Operated by the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA).
A popular picnic spot among locals, with a name ostensibly similar to Bengal's most popular beach destination. So, don't get confused while driving to your destination!

Chandigarh.x: Chandigarh is India's first planned city, quite distinct from the rest of the country and considerably better organised. It is the capital of both Haryana and Punjab states, but the city is not part of either state, being a union territory, i.e. administered directly by the central government.

see.d: Most of the capitol complex is fenced off due to tight security, the open hand is accessible and from there you can see the main buildings, albeit from a distance.
This provides an interesting aspect on how Chandigarh was founded. It begins with the principles on which Chandigarh was built, selection of the Architects, the design for the people etc.
Elante Mall at Chandigarh is among the largest malls in North India, covering 20 acres. It is a mixed use development project which includes entertainment, hotels and business.
