The letter is fine for looking around the High Court; just show it to security at the entrance, around the back, but if you want to take photos you need to surrender your camera, and head…
The Japanese Garden is a park in Sector 31 in union territory of Chandigarh. Built in 2014 in 13 acres of Land, by Indian Government, it was inaugurated by Shivraj Patil on 7th November…
This is the Assembly for both Punjab and Haryana. It's easy to run out of time, so make sure you have a whole clear weekday to appreciate all the capitol buildings.

do.d: This stadium, capacity 40,000, was completed in 2021. It hosts the Punjab cricket team and is expected to become the home of Punjab Kings in the IPL.

Chandrapur.x: Chandrapur, also known as Chanda, is a city in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra in India. The city gets its name from the Chanda Fort present here. The city is also known as City of Black Gold due to the large number of coal mines present around the city.

see.d: A newly developed place for all ages, especially for kids.
Goddess Kali attracts devotees from different parts of State.
This is the place where Baba Amte made a home for the patients of leprosy.
A rapidly developing municipal town situated on the Chandrapur-Chennai railway route.
Located in Chandrapur district in the Vidharba region of Maharashtra covering an area of 104.38-sq-km.
A flourishing ancient village in Waroda Tehsil, which is today better known to the general public as a place of Jain religious importance for majestic temple of Parsvanatha than for its…

Chathannoor.x: Chathannoor is a city in Southern Travancore in India.

see.d: A small place, home of the famous Vilappuram Devi Temple (Anandavilasam Bhagavathi Temple).
A favourite haunt of migratory birds. Now it is a developing zone in tourist concept. Now there is a bridge over polachira which connects road named Polachira Bund Across Road.
If you interested you can visit the famous temples of Chathannoor, Bhoothanatha Kshethram,Kanjiram vila bhgavathi kshethram, Chennamath Kshethram, Vilappuram bhagavathy kshethram, paniyil…
The Mosque is an important place to visit. Hundreds of people will be coming here for the Friday Juma.

do.d: Go to and see the beautiful views of the nature then you can go to Anathavalam to see elephants. Do not forget to stay some time at Mannathipara here to have a better look of Polachira.
This is lord Ayyappa Temple.
This is a temple of lord Ayyappa..Hundreds of people come every Saturday for Shani pooja (Saturn prayers).
Sree Bhoothanatha Temple, Kanjiramvila Bhagavathi Temple, Chennamath Shiva Temple, Vilappuram Bhagavathy Temple, Vayalunada Bhagavathi Temple etc are famous temples in this town.
Christhos Marthoma Church ,Malankara Catholic Church etc are famous churches in this town.

Chavakkad.x: Chavakkad is a municipality in Thrissur District of Kerala state in India. Chavakkad is noted for its beach and fishing. It lies on National Highway 17 is about 75 km (47 mi) north of the city of Kochi, the commercial capital of Kerala and 25 km (16 mi) west of Thrissur, the cultural capital of Kerala.

see.d: Located on the coast of Arabian Sea in West Coast, Chavakkad Beach is counted amongst Kerala's most popular beaches. It is two kilometres from the Chavakkad town.
Located at Thottappu 6 km from Chavakkad Town. Breathtaking view of Kerala and Arabian Sea. There are 140 steps in the lighthouse. You can see the western ghats from here on clear day.
A major shrine in India.
Located at Palayur, the church was established in 52 AD by St Thomas, one of the twelve close disciples of Jesus Christ.

Chennai.x: Chennai, formerly Madras, is the largest coastal city in southern India and the capital of the state of Tamil Nadu. It is on the east coast of peninsular India. Though Chennai traces its history to Fort St George and the adjoining village of Madrasapattinam founded by the British East India Company in 1640, some residential districts of the city are older.

Chennithala.x: Chennithala is a small village in Mavelikkara Taluk, Alappuzha district, Central Travancore in Kerala state, India.

Cherthala.x: Cherthala is a small town in Kerala.

see.d: It is the miraculous statue of the Passion of Our Lord that attracts thousands to Thankey every year in a pilgrimage marked by repentance and an earnestness to start a new life.

Chhapra.x: Chhapra is a city in Bihar in India.

do.d: A water-based amusement park.

Chhattisgarh.x: Chhattisgarh, the land of thirty-six forts, is a state in Central India.

Chidambaram.x: Chidambaram is a city in the southern state of Tamil Nadu in India with a population of about 62,000 (2011). Of the numerous temples the Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram is one of the most significant ones. In terms of its antiquity, richness in terms of worship & festival traditions, in architectural & sculptural splendour, in its association with music & dance, Chidambaram is a center second to none in representing the rich cultural heritage of India.

see.d: The temple complex is spread over an area of 40 acres (160,000 m²) in the heart of the city.
A village that is 31 km (19 mi) from Chidambaram known for Arulmigu Amirthakateshwarar Thirukkoil, constructed during the reign of Cholas by Kulothunga Chola.
Due to its strategic location on the Coromandel Coast, Parangipettai has long been a major trading centre.
The Pichavaram Mangrove Forest is the world's second largest mangrove forest.
Sacred to Hindus and Buddhists, it is one of the eight Svayam Vyakta Ksetras of Vaishnavas. The village is known for the Bhu Varaha Swamy temple.
Swetharanyeswarar (Shiva) Temple is a Hindu temple in Thiruvenkadu.

do.d: India's largest standup paddling program. Learn kayaking, outdoor science and various outdoor skills. The camp is on the bank of river Kollidam backwaters. Accommodation available.

Chikhaldara.x: Chikhaldara is a lovely hill station in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra,India. This place is the only hill station in the region and hence also known as 'Kashmir of Vidharbha'.

see.d: Located in Chikhaldara and Dharni talukas of on the Satpuda hill range. It spreads over an area of 1676.93 sq km. It is one of the last remaining habitats of Indian tiger in Maharashtra.

Rohilkhand.x: Rohilkhand is a region in Uttar Pradesh, India.

Chamarajnagar.x: Chamarajnagar is in Karnataka. It is about 195 km from Bangalore.

see.d: Large pond and a big prayer flag can be noticed from a distance.
Good selfie opportunities

Chinnadagudihundi.x: Chinnada-gudi-Hundi or C.H.Gudi is a small village near Nanjangud in Mysore district of Karnataka state, India.

Chengalpattu.x: Chengalpattu (formerly Chingleput), a town on the Palar River in Tamil Nadu, has developed as a tourist spot for many foreign travellers on their way to Mamallapuram, Thirukazhukundram, Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary and Kanchipuram, Karikili Bird Sanctuary.

see.d: A Ramsar site and a bird sanctuary. This region is surrounded by open areas, paddy fields and scrub forest.
The lake hosts migratory birds such as the whiskered tern, Indian spot-billed ducks, moorhens, coots, and small waders.
The temple consists of two structures, one at the foot hill and the other on the hill's crest. The large hilltop temple houses the deity Shiva, also known as Vedagiriswarar.
A Ramsar site and the oldest water bird sanctuary in India. It was a favourite hunting spot of the local landlords in the early 18th century.

Ramanagara.x: Ramanagara is a town near Bangalore, in a valley surrounded by rocky hillocks. It has an average elevation of 747 metres (2450 feet). The present town has an Agrahara on the left bank of the Arkavati with a temple of Arkeshwara built in later Vijayanagara style.

see.d: A folk museum with an exclusive display of the folk arts of rural Karnataka, The museum has a collection of 5,000 folk artefacts. The museum complex has various shopping outlets inside.
A bird sanctuary atop a hill. It is India's only vulture sanctuary with three vulture species: long-billed, Egyptian and white-backed vultures.

Chandrakona Road.x: Chandrakona Road is a town in Paschim Medinipur, West Bengal. It is named after the road to Chandrakona town that starts from here.

see.d: A natural river canyon that has different spectacular types of formation due to soil erosion. Better known as the "Grand Canyon of West Bengal", Gangani is a very popular picnic spot.
An integrated film city with replicas of various monuments.

Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus.x: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Marathi: छत्रपती शिवाजी महाराज टर्मिनस Chhatrapatī Shivājī Mahārāj Ṭarminas, IR code: CSMT (mainline) or ST (suburban)), formerly Victoria Terminus (VT), is one of the main disembarking stations for suburban and long-distance trains in Mumbai, India, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

see.d: A memorial dedicated to the victims of the 26/11 attacks in 2008 who were killed at CST.

Chandaneswar.x: Chandaneswar is a popular pilgrimage site in northeastern Odisha, near the border to West Bengal. It is often called the "Second Puri" due to the popular Shiva temple.

see.d: A popular Shiva temple, built in the typical Kalinga architecture style. A huge annual fair on the Pana Sankranti (Odia New Year) is celebrated on the premises.

Chitradurga.x: Chitradurga is a town in Southeastern Karnataka in India.

see.d: While driving from Bangalore to Chitradurga, it is kind of on the way. This is a very old dam, built in 1907. The view is incredible from here. You are allowed to walk on the dam.

Chitrakoot.x: Chitrakoot is a culturally and archaeologically significant town in Baghelkhand, split between Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. Though relatively unknown to tourists, the area is a pilgrimage destination known for a number of important temples and sites mentioned in Hindu scriptures. It is well worth visiting if you have the time.

see.d: Ramghat is the main feature of Chitrakoot and resembles a minature Varanasi with river boats and pilgrims. It is located on the banks of the quiet river Mandakini.
Gupt Godavari is a natural wonder consisting of two caves. There is a pond known as 'Sitakund' in one of these caves which is perpetually fed by a small stream of water.
Hanuman Dhara is a spring located on a steep hillside in Chitrakoot. On foot one has to climb a steep flight of 650 steps to reach this place.
Janaki Kund is situated 2 km south of Chitrakoot in Satna District, on the banks of the Mandakini River. Literally ‘Janaki Kund’ means the ‘Pool of Sita’.
Some people said that during exile of lord Ram. Rama prayed to Kamtanath (Deity of local villagers) to fight with devils.
Some people believed that during exile younger brother of Ram stayed on the Lakshaman Hill. Lakshman hill is situated on half way of Parikrama path of Kamdgiri.

Chittoor.x: Chittoor is a city in Andhra Pradesh, India. It is the headquarters of Chittoor district Chittoor, very close to the revered temple of lord Balaji or Venkateswara at Tirupati, is also close to two eminent wildlife sanctuaries and the famous Horsley Hills, a famous hill resort named after W.D Horsley. Situated in the valley of the Ponni river, Chittoor is a market for grain, sugarcane, and peanuts.

Chittorgarh.x: Chittorgarh, also spelled Chittaurgarh, is in the southern part of Rajasthan, lies on the Berach River, a tributary of the Banas, and is the administrative headquarters of Chittorgharh District. It is 112 km from Udaipur and 182 km from Ajmer. The city served as a capital to the Sisodia clans of Rajputs of Mewar for a long time.

see.d: Kirti Stambha ("Fame Tower") is a 22 m (72 ft) high tower built on a 9.1 m (30 ft) base with 4.6 ft (1.4 m) at the top, is adorned with Jain sculptures on the outside and is older (probably…
Built by Maharana Kumbha in 1449, this lord Vishnu Temple has beautiful idols in its sanctum, mendap and pillars. In the same premises, there is a small temple of Lord Krishna.
This palace, a white building, a three storied structure (a 19th century reconstruction of the original), is located in the southern part of the fort.
At the entrance gate near the Vijaya Stamba, Rana Kumbha's palace (in ruins), the oldest monument, is located. The palace included elephant and horse stables and a temple to Lord Shiva.
The tower is called the symbol of Chittor and a particularly bold expression of triumph, was erected by Rana Khumba between 1458 and 1468 to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Shah I…
Built by Maharana Fateh Singh, this huge palace is of modern style. This place has been named Fateh Prakesh after Maharana Fateh Singh.

Chunar.x: Chunar is a town in Purvanchal region of Uttar Pradesh in India. Located on the Banks of the Ganges it houses a mighty fort with over 2000 years of history. The town also has several temples, tombs and darghas.

see.d: Established by Maharaja Vikrmaditya the King of Ujjain to commemorate the stay of his brother Raja Bhartihari who had taken his Samadhi when he was alive and still that Samadhi Sthal is…
Iftikhar Khan was an official in the court of Jahangir. The tomb dates back to 1605.
Kasim Shah Sulemani was a Sufi saint from Peshawar who visited the Purvanchal region during the reign of Jahangir.
The cemetery is located on the banks of the Ganges and falls on the left side of the road leading to Chunar Fort. There are several graves of British and European origin.

Churu.x: Churu is a town in the desert region of Rajasthan, India.

Coimbatore.x: Coimbatore, also known as Kovai, is an industrial city of 2 million people (2020) in Tamil Nadu, often likened to being the Manchester or Detroit of Southern India. It's famous for the manufacture of motor-pump sets and varied engineering goods.

see.d: The park includes a zoo and a children's park. Evening is the best time to visit the park.
Interesting collection of inventions by G.D. Naidu, who is also referred to as the Edison of India.
The museum was founded by GD Gopal in 2015 as a commemoration of his late father, Gopalswamy Doraiswamy Naidu.
Interesting science experiments. There are the History of Industrialisation in Coimbatore exhibition and an old motor bike which G.D.Naidu learned to assemble from a British officer after…
The museum aims to stimulate curiosity, develop an inquiring mind and enable children & adults to learn science in an informal and fun-filled manner.
Natural history museum with exhibits and artifacts related to forests and their wildlife. It is housed in a heritage building, which is more than 100 years old.

do.d: This yoga centre is an ashram in the foothills of the Velliangiri Mountains beside the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Visitors can participate in yoga programmes and ceremonies in the temples.
A place for food and recreation. Ideal for morning and evening walk. There are various installations, which include the Eiffel Tower, Leaning Tower of Pisa, Red Fort and many more.

Colva.x: Colva is a town in South Goa, 8 km away from Margao. It is popular for its beach.

Cooch Behar.x: Cooch Behar, a small city in northern West Bengal in India, is known for its rich cultural heritage and the remnants of its royal heritage. Being one of the main tourist destinations of West Bengal, housing the Cooch Behar Palace and Madan Mohan Temple, it has been declared a heritage town.

see.d: The main attraction of Cooch Behar and the "Buckingham of West Bengal". The palace shows the acceptance of European idealism of the Koch kings and the fact that they had embraced European…
A minuscule version of the National Rail Museum in New Delhi. The museum is based on the theme "Role of Railways in Development of Dooars region".
Large rectangular pond surrounded by government offices and seasonally populated by migratory birds. The walkway around it is favourable for morning and evening walks.
The graveyard of the Cooch Bihar Northern Evangelical Lutheran Church (NELC), initially set up for European residents and Christian missionaries of the area during British India.
A park full of Sal trees. Great place for walking and relaxing. Has a view of the airport and a railway line.
Cooch Behar's only church and convent, with a school for the blind.

do.d: Good place for movies in a busy street. Mostly Bengali movies are aired.
One of the best places to watch movies in the town. Refreshment facilities are available too. English and Hindi movies are mostly aired here.
Great place to watch movies with friends and family. Mostly Bengali and occasionally Hindi movies are aired.
A multiplex in the town airing Hindi and Bengali movies. Refreshment facilities are also available.
A great park to go to with family and kids. It has a child-playing area and features a toy train. It has lush green gardens and also has some animals in an enclosure.

Coonoor.x: Coonoor is a famous hill station that is 17 km from Ooty in Tamil Nadu, India. It is probably the second most popular hill station in the Nilgiris. The hill station stands at a height of 1,839 metres and is known for its great picnic spots and picturesque surroundings.

see.d: This is an important place to visit. It not only provides a panoramic view of the vast expanse of the Nilgiri hills but also of the famous Catherine Falls.
Lamb's Rock commands a grand view of the Coimbatore Plains and is a favorite place for tourists.
Beautiful picnic spot. The height of the falls is about 180 feet. There are vast stretches of undisturbed sholas and it is a paradise for naturalists.
The park is in a deep ravine on the Northern side of Coonoor Railway Station at an elevation of 1768 to 1798 m. The park can be divided into eight major sections.
It is called the Sunset point of Coonoor. It's highly recommended to walk the trail up to the desired point. There are beautiful vistas of nature everywhere, overlooking Nilgiri Hills.

Courtallam.x: Kuttralam is a city in Tamil Nadu, India. Courtallam is the anglicized version of Kuttralam.

see.d: After the main falls, this is the most famous waterfalls and definitely the most enjoyable of all. It is located 6km from the main falls.
This waterfall is located close to the bus stand, and greets you as you enter Kuttralam. It is usually crowded during the season, and you can take bath here 24 hours a day.
This is not a historic place, but there is a waterfall here too! This waterfall is maintained by the PWD by controlling the waterflow.
Another wonderful spot little away from Kuttralam is the Karayar dam. Believe it you have a wonderful waterfall inside the dam which takes about 15 minutes of boat ride from the shore.
This beautiful falls is located upstream and as part of the cascade that forms the Main falls. You can reach shenbagadevi only by trekking for about 30 minutes.
Sittraruvi or "Small Falls" is an offshoot of the Main falls located to its side. It is very small and completely safe to enjoy a shower here.

Cuddalore.x: Cuddalore is a town at the central coast of Tamil Nadu. Cuddalore is a beautiful town located along the Bay of Bengal which is home to the famous Silver Beach.

see.d: The collection represents the history, culture, flora and fauna of the district. Natural History specimens include South Indian timbers, fibres, swans, bears, lizards and snakes.
A ruined British fort.
A Shiva temple of Pallava and Chola periods.
2nd largest beach in Asia.

Cuttack.x: Cuttack, officially Kataka, is the second-largest city of Odisha after Bhubaneswar. The state's former capital is steeped in old traditions, with a perfect combination of traditional and modern lifestyles. Its silver filigree works have led the city to earn the nickname "Silver City".

see.d: A 13th-century fort built by the Eastern Ganga emperor Anangabhimadeva III (1211-1238).
A law museum hosted in a colonial-era bungalow, which was once the residence of the Chief Justice of the Orissa High Court.
Janakinath Bhavan, the birthplace of Indian independence activist Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose is converted into a museum and is named the Netaji Birth Place Museum.
The museum came up in 2013 and is housed in the former complex of the River Boat Construction and Repair Workshop.
An ancient temple dedicated to the Goddess Chandi, the presiding deity of Cuttack. It is famous for the annual Durga Puja and Kali Puja festivals.

do.d: A multipurpose stadium used for cricket, football and hockey. It is a regular venue for international cricket and is the home ground of Odisha cricket team.

Dabhoi.x: Dabhoi is a city and a municipality in Vadodara district in the state of Gujarat, India

Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.x: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu is a small union territory in Western India.

Chulanur Peafowl Sanctuary.x: The Chulanur Peafowl Sanctuary is in Palakkad district of Central Kerala in India.

Chinsurah.x: Chinsurah is the headquarters of the Hooghly district of West Bengal, India. Lying on the Hooghly River close to Chandannagar, 35 km (22 mi) north of Kolkata, Chinsurah has a strong significance in the history of Bengal.

see.n: Armenian Church of St. John the Baptist
see.d: Founded in 1695 the Armenian church in Chinsurah is the second oldest Christian Church in West Bengal (the oldest is in Bandel).
One of the residences of Bengali novelist Bankim Chandra Chatterjee. He lived in this house during 1877–1881.
A clock tower built in 1914 to commemorate the life of the British King Edward VII. He was the eldest son of Queen Victoria.
The district court of Hooghly. The courthouse was originally a British military barracks built after the demolition of Fort Gustavus in 1829, which became the seat of the district court…
One of the few extant non-British colonial legacies in Chinsurah. It is one of the oldest Christian cemeteries of India dating from 1743 to the end of the 19th century.
The monument is a blend of neoclassical and baroque architectures. It is dedicated to Susanna Anna Maria (died 1809).

do.d: A riverside platform with benches where you can relax and watch the flow of the wide Hooghly River. Many people engage in an āḍḍā at the ghat.

Contai.x: Contai is a town in the Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal.

see.d: It is fairly long beach, starting around 2-3 km from the resort. What is shown on the map is roughly the centre of the beach. This is a good sandy beach.
It is fully operational. Visitors can climb to the top and have a good view of the area
A rekha-deul temple. It was believed that Bhimsen Mahapatra, King of Odisha, built this temple.
If you go there having the sea in your mind then you will be quite disappointed. The water has shifted far off from there and the only thing left is white muddy sand.
Made famous by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's classic novel Kapalkundala. (1866). It is a story of a forest-dwelling girl named Kapalkundala, who fell in love with and married a young man from…

Chittaranjan.x: Chittaranjan is a railway town in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal, near the border to North Jharkhand. It is named after Indian freedom fighter Chittaranjan Das.

see.d: One of the largest locomotive manufacturers in India.

Dadra.x: Dadra is an enclave within Gujarat in Western India. It is a part of the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

see.d: Has boating facilities.

Daltonganj.x: Daltonganj is a city in Jharkhand. The city was named Daltonganj during the British Raj after Irishman Colonel Edward Tuite Dalton.

Daman (India).x: Daman is a city and an enclave within Gujarat, on the west coast of India. It was under the control of Portugal from 1539 to 1961, and as a result of this, Portuguese influence is still palpable today, particularly in the architectural and cultural spheres. It may not have all the facilities that a tourist destination should have but it does have peace, relaxation, friendly locals and beautiful places to see.

see.d: Moti Daman fort was built by the Portuguese between 1559 and 1593 on the site of former Islamic citadel. It has an area of 30,000 sq metres and still has cannons on its walls.

see.n: The Chapel of our Lady of Rosary
see.d: Built in 17th century, having simple exterior but stunning interiors. It has fine woodwork with golden cherubs and petals.
This church has decorated ceilings and carved gateways. Established in 1559 and consecrated in 1603.
Ruins of the 16th century massive church.
It is a small fort with high stone walls completed in 1627. It has two gateways with two huge human figures that face towards the Daman Ganga River. It covers an area of 12,250 m².
This 18th-century Jain temple is in the northern region of Nani Daman Fort and is dedicated to Mahavir Swami. It is built with white marble.

do.d: Gaming lounge and cafe with international attractions like laser paintball, Sumo wrestling, professional shooting and archery range.

Damoh.x: Damoh is a city in Madhya Pradesh in India.

Darbhanga.x: Darbhanga is a city in the northern part of Bihar, India. A part of Gangetic plains of the north India, Darbhanga is located just around 50km from Nepal. The city is known for its association with Darbhanga Royal family - one of the richest landowners of the country during British Raj.

do.d: The orchard of the old Darbhanga dynasty, located in Chatariya village about a kilometer away from Kadirabad at the banks of Adhwara river.
It is famous historical temple dedicate to gautam rishi's wife ahilya. This temple is situated about 3 km.
Rajnagar is the very important historical place of Madhubani District. But it is erasing its beauty in lack care.

Darjeeling.x: Darjeeling is a hill station in the northern region of West Bengal. It used to be a lovely Victorian town built among the Himalayan foothills, the remnants of which are still visible around the Chowrasta. The main attractions are the cultural diversity of the Tibetan and Nepali populations.

see.d: Quite a hike from the centre, Darjeeling's second oldest tea estate is open for visitors.
The oldest site of Darjeeling. This hill is also known as the “Makal-Babu-Ko-Thaan” in the local area. It is said that a Red Hat Buddhist Monastery stood at this very spot.
A rehabilitation centre for the Tibetan refugees in Darjeeling, established on 2 October 1959, following the Dalai Lama's escape from Tibet. It contains a monastery and a museum.
Ideal to visit early morning when the first rays of the sun kiss the Kangchenjunga mountain and give it a golden colour. To visit the hill, one needs to get up at 3AM.
The greenhouse has quite a nice collection of flowers.
It has a good collection of the more charismatic animals found in the Himalayan region, including leopards, a rare Bengal tiger, and red pandas.

do.d: Less visited but offers unique and charming views of Kangchenjunga. Few locals can be found jogging here and offering prayers to various deities.
A long ropeway (aerial lift) consisting of 16 cars and plies between the North Point and Singla, on the banks of the Ramman River.

Datia.x: Datia is a small town in Madhya Pradesh in India. 69 km from Gwalior, on the Delhi-Chennai main line, Datia is a town whose antiquity can be traced back to the Mahabharata. A town of great historic significance.

see.d: Peetambra Peeth" is located near the city. Peetambra Peeth is the famous "Sakti-Peeth" of the country. Sh.
Palace built entirely of stone and brick by Raja Bir Singh Deo in 1614 considered to be one of the finest examples of Bundela architecture in the country.
Imposing temple.
There are 77 beautiful Jain temples with sky high spires. Temple 57 on a hill is the main temple. This is vast in size, very beautiful, having attractive artistic spire.
There are 26 temples in the village, most of them are very ancient. At Kund-Kund Nagar, on a 25 feet high platform, a colossus of Lord Bahubali, in standing posture, 18 feet high has been…

Davanagere.x: Davanagere is a city in Central Karnataka. Davanagere is known for its business. Crop business is a most common source of income here.

Dehradun.x: Dehradun is the winter capital of the Indian state of Uttarakhand. Nestled between the Himalayan foothills to the north and the Shivaliks to the south, the town offers breathtaking scenery. It is a favourite destination among tourists, pilgrims and enthusiasts alike from different regions with its serene environment.

see.d: The Indian Military Academy. A charming little museum housing collections of 20th century military artifacts.
Built by the British, this remains the icon of the downtown area.
Majhon- Paunda, Via Nanda Ki Chowki, Premnagar, Dehradun
The only war memorial of its kind in the world which was erected by the British to honour their foe, the Gurkhas (or the Gorkhas).
Small town in the Dehradun District with ancient monuments such as the Edicts_of_Ashoka.
Lavish environs and one of the largest institutes of its kind. Guided tours available. Admission free. Museum entry ₹25, covers 6 halls.

Delhi.x: Delhi, the largest city in northern India, is the country's thriving melting pot. Home to New Delhi, the country's capital, Delhi is at the centre of India's arts, commerce, education, tourism and transit. As the capital of several empires over the last 2000 years, the city contains a striking array of well-preserved historic sites for tourists to visit.

Deoghar.x: Deoghar, also called Baidyanath Dham, is a Hindu pilgrimage town in Jharkhand. It is famous for the Baidyanath (Shiva) temple.

see.d: According to Hindu mythology, Ravana went to Mount Kailash and prayed to Lord Shiva, who gave him a Jyotirlinga to take to his land, with the promise not to place the lingam anywhere else.
The Universal Temple of Sri Ramakrishna held in the bosom of the Vidyapith campus is a place of attraction to the religious minded.
Source of the Mayurakshi River. Vehicles come to the base but one has to walk up. A ropeway has been built to ferry people to the top.

do.d: Rikhia peeth is the tapobhumi (place of spiritual sadhana or practice) of Swami Satyananda Saraswati, founder of the Bihar School of Yoga, Munger.

Dewas.x: Dewas is a town in the Malwa region of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh in India. Dewas is 35 km from Indore on National Highway 3.

see.d: The Tekri can be climbed by two ways one through steps and another through slope. We took the slope way which was more lengthy but easier to climb.In the south of the tekri is the temple of…
Lake.

Dhanbad.x: Dhanbad is a city in Jharkhand; it is considered the coal capital of India. The coalfields around Dhanbad are known as the Jharia coalfields. They cover an area of around 448 km2, the total reserve of coal is estimated at 5,000 million tonnes.

see.n: Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research
see.d: CIMFR, Dhanbad is one of the national laboratories of Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, Government of India.
An institute of national importance. It was established in 1926, and has one of the most beautiful engineering campuses in the country.
The village, which is about 10 km from Tundi on the Dhanbad-Govindpur -Giridih Road, is noted for its hot spring.
The village is in Govindpur development block, contains two ancient pillars which are locally associated with Emperor Asoka and the Afghan Chief Sher Shah.
The village lies in Nirsa-cum-Chirkunda development block. It contains an ancient pillar said to date back to the time of Emperor Asoka.
The village is in Baghmara development block. It is said that an ancient temple of Lord Shiva was found when the mines here were being worked.

Dharmapuri (Tamil Nadu).x: Dharmapuri is a city in Tamil Nadu.

see.d: 2 km from Dharmapuri.
7 km from Dharmapuri
It was built in 9th century. 2 km from old bus stand
Near the four roads.

see.n: Malligarjuneshwaraswamy (Lord Shiva) Temple and Perumal Temple
see.d: This may be the only place where Perumal is in sitting position with thaayar. This is 108th in 108 Vaishnava Divya Desams.
Ancient Siva temple in Teerthamalai

Dharmanagar.x: Dharmanagar is the second most populous city in Tripura.

see.d: A small sanctuary reflecting the natural vegetation of the region. You will be able to spot several species of birds and primates.
Historic site containing large and mysterious yet fascinating rock-cut and stone sculptures of Hindu deity Shiva.

Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.x: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, also known as the DHR or the Toy Train, is a 2 ft (610 mm) gauge railway that runs between New Jalpaiguri and Darjeeling in the Indian state of West Bengal. Built between 1879 and 1881, it is about 88 km (55 mi) long. It climbs from about 100 m (328 ft) above sea level at New Jalpaiguri to about 2,200 m (7,218 ft) at Darjeeling, using six zig-zags and five loops to gain altitude.

Deulti.x: Deulti is a popular picnic spot in the Howrah district of West Bengal, along the Rupnarayan River. It was also the residence of Bengali writer Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay for 12 years.

see.d: A 370-year old Hindu temple, locally known as Gopāler Mondir (the temple of Gopala, another name of Lord Krishna).
The house of Bengali novelist Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay for twelve years. The house was constructed in 1923 by a local worker named Gopal Das.

Daulatabad.x: Daulatabad, also known as Devagiri, is a town in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, close to Aurangabad.

see.d: Inspired by Delhi's Qutb Minar, the Chand Minar is considered to be among the finest specimens of the Islamic architecture in India.
It houses a stupendous 12th-century fortress well placed atop a charming hill. This invincible fortress boasts of a sturdy wall and an intricate series of ramparts.

Dharashiv.x: Dharashiv, formerly Osmanabad, is a town in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, known for the Dharashiv Caves.

see.d: A nexus of seven Shramanic caves on the Balaghat range. It is believed to be built around 5th-7th century, and there has been debates over whether those caves are Buddhist or Jain…

Deoband.x: Deoband in northern India is famous for the Deobandi movement, an Islamic revivalist movement.

Dhenkanal.x: Dhenkanal is a town in the central region of Odisha (formerly Orissa).

do.d: Elephants, leopards, deer and hyenas are some of the animals that reside in these deciduous forests. Boating activities available.

Dholpur.x: Dholpur or Dhaulpur is a town in northeastern Rajasthan, south of Agra.

see.d: Home to various endangered species like the gharial, Gangetic dolphin, red-crowned roof turtle and various species of birds.

Dibrugarh.x: Dibrugarh is a city in Upper Assam and the main urban centre within the tea growing areas of North-Eastern India. Dibrugarh is also known as the Tea City of India.

see.d: See the majesticity of Nature's gift to this land, the mighty Brahmaputra.
A park for recreation with views of the Brahmaputra River.
A newly developed park for recreation, one of the best in the North East.
A temple, built of marble stones, near Assam Medical College campus.

do.d: Refresh you health in the morning and the evening by jogging at the jogging track around the Chowkidinghee Field.

Digha.x: Digha is one of the most popular seaside destinations in West Bengal. Once a small fishing hamlet, Digha has emerged as a weekend getaway with numerous hotels and eateries. People from Kolkata and sourrounding cities flock around the beaches during the holiday.

see.d: One of the most popular beaches in West Bengal, and the best place for a safe dip. The beach here is flat and it gets overcrowded, especially during the cooler winter break.
The original beach, popular among older generations. However, Old Digha is not safe and conducive for bathing. It is not as wide as it used to be due to heavy soil erosion.
A less-visited beach at the estuary of the Champa River. There's a fish market at the beach.
There is a river by the beach. It gets submerged with high tide. The river gets dried up twice a day. Again it gets filled with water once there is high tide.
The newly-built temple in New Digha, built in 2022-2025 to rival the Jagannath Dham in Puri.
The Digha counterpart of Puri's Gundicha Temple, used in Digha Ratha Yatra (Chariot Festival).

do.d: A park developed in 2015 with the iconic "Biswa Bangla" (World Bengal) globe. The globe depicted the location of West Bengal in the world with the Bengali letter "ব" (from "বঙ্গ" or…
A large seaside space with activities like boating and bungee jumping.
A pond with toy train (miniature railway) rides.

Dimapur.x: Dimapur is the largest city of Nagaland, India.

see.d: The largest church in Asia.

Dindigul.x: Dindigul is a city of 290,000 people (2011) and the headquarters of the Dindigul district of Southwestern Tamil Nadu.

see.d: This 280-foot-tall fort was constructed in 1605 by Madurai King Muthi Krishna Naicker and Thirumalai Naicker.
This is an economical Hill resort and a picnic spot for weary travellers. This is on the way to Natham 25 km from Dindigul city. This place is accessible from Madurai also.
Established in 1956, Gandhigram Rural Institute was founded by two Gandhians; Dr.T.S.Soundaram and Dr.G.Ramachandran. They followed the Mahatma Gandhi’s ‘Nai Talim’ system of education.
It is 5 km from Dindigul on the way to Karur. The main deity is Lord Alagar and the main festival is during the Tamil month of Chitrai.(April–May)
This is a famous mosque in Begambur and is around 200-300 years old.
This is an ancient temple believed to be 200 years old and the idol is believed to have been installed by the King Tipu Sultan.

Doab.x: The Doab is the region in India between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers extending from the Sivalik Hills to the two rivers' confluence at Prayagraj.

Dona Paula.x: Dona Paula is a city in India, where two of Goa's famous rivers meet the Arabian Sea. Named after Dona Paula de Menezes, it's also called the Lovers' Paradise. Dona Paula Beach is 7 km from Panaji.

see.d: It is dedicated to the three Magi (the wise men of the East)—Gaspar, Melchior, and Balthazar who, according to a legend, were guided by a star to Bethlehem to greet the newborn Jesus.
Set up in the 1960s, the National Oceanography Institute delves not only upon marine biology, but incorporates almost all the major branches of coastal and marine oceanography.
The Cabo Raj Niwas (the Governor’s House) is half a kilometer away from the National Oceanography Institute. It houses the tomb of Dona Paula de Menzes in the Cabo Chapel.
The Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary is situated on the western tip of the island of Choro, along the Mandovi River, about 9 km from Dona Paula Beach.

Guwahati.x: Guwahati, the largest city in the northeast Indian state of Assam, is the nerve centre of both the Assamese culture as well as the broader Northeast Indian culture. Once known as Gauhati in colonial times, the city hosts the state capital Dispur, and is one of the fastest-growing cities outside mainland India, with a population of over 2.4 million in 2020.

see.d: Atop the Neelachal hill, the highest spot in the city draws pilgrims from all over India, especially during the Ambubachi festival.
A river port on the south bank of Brahmaputra in West Guwahati was the entrepot to Guwahati before the construction of the Saraighat bridge in the early 1960s.
Guwahati War Cemetery is one of the largest Second World War cemeteries in India. It is maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC).
One of the 51 Shakti Pithas.
A Krishna temple. It is known for its Holi celebrations in the month of February–March.
A small town, known for its silk production and the "Manchester of Assam".

do.d: A great place to visit for science geeks and also for lovers of entertainment.
The aerial lift across both banks of the Brahmaputra in Guwahati. The southern terminal (Kachari Ghat) is near Nehru Park, whereas the north terminal (Rajadwar) is behind Doul Govinda…
The annual festival caters to more than tea lovers. In addition to tea tasting and tours of the tea gardens, visitors can enjoy jungle safaris and river rafting.
A set of three Assamese festivals in April, October and January respectively, all of which celebrate the changing seasons.
A three-day festival where offerings are made to the goddess of snakes, Devi Manassa.

Kalyan-Dombivli.x: Kalyan-Dombivli is a suburb east of Thane, in the North Konkan region of Maharashtra. It is the result of an amalgamation of the two towns: Kalyan and Dombivli. Kalyan has a historical importance with the foot-touch of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and many more leaders, while Dombivli is the home to most of the employees of Mumbai.

see.d: A fort Which was built by Shivaji Maharaj near Ganesh Ghat at Kalyan, on the Ulhas river bank.
A famous & hostorical lake.
Caves as old as the ones at Ajanta and Ellora, on a hill near Lonad village. The Sun Temple is in the village.

Dr. Ambedkar Nagar.x: Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (Mhow) is a town in Western Madhya Pradesh.

see.d: The waterfall that comes in the movie Maine Pyar Kiya at the end.

Dharwad.x: Dharwad or Dharwar city is in the northern part of Karnataka state, in South India. It's known for its numerous world class universities and colleges.

see.d: Fortress ruin built in 1403.

Dinhata.x: Dinhata, a town in North Bengal, is famous for the historical Gosanimari, which was the capital of Kamata and Khen dynasties.

see.d: A holy Hindu temple dedicated to the gods Krishna and Balaram.
There have been various opinions about who built the temple because both the Khen and the Koch dynasties were worshippers of the goddess Kamteswari.
Ruins of the palace of Khen rulers dated to the 14th-15th century CE. Excavations have surfaced many artefacts.

do.d: A great place to watch movies. Mostly Hindi and Bengali movies are aired. Online booking is not available so you need to book the tickets when you visit the theatre.
A nice open ground surrounded by long trees. It also has a temple.
Great place for morning walk. It has a boating dock with a descent sized pond. It also has a coffee stall.
A great park near the famous Balaram temple.
A park for children in commemoration of Kamal Guha.

Dooars.x: The Dooars region covers the foothills of the Himalayas in North Bengal and Assam, and an eastern extension of Nepal's Tarai region. It is home to animal species like the famous one-horned rhino and numerous other species of animals and birds. The region has an undulating span of tea gardens and rice plantation.

Dhuri.x: Dhuri is a small city of Sangrur in the state of Punjab, India, It has got the status of Tehsil. the language here is Punjabi. It is a part of the historical Malwa region of Punjab.

Doddaballapura.x: Doddaballapura is a town north of Bangalore in Southeastern Karnataka.

see.d: The uniqueness of this temple is that the prime deity Lord Kartikeya (Murugan), is found together with Lord Narasimha.

Dhubri.x: Dhubri is a commercial centre in Lower Assam.

see.d: The palace was built by Raja Prabhat Chandra Barua of the Gauripur royal family on a small hill-top at Matiabagh, Gauripur on the banks of the Gadadhar river.
Built between 1493 and 1519 after the Bengal conquest of Kamata, the mosque is considered to be the oldest in Assam, and an example of the late medieval Bengali architecture.

see.n: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib

Digboi.x: Digboi, a town in Upper Assam, is where Asia's first oil well was drilled.

see.d: A museum established by the Indian Oil Corporation to commemorate the history the oil industies in the Assam Valley. This museum was opened behind the oil refinery in early 2002.

Diphu.x: Diphu is a tribal town on the hills of of Assam.

see.d: It hosts animals like the Asian elephant, the Hoolock gibbon, the Bengal tiger and the Himalayan black bear.

Dholka.x: Dholka is a historic city and municipality in Central Gujarat, India. Located 50 km southwest of Ahmedabad, Dholka offers a quiet escape into medieval Indo-Islamic architecture, Solanki-era stepped tanks, and rich mythological lore.

see.d: A 15th-century mosque with adorned walls and pillars
Built in 1453 on an immense scale near a large lake, this rare brick-and-limestone mosque features massive domes, grand arches, and ornate carved jalis (stone screens).
A 14th-century stone mosque which is an example of early Indo-Islamic architecture. It features stone as well as wooden colonnades. Permission required to enter.
Locally significant tomb complex.
A large octagonal lake next to the Alif Khan Mosque. Picturesque views. Check its sluice gates which bring in the waters.
Constructed in the late 11th century by Queen Minaldevi (mother of Jayasimha Siddharaja), this historic stepped tank remains a central landmark.

do.d: A large annual fair. Held around November, for five days ending on the full moon day of Kartik month in Hindu calendar.

Dudhsagar Falls.x: Dudhsagar Falls is a waterfall in the southern part of Goa at Mollem, near the border with Karnataka state. It is one of the highest waterfalls in India, and among the hundred highest waterfalls in the world.

Dudhwa National Park.x: Dudhwa National Park, in Lakhimpur-Kheri District of Uttar Pradesh, adjacent to Nepal border, is one of the major projects for wildlife preservation in India. Spread over an expanse of approximately 811 km² of marshes, grasslands and dense forests, it is a home for over 38 species of mammals, 16 species of reptiles and numerous species of birds. It has two core areas: Dudhwa National Park and Kishanpur wildlife sanctuary.

Durg.x: Durg is a major city in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh.

see.d: Balod houses Prachin Kila or oldest Palace, Mandir and Sati Chabutra.
Famous for its ancient Shiv Mandir.
Its major attraction is a Dam which is 1,128 m long and is located on the Kharkhara River.
It features landscaped garden which is a joint initiative of Indian and Russian government and a Zoo. The highlights of Zoo are exotic animal and avian species, lake, toy trains and others.
It is a site to visit exquisite Jain temples and Pasharwanath Tirth.
The prime attraction of this place is a Dam on Tandula River. It is an exciting picnic spot also.

Durgapur.x: Durgapur is an industrial city in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal, India. Being an industrial hub, there is little here of interest to tourists.

see.d: Made famous in the novel Devi Chaudhurani by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. An unbelievable network of tunnels starting near the City Centre region right up to the Damodar river.
A Kali temple established in 1852. People from different places arrive at the temple during Kali Puja.
Definitely one of the best places to see, if you are interested in one of two things: nature and man's effort to control its fury.
The steel plant is one awesome thing to see. It is hard to imagine the scale of things that happen and how the heck all of this works together.
According to the Archaeological Survey of India, this temple is more than 800 years old, with a unique architectural style. It is built in the style of Rathas of Southern India.

do.d: It is a fraction of its former colonial self. Yet, with swimming pools and the who’s who of the Durgapur Steel Plant, complete with its British era high-nosedness, is still a hotspot.
This was one of the most beautiful parks around, being the first park in the entire Paschim Bardhaman district to have a musical fountain.
It is a fun place for kids near City Centre. It has a toy-train, a few rides and a bunch of other attractions. Adjacent to it is a deer park.

Dwarka.x: Dwarka is a city and a municipality in Gujarat, India. Dwarkadish temple is one of the finest in India, and it dominates the city's small skyline. Sunset point near the Gomti river and its ghats are exceptionally beautiful at all times of day, though perhaps a little risky late at night.

see.d: The over 2000-year-old, 5-storied Hindu temple is the main sight of the holy town. The temple is dedicated to the god Krishna, who is also believed to have been King of Dwarka for 100 years.
This is supposed to be the place where Krishna lived, met his friend Sudama and blessed him, and there is a Peetha (Seat) where Krishna is said to have met Sudama.
This temple is 8 km from Dwarka. This is in the outskirts of the city and this is a lonely temple and there is an interesting story of Rukmini being cursed by sage Durvasa because of which…
Shivrajpur Beach is another notable beach located near Dwarka. It has been awarded the prestigious Blue Flag beach certification for its cleanliness and eco-friendly initiatives.

Edathua.x: Edathua is a place in Kuttanad which a low lying wetland located in the Alappuzha district, Kerala, India. It is situated 14 km from Tiruvilla town.

see.d: Celebrates its feast during the month of May is an important location for Christian pilgrims.

Edava.x: Edava is in the state of Kerala in southern India.

Eluru.x: Eluru is a small colourful city in central Andhra Pradesh.

see.d: 74 feet statue of Abhaya Buddha in a pond.
Recreational park with walking track.
A bird sanctuary based on one of the largest freshwater lakes in India

Erode.x: Erode is a city in Tamil Nadu in South India, likely to be called by various names such as Textile City, Turmeric City or Loom City of India.

see.d: Bannari Amman Temple is 75 km away from Erode and 10 km distance from Sathyamangalam.It is the famous temple in Erode District and situated at the bottom of the Western Ghats and on the way…
Sangameshwarar Temple, Bhavani is about 12 km. from Erode. The famous Sangameshwara Temple is on the shores of the Bhavani river.
Bhavanisagar Dam is about 16 km from Sathyamangalam across the river Bhavani.
Birds Sanctuary, Vellode - is about 15 km from Erode
Chennimalai - is about 30 km. from Erode and 12 km from Perundurai
Government Museum, was opened to the public in 1987. The important exhibits are inscription of Kongu Chola, hero stones from Bargur, Tanjore paintings, manuscripts, coins, geological…

Etawah.x: Etawah is a city in western Uttar Pradesh, famous for its lion safari, as well as the Chambal River valley that houses various endangered species.

see.d: One of the main attraction of the city, with a breeding centre for the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo leo).
Home to various endangered species like the gharial, Gangetic dolphin, red-crowned roof turtle and various species of birds.

Faridabad.x: Faridabad is a satellite city of Delhi, in the state of Haryana. Urban sprawl from Delhi has made Faridabad the most populous city in Haryana.

see.d: A very peaceful place.
A must see, with -high Shivaling.
A beautiful park which hosts one of the largest Indian flags.
A palace built in the 18th and 19th centuries. Now partially converted to a motel and restaurant.
At , this is supposed to be one of the biggest statues of Lord Hanuman in India. There is a temple adjacent to the statue.

Gandhidham.x: Gandidham is a port city in the Kutch district of Gujarat.

see.d: The only second place where last remains of Mahatma Gandhi is kept and over that a memorial is built.
At nearby town named Anjar, you can visit this legendary temple famous amongst locals.
One can take permit from Port officials to visit one of the biggest port of India.

Gandhinagar.x: Gandhinagar is the capital city of the Indian state of Gujarat and the twin city of Ahmedabad. Often hailed as the greenest capital in India, it is fast emerging as a desirable destination for real estate for the Gujaratis, with neighbouring Ahmedabad spilling over. It is in a green farm belt, and houses major Gujarat Government organisations and administrative buildings, along with famous educational institutes like Pandit Deendayal Petroleum University (PDPU), Gujarat National Law University (GNLU), National Institute of Design, National Institute of Fashion Technology and the Dhirubhai Ambani Institute of Information and Communication Technology.

see.d: One of the biggest religious attractions in Central Gujarat, this temple has pink stones with beautiful carvings and is surrounded by beautiful gardens and awesome fountains.
A magnificent domed building.
An attraction for children and tourists, the Children's Park in Sector 28 has a mini train and a lake with boating facilities.
Near Sarita Udyan, at Indroda village, nice place to visit for both children and adults.
In sector 9 and along the river front is the lovely Sarita Udyan, a great spot for picnickers. The entire area is being developed to provide full recreational facilities.
A nature park having a dinosaur fossil park, a botanical garden, a deer park, a blue whale skeleton on display, a cactus garden, a bird cage and places for family picnic.

Firozpur.x: Firozpur or Ferozpore is in the Malwa region of Punjab, in northern India.

Fatehpur Sikri.x: Fatehpur Sikri is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, about 40 km (25 mi) away from Agra.

see.d: This grand gate was built to commemorate the military triumphs of Mughal emperor Akbar in Gujarat.
One of the largest mosque complexes in India. The architecture blends Indian with Persian influences.
Salim Chishti was a Sufi saint, dearly respected by Emperor Akbar. In fact, the emperor held Salim in such great esteem that he named his son Salim (who would later be known as the Mughal…
The red sandstone architectural symmetry of the walls and bridges that crisscross the artificial lake or pool is beautiful but the water nowadays is polluted and dirty.
Birbal was a Hindu courtier of Akbar, who ended up becoming one of Akbar's closest and most trusted military advisors.
Striking architecturally, a central pillar dominates the hall which is thought to represent religious syncretism that Akbar sought.

Feroke.x: Feroke is a small town near Kozhikode in Malabar region, Kerala, India.

see.d: 1,000 m above sea level
Beach, lighthouse, fishing village.
Very tiny park with swings, merry-go-rounds, and slides. Ideal for taking photographs because of the river, bridge and wooden boats.
Very photogenic building built by the British in the 19th century.
Ferry service across River Chaliyar for only ₹5 per head. Take the 4:15PM bus to Edavannappara. Travel by bus/auto to Elamaram jetty. Cross the river and come back the same route.
Bird sanctuary. Birds can be spotted only between November and February. (Herons, Sandpipers, whimbrels and Terns).

do.d: Walk from the Railway Station to the Commonwealth Tile Factory on the bank of River Chaliyar.
Small rooftop farm growing rice, cabbage, lemon, ladies fingers, peas, carrots, brinjals, spinach, ginger and turmeric.
A ten-acre hill with scenic sunrise. Suitable for cycling and trekking. Ottamaram or 'single tree' is the highest point.

Faridkot.x: Faridkot is royal and historic city in Punjab, India. In 2011, it was home to around 88,000 people.

see.d: It is believed that Baba Sheikh Farid left his godari (jacket) there before entering Faridkot town.

Dubrajpur.x: Dubrajpur is a town in the central region of West Bengal.

see.d: A palace built in the shape of a castle with 999 doors.
A large number of large sized rocks are found in the area. Two remarkable pieces of these rocks were known as Mama and Bhagne (maternal uncle and nephew).

Gaya.x: Gaya is a major pilgrimage city in Bihar for Hindus. It is visited for doing piṇḍ dān (funeral offerings for the benefit of the soul of the deceased) and for visiting Bodh Gaya and Vishnupad temple.

see.d: Hillock, which offers nice bird's eye view of the plains.
A temple on top of the mountain. One of the most holy Shakti peeths of India.
Hillock, which offers nice bird's eye view of the plains.
Has got the impression of Lord Vishnu's foot. Lots of person visiting every year to offer Shrad for their died family member (Purvaj).

Ghatshila.x: Ghatshila is a town in East Singhbhum district of Jharkhand, India.

Ghaziabad.x: Ghaziabad is a suburb east of Delhi, in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh in India. It is often called the "Gateway of Uttar Pradesh" from the western side.

see.d: Hanuman temple with an adjacent bazzar.

do.d: The only IMAX dome of north India.
Multiplex with three screens.

Giridih.x: Giridih, is a mining town in northern Jharkhand, India.

see.d: 10 km from Giridh, it is a water reservoir, one of the best sites for water-related adventure sports and bird watching.A water reservoir some 10 km North-East of Giridih headquarters is one…
This is a famous Shivlinga temple. A small hamlet about 60 km South-west of Giridih district headquarter under Bagodar Block possesses the largest Shiva Linga of India. Its height is 65 ft.
Langta baba was a saint of the locality, and is worshiped like a god. Offering chadar to his samadhi is a ritual followed here.
This is a nice and beautiful temple built in the middle of a lake in the shape of a lotus flower.
An institution which spreads the message of Sant Kabir and Sanatan Dharma. It has beautiful temple Guru Govind Dham and Kabir Gyan Darshan with murals and paintings based on life of Sant…
14 km away from Giridh, Three Wheeler Autorickshaws are available as the main local transport here.A famous picnic spot situated about 14 km east of Giridih town Amidst in the range of the…

Goa.x: Goa, a state on India's west coast, is a former Portuguese colony with a rich history. Spread over 3,700 km² with a population of approximately 1.4 million, Goa is small by Indian standards. It has a unique mix of Indian and Portuguese cultures and architecture that attracts an estimated 2.5 million visitors each year (including about 400,000 foreign tourists).

do.d: You can experience the real Goa while helping in projects in orphanages, nature centres, animal rescue and charity shops.

Gokarna.x: Gokarna is a small pilgrimage town on the coast in the Karnataka state of India. It's a conservative Hindu pilgrimage town, home to several temples and festivals. The town is full of locals and pilgrims, and doesn't have much in the way of facilities for tourists, other than a handful of guesthouses and local restaurants.

Gondia.x: Gondia is a city in Vidarbha close to the Madhya Pradesh state border.

do.d: Considered to be a "green oasis" in the easternmost portions of Maharashtra, Nagzira hosts a number of migratory birds species, including 13 that are endangered.
Another hotspot of diverse flora and fauna. It is a popular picnic place among the locals.

Gopalpur.x: Gopalpur-on-sea is a beach resort in Ganjam district of Odisha (formerly Orissa). Once a busy sea port, it is now a quiet place. The din and bustle of the temple towns is totally absent and one can really enjoy the roar of the waves and the breeze bustling through the palm trees.

Gorakhpur.x: Gorakhpur is a city of 675,000 people (2011) in the eastern part of the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is the administrative headquarters of Gorakhpur District and Gorakhpur Division. Located near the Nepalese border, it is on the popular overland route from India to Nepal.

see.d: A good place to spark children's interest in astronomy and physics. The planetarium runs 45-minute long shows at 1pm, 3pm and 5pm daily.
The second largest zoo in the state with several big cats, deer, monkeys, bears, reptiles, birds and fish in the aquarium section.
Beautiful temple of Lord Krishna and Radha
A temple named after Yogi Gorakhnath.
200-year old church with rich history.
Nice and quiet place to visit.

do.d: You can go Taramandal for boating
The only water park in Gorakhpur, it has a number of water slides, pools, wave pools and a few non-water related amusement rides like a merry-go-round and Ferris wheel.

Goregaon (Raigad).x: Goregaon is a city in the Raigad district of Maharashtra near the river Kal.

see.d: Bheema Devi Peeth is the latest addition in the tourist spot around Goregaon. It has spectacular stone temple of Goddess Bhima with beautiful surrounding of 42 acres (16 ha).
Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Technological University is the only one of its kind in the State.
Enjoy the beautiful view of Kaal river.
Temple of Mallikarjun or Siddhesvar is said to have been built about 800 years ago. The shrine is said to be self-originated or Svayambhu.
Panhalghar fort is one of the fort from King Shivaji era. You will have to climb the fort. The water tanks are still visible on the top of the fort.
The temple of Vithoba is 200 years old and has fine specimens of sculpture and carving on the pillars.

Gorumara National Park.x: Gorumara National Park is a national park in the Dooars of West Bengal.

see.d: Good for birding.
An elephant camp with five cottages and a treehouse.
Named after a legendary elephant.

Guntur.x: Guntur is the third-largest city in Andhra Pradesh, southwest of the state capital Amaravati. Once known as Garthapuri, the city is a major trade hub for chili, cotton and tobacco, and home to Asia's largest chili yard. Amaravati, Guntur and Vijayawada together constitute the "Capital Region" (CR) of Andhra Pradesh, the modern heart of the state since 2014.

see.d: Guntur's landmark tower, named after the founder of Pakistan. According to a legend, Liaquat Ali Khan, a representative of Jinnah, visited Guntur in the pre-Independence era.
This historical fort was built during the reign of the Reddy kings in the 14th century CE. There are 21 structures in the fort.
The water tanks in the village are unique as they provide refuge to many species birds including endangered Spot-Billed Pelicans and Painted Storks.
This is the place of Sri Viswayogi Viswamji and the Universal Integration Pillar. It is an envisioned symbol of oneness of humanity.
The oldest temple in Guntur, dedicated to Shiva. As the legend goes, the sage Agastya built this temple during the Treta Yuga, centring around a naturally-occurring Swayambhu Lingam.

do.d: Often called the "Central Park of Guntur".

Gurugram.x: Gurugram or Gurgaon, a satellite city in South Haryana, is a major IT and shopping hub of Delhi. Once a mere commuter town, Gurugram now boasts slick office complexes housing companies from Accenture to Xerox, with more shopping malls per square mile than anywhere else in India. However, the city is also one of the victims of Delhi's unprecedented urban sprawl, with poor infrastructure, traffic jams as well as the winter smog.

see.d: Sohna Lake is about 10 km from Gurgaon. It is best to visit after rainfall and during winters.
India's largest camera museum. One can visit from Tuesday-Saturday from 11AM-5PM only via appointments.
Miniature railway modelling project about 5 km off National Highway 8 through a bumpy road.
A rare temple dedicated to the teacher Dronacharya in the Mahabharata epic.
The park on the Aravalli Range includes a number of trails and a native plant nursery and interpretive displays at the entrance.

do.d: DT City Centre and Mega Mall. Tickets would cost you around ₹150 on weekdays and as much as ₹200 on a big opening on weekends. Late shows too last show starts around 11PM!
Sahara Mall (2 screens), Metropolitian Malls (9 screens), Ambience Mall (9 screens). Good thing is that there are lot of late shows the last show starts almost at midnight
The Devi Art Foundation is one of the first not-for-profit spaces dedicated to showcasing contemporary art from the Indian Subcontinent.
Chill down your summer heat, water games and sports are great fun. Don't forget to take you swim wear.
An exciting place to be, especially for kids, with more than 100 trampolines connected with built-in rock climbing optional too.

Guruvayoor.x: Guruvayoor is one of the most sacred and important pilgrim towns in India. This temple-town is extremely famous for its large Sree Krishna Temple, believed to be one of the 108 most divine Vishnu temples of world. The town is in Thrissur district, about 102 km from Kochi.

see.d: One of the earliest Christian churches of the sub-continent. Established by St. Thomas, it is one of the seven-and-a-half churches he founded.
The large Shiva Temple, is 500 m from the Main temple. Its believe Lord Shiva was the original owner of Guruvayur temple and decided to relocate to current site to place the Vishnu idol in…
Located within a kilometer from main temple, it's a must see temple, with its main shrine built as a chariot and Lord Krishna sitting as Parthasarathy, advocating Gita to Arjuna.
A small temple, dedicated to Thirupathi Venkatachalapathy, established by Telugu pilgrims as their token to devotion to Lord Krishna.
Devaswom museum is very close to Guruvayur temple’s east gate. The museum has many collections of antiques, temple materials, mural paintings, musical instruments and other valuable…
Vrindavanam Gokulam Estate is a 100-acre estate at Vengad in Malapuram District under the possession of Devaswom.

do.d: The highlight of Guruvayur Ekadashi day is this Carnatic music festival that brings together musicians from across South India.
This is one of the main festivals of temple, held on Ekadeshi day of month of November, where the temples are illuminated with more than 10,000 lamps.
The annual Guruvayur festival is in months of February–March, as per Malayalam calendar and zodiac signs. The festival is for 10 days.
Outside the temple, this is a regular venue for various cultural performance. People irrespective of caste, religion etc can attend and watch the regular performances at the hall.

Garh Panchkot.x: Among the hills in the Purulia district of West Bengal, the ruins of Garh Panchkot are a silent testimony to the Bargi attack during the 18th century. The ruins sit on the slopes of Panchet Hill and adjacent to Panchet Lake, is a scenic hilly forested area, with a tinge of history. Garh Panchkot was a fortified area owned by the Rajas of Panchkot, the Singh Deo dynasty.

see.d: Ruins of a fort of the Rajas of Panchkot.
This hill is about high and occupies an area of . It is thickly forested. The area is located on the lowest step of the Chota Nagpur Plateau.

Golaghat.x: Calm and scenic, Golaghat, one of the oldest urban agglomerations of Assam, has a beautiful landscape with several streams. Within the city limits, there are two wildlife preserves, a UNESCO-listed park, ancient ruins and sacred Hindu and Christian sites from the 17th and 19th centuries.

see.d: Assam's one of the oldest burial grounds dating back to India's pre-independence era, containing 28 burials of British officers.
One of the oldest and biggest Baptist churches in Assam that was established in December AD 1898.
One of the prominent religious places of Assam. The Namghar was built in AD 1681 by Ahom king Gadapani.
Constructed in AD 1687 by Ahom king Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha, perched on a hill top, it is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Assam.
Museum contains dolls, artefacts, mementos, movies and other personal collections of Dr. Banerjee (a Padma Shri awardee, and a medical doctor from Edinburgh and Liverpool Universities).
Spread across 97 square kilometres (37 sq mi) in 3 blocks, the sanctuary is famous as a spot for Hot water spring and wildlife viewpoint to spot Rhino and other animals.

do.d: With a landscape of sprawling tea estates in and around Golaghat, planning an excursion to visit the heritage buildings and sites gives a very refreshing experience to travellers.

do.n: A walk down to Dhansiri bridge
do.d: A walk down the Dhansiri bridge towards the river offers a very beautiful sight. It is a popular picnic and outdoor spot for barbecues for the citizens of Golaghat and travellers alike.
Jeep safaris to Kaziranga National Park is one of the best ways to experience the scenic beauty of the protected area for wildlife.

Guptipara.x: Guptipara is a village in the Hooghly district of West Bengal. It is an important Vaishnava centre known for its temples and rath. The place has a rich history along with a mix of tradition and legends.

see.d: The place of Bengal's first barowari (publicly organised) Durga Puja which introduced Sri Bindhyabasini Jagaddhatri Puja. Guptipara was a citadel of Vaishnavite culture.
It houses four Vaishnava (of Lord Vishnu) temples: Chaitanya, Brindabanchandra, Ramchandra and Krishnachandra.
The Temple where the Jagannath idols are kept during Rathayatra.
A dedicated shrine to the goddess Kali.

do.d: Rathayatra is more than 400 years old. The present ratha or the chariot is a wooden Nabaratna temple having nine shikharas. The ratha has a square base measuring by .

Greater Noida.x: Greater Noida is a modern city in the Upper Doab region of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is a fast-growing business, education, and technology hub near New Delhi and Noida. It has wide roads, green spaces, and planned infrastructure.

see.d: A landmark educational institution known for its architecture, cultural events, and open green spaces.
A protected nature reserve, home to over 180 species of birds. Best for bird watching and eco-tourism.

do.d: India’s first Formula One race track, hosting motorsports events, karting, and driving experiences. Since 2023, it has been the home of the MotoGP Grand Prix of India.

do.n: Shaheed Vijay Singh Pathik Sports Complex

Chandrakona.x: Chandrakona is a town in Paschim Medinipur, West Bengal.

see.d: A 17th-century stone-built temple.

Goalpara.x: Goalpara is a town in Lower Assam, along the Brahmaputra.

Gwalior.x: Gwalior is a historic city in northern Madhya Pradesh. Gwalior's history is reflected most famously in its fort, but also in the architecture of other buildings, and in addition, the city is known as a centre of Indian classical music.

see.d: Literally meaning "canopy", Chhatris are elevated, dome-shaped pavilions used as an element in Indian architecture. These chhatris were built in 1817 in memory of the king Jayajirao Scindia.
One of many of the beautiful zoological parks of Madhya Pradesh. This park includes a white tiger, golden pheasants, sambhar, bison, and many other animals.
an ideal picnic spot for the whole family or a group of school children. The garden adjacent to the palace grounds is built in Italian style.
The museum has a diverse range of exhibits, including sculptures made from terracotta, bronze and stone, paintings, inscriptions, weapons and other excavated material from the Sunga, Gupta…
A former residential palace turned museum of Scindias. Contains the world's largest chandelier as well as many diverse collections of antiques and gadgets.
A very ornate 10th-century Hindu temple, probably dedicated to Shiva, of which only the Mukhamandapa remains, with exquisite sculpture from ceiling to floor.

do.d: A great place for an outing, boating and other water facilities are available.
Be Safe while Visiting.10+ Peoples have died while bathing.
The biggest fair of Madhya Pradesh and a very colourful one. It begins in the second week of January and continues until February.

Hampi.x: Hampi, in the state of Karnataka, India, is the site of the once-magnificent capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. The ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

#23. Dedicated to Vithoba, an avatar (incarnation) of the gods Vishnu and Krishna. The famous Stone Chariot is here as well as the Musical Pillars.
