Haridwar.x: Haridwar, also spelt Hardwar, is a Hindu pilgrimage site at the Ganges River, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

see.d: Dedicated to Mother India, it is half temple, half nation-building exercise, with seven floors stacked with deities, saints, and secular heroes of all Indian faiths. Some signage in English.
A temple dedicated to Chandi Devi on the Neel Parvat. It was built in 1929 by Suchat Singh, the King of Kashmir.
To the north of the centre, this is Haridwar's focal point, where devotees gather to bathe and worship on the Ganges.
Located on upper road. This temple is one of the 51 Shakti Pithas and it's the presiding deity of Haridwar. It is from this temple Haridwar derives its other name Mayapur.
At top of hill near the centre of town. Can be reached by cable car (₹48 for a return ticket) or by a road that gently winds uphill (about 2 km), starting from Railway Rd.
Located outside of Haridwar and within the Rajaji National Park, this serene and religious site is a place to see. Permission to enter this site is required from forest rangers.

do.d: While walking around the park you can spot elephants, leopards and deer. The bird life is prolific here and there is a large elephant population.

Haryana.x: Haryana is a state in northwestern India, southeast of Punjab. Often overlooked by the travellers to northern India, Haryana is home to various historical and religious sites. Surrounding the city of Delhi by three sides, the state also dominates the city's suburban and commercial sprawl, including the bustling tech hub of Gurugram.

Hassan.x: Hassan is a small town in Karnataka State. It is a once-in-a-lifetime trip to the heart of Karnataka architecture, greenery and water.

see.d: This dam was built across the Hemavathy river in early 1900s and forms the Hemavathi Reservoir. 46 villages were submerged by the dam waters.
There are 2 temples – Chennakeshava and Someshwara temples – built in Hoysala architecture with intricate details.
This is a holy town on the banks of River Cauvery. This temple town is also known as “Dakshin Kashi” for its many temples that are at the banks of the river.
This church is said to have been built about 450 years and is in Gothic architecture. The church gets submerged by the Hemavathy River backwaters.
This temple is a modern construction on top of a hill. The Hanuman statue. The drive to the hill is very picturesque and the road is very good. The temple is open from 6:30AM to 5PM.
This dam was built across the Hemavathy river in early 1900s and forms the Hemavathi Reservoir. 46 villages were submerged by the dam waters.

Hisar.x: Hisar is a district and divisional headquarter city in the state of Haryana in India.

see.d: Built by the Tughlaq Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1394, the palace is made from red sandstone and is an example of Seljuk architecture.
A village and Indus Valley Civilisation archeological site. Although only 5% of the site has been excavated, many interesting artifacts have been found so far, including fire altars, toys,…
An important point for several migratory birds.
A 19-hectare (48-acre) park containing 20 blackbucks, 16 chital spotted deer and six sambar A part of the park is reserved for fodder.
A park which preserves many endangered species of herbs used in Ayurvedic medicine.

Hospet.x: Hospet, now known officially as Hosapete, is a city in Karnataka. The name Hosapete literally means "new market". Hospet is the town nearest to the Hampi/Kishkinda area.

do.d: This is one of the biggest dams in Karnataka. Take a bus or share auto here for ₹10, or a tuk-tuk for ₹60.

Howrah.x: Howrah is the twin city of Kolkata and an important industrial and transport hub of southern West Bengal.

see.n: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden
see.d: An extraordinary place of vivid nature under the smog filled sky of the city. You will value the silence that is only filled by some birds singing.
Officially Rabindra Setu (রবীন্দ্র সেতু Robīndro Setu), the Howrah Bridge is one of the iconic bridges of West Bengal. See the Kolkata listing for details.
Based on the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, the gate is an entrance to the Kolkata West International City (KWIC), a satellite township in Howrah developed by Indonesia's Ciputra Group.
A large lake next to Santragachi railway station. It attracts a lot of migratory birds in the winter months, particularly in December and January, impart because migratory birds are…
A pair of brass statues of the Buddha at Kona Expressway.
The longest cable-stayed bridge in India and one of the longest in Asia, south/downstream of Howrah Bridge. See the Kolkata listing for details.

do.d: An amusement park. Within the park, there is a pond and the trees around here provide greenery to the region. A marriage hall is also present here for marriage events.
A sports complex with plays host to several prominent talent hunt contests and sports activities.

do.n: Howrah Planetarium and Astronomical Research Centre
do.d: A planetarium in Howrah with virtual tours of the night sky and cosmic shows in a specially perforated hemispherical dome. It is India's first 3D planetarium.

Jaigaon.x: Jaigaon is a city in the Alipurduar district of West Bengal, India. It is a trading post for cross-border business with Bhutan. Unless you are planning to enter Bhutan or have an interest in construction material and fake branded clothes, there is no reason to visit Jaigaon.

see.d: A traditional-style Bhutanese gate, used as a gateway between India and Bhutan.

Jharkhand.x: Jharkhand is a state in Eastern India. Home to the Chota Nagpur Plateau, Jharkhand can fairly claim to be one of the most attractive parts of the country. The scenery of the main plateau is most attractive with its undulations, detached abrupt hills and forest tracts.

Haldwani and Kathgodam.x: Haldwani and Kathgodam are twin towns in the Kumaon division of Uttarakhand, India, situated in the Bhabar foothills along the banks of the Gaula River. Known as the "Gateway to Kumaon," Haldwani is the commercial and logistics hub of the region. Kathgodam ("Timber Depot") is the scenic terminal railhead nestled against the Himalayan foothills.

see.d: A quiet reservoir and wide pebbly riverbed, favoured for birdwatching, sunrise walks and quiet reflection. The forested foothills form a dramatic backdrop.
An easy, unpaved walking route that follows the river into sal and pine forest. Rich in birds (kingfishers, barbets, forktails) and occasional sightings of barking deer.
A pedestrian hanging bridge across the Gaula River, offering fine views of the valley and the forested hills. A peaceful spot to watch the river rush beneath, and a popular photo point.
Entry point to the Gaula forest range, with marked nature trails and bird-watching hides. The checkpost staff can advise on current trail conditions and recent wildlife sightings.
An international spiritual community founded by the mystic Haidakhan Baba, set in a wooded valley beside a stream. The main temple and meditation hall are open to day visitors.
A small, ancient hilltop shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali. The 20-minute climb through a scrubby forest rewards with sweeping views over Haldwani, the Gaula valley and the Shivalik ridges.

do.d: Well-maintained park with a man‑made lake, paddle boats, shady paths and a cafeteria. Entry ₹10.
A tree-covered park ideal for a quiet stroll or jog, managed by the forest department.
A small riverside park with lawns, children’s play equipment and benches overlooking the Gaula.
A youth‑led environmental organisation based in Haldwani. Their flagship project organises tree-plantation drives, riverside clean‑ups and nature education walks along the Gaula.

Patna.x: Patna, the capital of Bihar, is a bustling city in the Indian Plains with a glorious past. It is a gateway to the Buddhist and Jain pilgrimage centres of Vaishali, Rajgir, Nalanda, Bodh Gaya, Kesariya and Pawapuri.

see.d: Captain John Garstin built a Golghar for the storage of food for the British army with storing capacity of 140,000 tons in 1786.
The bridge over the river Ganges connecting Patna and Hajipur.
Explore the ancient ruins of Pataliputra. Of the 80 pillars (Fa Hien, in 5th century CE, found the pillars shining as bright as glass) excavated at the site; only one remains.
Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar. It has several galleries, including the regional gallery, the contemporary gallery, the historical art galleries and the gallery…
Small local history museum, named after independence hero and first minister of Bihar, Deep Narayan Singh, who was born in Hajipur.
A public museum showcasing the life and principles of Mahatma Gandhi. It contains an exhibition containing photos, paintings, sculptures, manuscripts and quotations; all the major events in…

do.d: You can buy famous Maner Ka Ladoo(Sweets). Maner Sweets is one of the popular shops that specializes in these. However, avoid going there in the late evening or night.
Largest cattle and animal fair in Asia. It is held in November in Sonepur which across the Ganges from Patna.
A large park constructed in former jail ground is an oasis from noise and bustle of the city.
Contains attractions like waterslides, wave pool, swimming pools, multi-cuisine restaurant, coffee shops, souvenir shops and a banquet hall.
Gandhi Maidan is the heart of this city today.

Hosur.x: Hosur is an industrial town in northern Tamil Nadu, on the bank of the River Ponnaiyar. It is considered the manufacturing twin of Bangalore (Bengaluru) due to its presence of major manufacturing industries, compared to Bangalore's presence of major IT industries.

see.d: An ancient Shiva temple. The exact history of the temple is unknown. This is the only temple in Northern Tamil Nadu that uses a golden chariot for temple functions.
The birthplace of C. Rajagopalachari, fondly called "Rajaji".

Honavar.x: Honavar (also spelled Honnavar) is a port town on the coast of Arabian Sea in Uttara Kannada district of Karavali region of Karnataka. Sharavathi river flows through this town and joins the Arabian Sea. Konkan Railway's longest bridge, which is about 2km long, also runs through this town.

see.d: At Apsarakonda, one can get nice view of Arabian sea and beach from hilltop. There's also a small waterfall, garden and temple at this place.
The beach is about 2km from Honavar and about 5km long on the coast of Arabian Sea.
This fortified island is 4km from Honavar. It has a total area of 19 hectares and an elevation of 45 to 50m and a temple was constructed by the ruler between the 16th and 17th century.
Idagunji Devasthana is an ancient temple with a history of more than 1,500 years.

do.d: Motorboat and shikara-style boat rides through the pristine Sharavathi river backwaters and tidal creeks.
Elevated wooden timber boardwalk constructed over the sensitive tidal mangrove marsh.

do.n: Kasarkod Blue Flag Eco Beach Walk
do.d: Stroll along the 5-km stretch of clean golden sands. Awarded the international Blue Flag certification for eco-tourism standards, featuring solar-powered energy, children's park, purified…

Hoshiarpur.x: Hoshiarpur is a city in the Doaba region of the Punjab of India. It stands at 300 m (982 m) altitude so it's a little cooler than the nearby sultry river plains, with forested upland terrain.

see.d: The museum's main attractions are a collections of sculptures during the medieval kingdom period as well as fossils and stone tools from a much earlier era in the ancient site of Dhol Baha,…
You will come across nilgai, wild boars, peacocks, deer and leopards at this sanctuary.

do.d: One of the oldest cinema complexes in town. Classier but pricier than the cinemas in the malls.
A large cinema with good acoustics. The popcorn and snacks are quite costly.

Halisahar.x: Halisahar is a town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal.

see.d: Scenic views of the Hooghly at sunset.
An at-chala temple with terracotta reliefs.
Birthplace of Ramprasad Sen, known for composing various hymns and poems. The Ramprasadi tune used to sing his song has influenced various composers, including Rabindranath Tagore.

Hooghly.x: Hooghly is a former Portuguese colony at the Hooghly River, in the Hooghly district of West Bengal.

see.d: Founded in 1817 beside the Hooghly River, Hooghly Jail is one of the oldest prison centres in West Bengal. During British rule, political prisoners were kept there in solitary confinement.
A congregation hall for Shia Muslims. It was built with the money of Haji Muhammad Mohsin from 1841 to 1861.
A former rail bridge over the Hooghly River between Bandel and Naihati. The bridge was opened on 16 February 1885 in the golden jubilee year of the reign of Queen Victoria.
Haji Muhammad Mohsin (1732–1812) was a philanthropist. He had inherited a lot of money from his relatives and spent them mostly in philanthropy.

Haldibari.x: Haldibari in Cooch Behar is the last station of North Bengal in West Bengal.

see.d: One of the 51 Shakti Pithas. It is believed that the left leg of Shakti fell here.

Hanumangarh.x: Hanumangarh is a town in the Bagar region of Rajasthan. It is home to the 1700-year-old Bhatner Fort, considered to be one of the oldest forts of India.

Hubli.x: Hubli, officially known as Hubballi, is a city in Northwestern Karnataka. The city is a bustling trading centre of little scenic beauty.

see.d: 11th-century Shiva temple.
promising panoramic view of the expanse of Hubli City- with in city,

Beautiful place to visit.

Hyderabad.x: Hyderabad,, the "Pearl City", is the capital of the state of Telangana. Founded in the late 16th century on the hot and dry Deccan Plateau, Hyderabad is a city replete with history and traditions, as well as the wonderful palaces, mosques, bazaars, lakes and other heritage sites in the city. One of the most populous cities in Southern India, the modern-day Hyderabad is the result of the amalgamation with its twin city Secunderabad across the Hussain Sagar lake, a former British enclave during the city's Nizam rule.

do.d: They are organized by the Telangana tourism department and led by a knowledgeable guide and Tourist Police.
For reptile conservation work and field trips.
Active and well-organised trekker’s group organising out of the Hyderabad area. It makes an effort to be as inclusive as possible by offering adventure treks at all levels, from bouldering…

Indore.x: Indore, the commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, is on the Malwa Plateau. While growing at a fast pace, it still manages to combine traditional and modern lifestyles. Indoris are well known for their warm and friendly attitude.

see.d: It is a famous temple of the goddess of food. The name of the temple Annapurna means "anna" which literally means food. The people in town have great faith in the temple.
Better known for its size than antiquity, this temple houses perhaps the largest Ganesh idol in the world measuring 25 feet from crown to foot.
Right across from the famous MY Hospital in Indore, in the Jaora Compound Area, is the statue of Rai Bahadur Sir Siremal Bapna, the legendary Prime Minister of Holkar State during the reign…
The Indore Museum houses the finest collection of Parmar sculptures from Hinglajgarh.
Chhatris are the tombs or cenotaphs erected in memory of dead Holkar rulers and their family members.
One of the most famous temples in the city. Located near the heart of town (Palasia). You can find idols of almost all gods and goddesses and the peace found here is unique.

do.d: It is a huge garden with a fountain show and many kinds of plants and flowers are planted here. It brings you close to nature within the city itself and lovely point for couples.
A one of its kind Rajasthani Village-themed park become amusement park and restaurant. This is an exclusive park in Indore which lets you enter into the world of a Rajathani village.
The most beautiful park in town. It was developed by Indore Development Authority on the banks of ancient pipliyapala lake.
Another famous water cum amusement park in the outskirts of the busy town. A park that offers wide range of entertainment.

Jabalpur.x: Jabalpur is an ancient city in Central India, on the shores of the holy river Narmada and on the tributary plains of the Hiran, Gour, Ken and Sone rivers. This article also covers the small neighbouring villages of Bagri and Dumna.

see.d: Jabalpur is also famous for eroded volcanic rock formations called as Balancing Rock of Jabalpur. Amazingly this rock survived even in earthquake of magnitude 6.5.

see.n: Gopal Lal Ji Maharaj Ka Mandir, Hanumantal
see.d: Pushti Margiya Mandir of Lord Krishna and Radha. No mandir (temple) is like this in the Mahakaushal region. No donations allowed here.
Nearest ghat of the Namada River to have a holy dip (snan) in Narmada. There is always a small mela present. At 19:30 every day, there is traditional Narmada aarti (worship ritual).
Small wildlife reserve and a beautiful dam, one source of drinking water to Jabalpur.
Built by the Gond ruler, Raja Madan Shah, in 1116 atop a rocky hill, the fort dominates the skyline and provides a panoramic view of the town and the country side around it.
Dedicated to the memory of the great Queen Durgavati is her memorial and a museum which houses a fine collection of sculptures, inscriptions and prehistoric relics.

Jagdalpur.x: Jagdalpur is a city in Bastar district in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh.

see.d: Shaped like a horseshoe, it is a popular picnic spot.
The third largest waterfall in India, justly known as the "Indian Niagara Falls", will not disappoint you.

Jaipur.x: Jaipur, also known as the Pink City, is the capital of Indian state of Rajasthan, and its largest city. The city was built in the 18th century by Sawai Jai Singh as India's first planned city, and today it's a major tourist attraction for Indians and for international visitors. It is a very picturesque city with splendid palaces, forts and historical monuments and belongs to the tourist Golden Triangle along with Delhi and Agra.

see.d: This massive fort-palace complex built in hybrid Hindu-Muslim style dates back to Raja Man Singh and was the royal palace of the Kachwahas from c. 1600-1727.
A palace adorned with thousands on thousands of mirror tiles on the walls and ceiling.
Never conquered in battle, this was considered the strongest of the three forts in the area.
The smallest of the three forts, notable primarily for excellent views over Man Sagar lake and the vast sprawl of Jaipur.
An imposing blend of traditional Rajput and Mughal architecture. It is a vast palace complex occupying nearly one-seventh of the Pink City. It was built by Maharaja Jai Singh II.
Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Singh as part of City Palace, it was an extension of the Zenana (women's) chamber.

do.n: Amber Fort Sound and Light Show
do.d: Experience the history, culture and life of Amber through this spectacular show. Amitabh Bachhan narrates the story of Rajasthani kings with a script written by Gulzar.
With a capacity of 30,000, this hosts the Rajasthan team and Rajathan Royals in IPL.

do.n: B.M. Birla Auditorium and Conference Hall
do.d: These are at the heart of Jaipur. This auditorium is spread over 9.8 acres and includes a computer centre, interactive science museum, an information processing centre, library, a…
An experience in itself, and another "don't miss". Once known as the best cinema India, and still the best in Rajasthan, it offers an overwhelming experience.
Heiwa Heaven is a Jaipur-based luxury resort that hosts parties and destination weddings.

Jalandhar.x: Jalandhar is a city in Punjab, India. Jalandhar is now industrial center with leather goods and sport equipments being the big earners. This is a good place to share Punjabi people passion for foods.

see.d: A replica of Amritsar Golden Temple.
Nice park for strolling.
The town was founded by the Hindu Kamboh. The Kamboh settlements lay to the west of present town and the sites are still marked by extensive ruins and two old tombs, now called the Black…

do.d: Almost all students in Punjab are taken on school trips to visit Science City.
One the best place for enjoyment for one day outing for the entire family with thrilling rides, water games and many more.

Jaldapara National Park.x: Jaldapara National Park is a national park in the Alipurduar district of West Bengal, India.

Jaleswar.x: Jaleswar is a small town in the east of India.

Jalgaon.x: Jalgaon is a major and a very large city in western India, located in Northern Maharashtra state within the region of Khandesh. It is mostly famous for its gold, bananas, cotton and industries. It's metropolitan area is being marked as largest in North part of Maharashtra.

see.d: Boating, You can see rabbit, ostrich, sunflower garden.
A museum and research institution dedicated to the life and achievements of Mahatma Gandhi.

Jalpaiguri.x: Jalpaiguri, a small city on the Teesta River in North Bengal, is a twin of the larger city Siliguri.

see.d: Palace of the Raikat family of the Baiknthapur Estate. Although the original palace was built in 1770, the modern palace was built in the early 20th century by Raja Jayantadev Raikat.
Karala, a small river, flows through the middle of the town, bisecting it into two halves.

do.d: Jubilee Park is situated on the bank of River Teesta. There is a garden with different flowering plants. There is a wooden statue of an elephant.
Watch football matches and other sporting events.

Jammu.x: Jammu, the largest city in the Jammu region of northern India, is the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir, sitting at a low elevation in the mainly mountainous state. Srinagar, the state's summer capital, is at a much higher elevation.

see.d: A beautiful red sandstone palace that has been converted into a museum. It stands amidst the most picturesque surroundings of Jammu.
5 km. These extensive gardens, laid around the Bahu Fort provide a pleasant view of the city.
5 km. Situated on a rock face on the left bank of the river Tawi.

see.n: Dargah of Peer Budhan Ali Shah (Peer Baba)
see.d: On the backside of the Civil Airport is famous Dargah of the Muslim saint, Peer Budhan Ali Shah.

see.n: Maha Maya Temple and City Forest
see.d: On the By-pass Road behind Bahu Fort, the city forest surrounds the ancient Maha Maya Temple overlooking the river Tawi.
The most memorable and beautiful work of King Lalitaditya is the construction of spacious Martand temple, which the emperor got built in honor of the Sun God or Bhaskar.

Jammu and Kashmir.x: For the Pakistani-controlled part of Kashmir, see Azad Kashmir. Jammu and Kashmir is a union territory in northern India. It is primarily in the Himalayan mountains, an area of great beauty and diversity offering much in the way of outdoor activities and spectacular sights for the tourist.

see.d: One of the Hindu trinity, Shiva is considered by Hindus to be a living god. Legend has it that Shiva recounted to his consort Parvati the secret of creation in a cave in Amarnath.
Bahu Fort was built by the Raja Bahulochan and modified and improved by the Dogra rulers of Jammu. This fort is around 5km from the main city and perhaps is the oldest edifice in the Jammu.
Located in the heart of Srinagar, this beautiful lake is fed by natural springs.
Gulmarg is a small hill station 52 km from Srinagar. While trekking, horse riding and picnics can be fun in summer, in winter it has some of the best powder snow and slopes for skiers.
A pilgrimage to the holy shrine of Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Ji (the Hindu Mother Goddess) is considered to be one of the holiest for Hindus.
Mubarak Palace was built with the touch of three different styles, Rajasthani, Mughal and Gothic. The most famous part of this palace is the Sheesh Mahal segment.

Jamnagar.x: Jamnagar, the Jewel of Kathiawar, is a coastal city on the Gulf of Kutch, in the state of Gujarat, India. It has unspoilt islands and beaches, hills, temples, palaces, forest, fantastic birdlife in the bird sanctuary and marine sanctuaries and fascinating corals and marine life in the Marine National Park. Its metro population was 600,000 in 2018.

see.d: This is where Ramdhun Sri Ram Jay Ram Jay Jay Ram is being chanted non-stop since the last 51 years. And it is a world record registered with The Guinness Book of World Records.
The two Jain temples in the Chandi Bazaar area are worth visiting. They are historic temples built around 1564-1622.
A historical palace with Rajput and European style architecture.

Jagatsinghpur.x: Jagatsinghpur is in the North Coast of Odisha, around 40 km from Cuttack, and around 65 km from Bhubaneswar by road.

see.d: In a village called Jhankad, under Tirtol Block of Jagatsinghpur District, around 18 km by road from Jagatsinghpur. Deity of Goddess Sarala is being worshiped here.
Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Igatpuri.x: Igatpuri is a town and hill station in Nashik district in the state of Maharashtra.

see.d: Founded by S.N.Goenka, Dhammagiri is a meditation centre offers courses in Vipasana (insight meditation) a technique taught by the Buddha in India, 2,500 years ago.
It is situated at the end of the Thal Ghat, just before entering Igatpuri from Mumbai. The valley lies in the basin of the majestic Bhatsa River.
A few km from Igatpuri, lies a huge and placid Arthur Lake, set like a huge jewel amidst the dense greenery. The lake is formed by the waters of the Pravara River in the Bhandardara region.
It is the highest peak in the Sahyadri ranges.
Built in 11th century AD, it is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Constructed in a distinct Hemadpanti style, the temple is surrounded by lush green fields and Mount Kalsubai the highest mountain in…
Just ahead of Igatpuri, after crossing the Camel Valley, comes across a small road, which leads to the Ghatandevi temple.

Jagadhri.x: Jagadhri is in Ambala Division in the northern Indian state of Haryana. This town is known for the cluster of brass and copper industries. Jagadhri is known as the "Brass City" of India.

see.d: This ancient monument was built during the reign of King Ashoka of the Maurya Empire.

do.d: Kalesar National Park and adjacent Kalesar Wildlife Sanctuary are protected areas in Kalesar of Yamunanagar district.

Jamboni.x: Jamboni is a town in the Jhargram district of West Bengal.

see.d: An ancient temple reconstructed in 1348, according to some. According to others, the present temple is just about a century old, the earlier Navaratna temple has been abandoned.
On the Jhargram-Jamboni Road and on the way to Chikligarh. Migratory birds visit the area in August-September.

Jainagar.x: Jainagar is a town in the Mithila region of Bihar, India, at the border to Nepal. The border town is one of the overland gateways to the Himalayan nation from India.

Ichalkaranji.x: Ichalkaranji is a city in the Kolhapur district of South Maharashtra, India, known for its prominent textile and engineering industries. Often referred to as the “Manchester of Maharashtra,” the city is one of the country’s leading centres for grey fabric production and hosts a dense network of power looms, processing units, and garment manufacturers. Ichalkaranji has experienced rapid industrial growth since the mid‑20th century, evolving from a small princely town into a major economic hub with strong cooperative and entrepreneurial traditions.

see.d: Ichalkaranji’s identity is deeply tied to its textile industry, and many visitors come specifically to observe the city’s power loom clusters and cooperative mills.
Dedicated to Lord Shiva, known for its peaceful atmosphere and traditional architecture. It’s a popular spot for morning and evening visits, especially during festivals like Mahashivaratri.
Dedicated to Lord Dattatreya, an important spiritual centre for locals. The temple complex becomes especially lively during Datta Jayanti.

do.d: A local sports ground that hosts athletic events, kabaddi matches, and community gatherings.

Kadapa.x: Kadapa, also called Cuddapah, is a city of 345,000 people (2011) in the state of Andhra Pradesh in India, 261 km from Chennai.

Jamshedpur.x: Jamshedpur is the largest city in the state of Jharkhand.

see.d: This park is at Shastri Nagar along the banks of the Kharkhai river.
Located in Telco, atop a small hill. Offers a panoramic view of the city, and the scenic surroundings (breathtaking view of a meandering river.) The temple premises add a serene and…
Located approximately 13 km from the centre of the township. It is a manmade lake built by Tata Steel for water supply to the town. It has wonderful scenario near the Dalma hills.
Located in Telco Colony, is a beautiful park and picnic spot with an artificial waterfall and lake.
This park was a gift by Tata Steel to the citizens of Jamshedpur on its 50th anniversary. This 200-acre park, with a rose garden and a lake, now has a zoo and an amusement park.
Very famous temple of Goddess Kali, made on a raised cut mountain.

do.d: Drive 20 min through Tata-Purulia Highway towards Purulia. There is a driveway from the base to the top of the hill, where you can stay.
This temple is atop a small hill and offers a panoramic view of the city.

Jaunpur.x: Jaunpur is a city in the Purvanchal part of Eastern Uttar Pradesh. A historical town with Medieval era fort, bridges and mosques. The city was founded by Feroz Shah Tughlaq and named in memory of his cousin, Jaun (popularly known as Muhammad bin Tughluq).

see.d: The name Sahi Quila literally translates into royal fort. The fort dates back to the 14th century and was constructed by Ibrahim Naib Barbak, a chieftain of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
The mosque dates back to 1376 and was built by Feroz Shah Tughlaq's brother Barbaq Shah. The mosque has three arches on the eastern side and is topped with three domes.
The Turkish Hammam is located next to the mosque. The hammam is located next to the mosque and is built in Turkish style.
A picturesque 16th century bridge across the Gombti which was constructed during Mughal times.
The mosque was constructed in 1408 by Ibrahim Shah Sharki. The foundation stone of the mosque was laid by Feorze Shah Tughlaque in 1393.
Built by Hussain Shah Sharqi, the 15th century is one of the largest in India. Situated inside a walled complex it has domed gates on the eastern, northern and southern sides.

Jhansi.x: Jhansi is a city in the Northern Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is very close to the central state of Madhya Pradesh and is overall more similar culturally to much of Madhya Pradesh than the rest of Uttar Pradesh. Jhansi's claim to fame is being the city where Rani Lakshmibai resisted against the British in the Great Rebellion of 1857.

see.d: Baruasagar is around 24 km from Jhansi. It is a small town on the bank of Betwa river. It has a large lake which is called Barua sagar tal.
Chirgaon is 30 km from Jhansi, It is on the banks of Betwa river. It is on National Highway 25. It is famous for National Poet Maithili Sharan Gupt who was from Chirgaon.
The fort of Jhansi was built in 1613, by Raja Bir Singh Judao (1606-27) of Orchha. This fort is built on a rocky hill and the city of Jhansi is around this fort.
The Government Museum is in a very picturesque location in the heart of the city. The surrounding area has some beautiful parks. At one side, is Deen Dayal Sabhagar (city auditorium).
This temple is in Jhansi cantonment. The beauty of this place is to visit it during sunrise. The spectacular view includes beautiful tree groves and beautiful aura of Jhansi.
Rani Mahal was built by Raghunath II of Newalkar family (1769-96). Rani Mahal is decorated with multicoloured paintings and art forms.

Jhargram.x: Jhargram is a town in the southwest region of West Bengal, India.

see.d: The zoo houses deer, snakes, peacocks, bears, crocodiles, black rabbits and various types of monkeys.
350 year old temple.

Jharsuguda.x: Jharsuguda is an upcoming industrial hub, popularly known as the powerhouse of Odisha, due to the large aluminium and power plants accessible from the city. Jharsuguda is located at the western end of Odisha (formerly known as Orissa).

see.d: old town temple
Ancient Shiva Temple.

Jind.x: Jind is a city in Haryana.

Jodhpur.x: Jodhpur is the second largest city in the state of Rajasthan. It is called the Gateway to Thar, as it is on the edge of the Thar desert. It is also called the Sun City as the sun shines (bright and hot) almost every day of the year.

see.d: Dominates the city and is the largest fort in all Rajasthan. Founded in 1458 as the site of Rao Jodha's new capital — hence the name, Jodhpur — the city has grown around it, and…
Royal cenotaphs built in marble, with a picturesque location next to a natural desert lake with lots of birds. Great view over the city and of the fort, as well as small well-kept gardens.
The ancient capital of Marwar, before Jodhpur was built.
Clearly visible to the south of the city and completed only in 1944, this is the last great palace built in India.
An architectural masterpiece built by Maharaja Sardar Singhji in 1910. It is illuminated with colorful lights at night.
Now converted to a resort.

do.d: International music festival held annually during October at Mehrangarh Fort.

Jorhat.x: Jorhat is a city of about 150,000 people (as of 2011) in Assam. It was the capital of the Ahom Kingdom.

see.d: Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary is an isolated protected area of evergreen forest located near Mariani in Jorhat district. The sanctuary is famous for the Hoolock gibbons.
This science centre cum planetarium provides the understanding of the solar system and recent discoveries of astrophysics.
The original temple dates back to 8th - 9th century CE. The present structure dates back to 1756 and was constructed by Ahom king Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha.

do.d: Multi-purpose stadium used for football and cricket games.

Junagadh.x: Junagadh is a historical city in Gujarat, in the west of India, on the Arabian Sea. The region of Junagadh became a district of Gujarat state in 1960. Junagadh used to be the state capital and is now a district administrative center.

see.n: The tombs of the 6th-8th Nawabs of Junagarh
see.d: The tombs of Nawabs from the Muslim Babi dynasty, known as maqbaras, stand just outside the train station.
The former Hall, where Junagadh' nawabs held their formal audiences, is now a museum, displaying textile works and different kind of weaponry (including swords, shields, guns).
One of the oldest zoos of India and the 4th largest. It was established in 1863 by Nawab Sahib Muhammad Mahabat Khan.
Must see. Built in 319 and rebuilt several times, Uparkot Fort was never restored and today is in a bad shape.
go to the top of this mosque to enjoy Junagadh's beauty.
Dating from before 500 CE, the caves are carved out of the rocky Uparkot Hill. The main hall is rich with decoration

do.d: Lake considered holy to Hindus.
Moti Baug is a park that includes the Botanical Garden and the campus of the Agricultural University of Junagadh
Famous place where Krishna ran and came from Mathura after which he was named as Ranchod Rai

Kakinada.x: Kakinada is a port city in central Andhra Pradesh, and a part of the mighty River Godavari Delta Region.

see.d: A religious site growing in popularity. This temple has great architectural features and sits on a hill top that offers a panoramic view of the surrounding fields and villages.
an important Siva temple located in Draksharama
is a large stretch of mangrove forests in India that is home to more than 120 bird species and a few endangered bird species. The sanctuary is very well maintained and lush green.
at Pithapuram (12 km)
in the Bay of Bengal and is around 7km east of Kakinada
on the banks of the Godavari River

do.d: Third largest stretch of mangrove forests in India with 24 mangrove tree species and more than 120 bird species, among others the critically endangered white-backed vulture and the long…

KGF.x: KGF (Kolar Gold Fields) is a town in the Kolar district of Karnataka.

Murshidabad.x: Murshidabad is a historic town in central West Bengal. It was the capital of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha during the Nawab rule. The last capital city of independent Bengal was named after Nawab Murshid Quli Khan, the Diwan of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

see.d: A palace of 1000 doors - 900 real and 100 fake. The palace was constructed by Duncan Macleod in 1837 on the orders of Sayyid Mubarak Ali Khan II, popularly known as Humayun Jah (reign: 1824…
The imambara is a congregation hall for Shia commemoration ceremonies, especially those associated with the remembrance of Muharram. It is situated just opposite the palace.
There is a Clock Tower between Hazarduari and Imambara. It was built by Sagar Mistri, assistant of Duncan Macleod. At the top of the tower is a big heavy sounding bell.
The barrel is 11′6″ long, with a girth in the middle of 7′9″. Made between the 12th and 14th centuries, it weighs 7657 kg. Look out for brass inlay lines and designs on the cannon.
The Chawk Mosque was built in 1767 by Munni Begum wife of Mir Jafar. The mosque has five domes and approached through an entrance flanked with minerates
The southern entrance of Quila Nizamat. The single arch entrance is surmounted by a Nawbat Khana, where royal instruments were played.

do.d: A park complete with toy train rides and a children's activity centre.

Rayalaseema.x: Rayalaseema, the western region of Andhra Pradesh, covers the undulating landscapes of the Deccan Plateau, in contrast to Coastal Andhra. The two regions are separated by the Eastern Ghats.

Kaithal.x: Kaithal is a city in Ambala Division of Haryana to the north of Delhi. The area is mostly farmland, growing rice, cotton and oil-seed. Kaithal's sights include the fort and the Shree Gyarah Rudri Mandir Temple.

see.d: Restored in 2016.
Purported to be the place where the only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was originally buried.
An Indus Valley Civilisation site which has yielded many plant remains.
The resting place of the 16th century Islamic saint.
A temple complex built in the 8th century and now partially in ruins. It has the oldest surviving temples made from brick north of Delhi.

do.d: Named after India's first prime minister, the lush green park has a dinosaur-themed playground, keeping kids entertained for hours.

Janjgir.x: Janjgir is the headquarters of Janjgir-Champa district in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh.

see.d: On the banks of the Mahanadi River, the temple is at its most liveliest during the Navratri Festival which takes place around October.
An 11th-century incomplete temple decorated with meticulous stone carvings. It is not used for prayer but is the most popular architectural sight in the city.
On the banks of the Hasdeo River.
A somewhat isolated temple surrounded by forest and hills.
One of the older temples around Janjgir, built in the 11th century.
According to local folklore, it was built by Laxman, the younger brother of Rama in the Hindu Ramayana epic.

do.d: A popular picnic spot surrounded by waterfalls.

Jiaganj.x: Jiaganj or Ziaganj, a heritage town in Murshidabad, is popularised by former playback singer Arijit Singh, who was born here.

Jangipur.x: Jangipur is a subdivision of the the Murshidabad district of West Bengal, covering the district's northern salient.

see.d: Ruins of a mosque built by Rafat Khan in 1495, during the reign of sultan Alauddin Hussain Shah.
Built in 1866 and later popularised by Satyajit Ray's film Jalsaghar, the neoclassical palace represents the heydays of the zamindar era, now in shambles.

Kalady.x: Kalady is a village on the right of Periyar (Poorna) river, in Ernakulam District of Kerala state, Southern India. This is an important pilgrimage center since it is the birthplace of Sri Adi Sankara, one of India's foremost philosopher saints who preached the monistic or 'Advaita' philosophy.

do.d: 22 km from Kalady.
10 km from Kalady.
An important Christanity pilgrimage center near Angamaly. It is believed that St. Thomas held his first sole prayer at this spot after being attacked by some tribes when he landed in…
Birth place of Adisankaracharya

Kalikiri.x: Kalikiri is a city in Andhra Pradesh, India

Kallooppara.x: Kallooppara is a village in Central Travancore in India. Kallooppara is on the eastern side of Thiruvalla. This pilgrim center is at the central part of the blue waters of the Manimala River.

Kalyani.x: Kalyani is a planned township in the Nadia district of West Bengal, India.

see.d: A char-chala temple with terracotta reliefs.

do.d: You can enjoy a day long picnic here. It is at the western end of Congress road that leads straight from Kalyani main station. Good for group picnics.
An event worth visiting.
A religious gathering.

Kanchipuram.x: Kanchipuram or Kancheepuram, formerly Conjeevaram, is a major pilgrimage site in northern Tamil Nadu. One of the most important spiritual centres of Hinduism, Kanchipuram has several medieval temples with spectacular architecture. It used to be the capital of the Pallava kingdom from the 4th to the 10th century, and was a centre of learning for all the major religions of South India.

see.d: The highest, largest and most impressive temple in town, spanning 40 acres and dating back to the Pallava period. Represents the earth form of the five form-element abodes of Lord Shiva.
Abode of Kamakshi (Parvati), consort of Shiva.

Kangra.x: Kangra is a town in Himachal Pradesh.

see.d: A popular pilgrimage.

Kanipakam.x: Kanipakam is a city in the Chittoor district of Rayalaseema.

Kolkata/South.x: South Kolkata is an important part of Kolkata city. It is less congested and more modern than the rest of the city. You will find more apartment blocks and green patches here.

see.d: The current residence of the descendants of the Bardhaman Raj family who shifted from Bardhaman to Alipore in 1955.
An auditorium shaped like a humongous conch-shell (শাঁখ shānkh), an example of mimetic or novelty architecture in India.
A Buddhist monastery.
This is a stately mansion. Once home of the British Viceroys, the Belvedere House is now the National Library. The oldest library in India with a huge collection, including some rarities.
A heritage building constructed in 1933.
A cultural hub of Kolkata, dedicated to Bengal's folk art and traditions, with a collection of textile practices, patachitra, old litho paintings, terracotta artefacts, ivory paintings,…

do.d: One of the four cinema halls that premiered Satyajit Ray's movie Pather Panchali. While the other halls were later shut down or became inactive, this one is still very active.
An iconic landmark in Kolkata, representing the elite (babu) Bengal with rich history and culture.
Founded in 1792, it is the second-oldest cricket club in the world after Marylebone Cricket Club. It arguably has the most picturesque cricket ground in Kolkata.
An open-air chess club under a busy flyover.
The venue of one of the biggest Durga Puja celebrations of South Kolkata. It also contains one of the tallest permanently-installed Durga statues of the city as well.

North 24 Parganas.x: North 24 Parganas, the most populous district of West Bengal, is also one of the state's most diverse districts, from the sprawling suburbs along the Hooghly River to the rural borderlands along the Ichamati River. The district borders Nadia to the north, Bangladesh to the east, Kolkata and South 24 Parganas to the south, and Hooghly and Howrah to the west.

Santiniketan.x: Santiniketan or Shantiniketan is a university town in central West Bengal, where students of different backgrounds study in open air, under the canopy of a tree. It is deeply associated with the Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore who developed the town. It is considered the manifestation of a utopian ideal of a community that became a crucible for intellectual and artistic ideas that were to have a decisive impact on 20th-century art, literature, poetry, music and architecture in South Asia.

see.d: Prayer place (under the chātim tree) of Maharshi Debendranath Tagore, father of Rabindranath Tagore.
College of fine arts and crafts, has a museum exhibiting sculptures, frescoes and murals and a library of art books.
Secondary school, is of particular interest, being an example of the traditional gurukula method of learning, although things have changed slightly.
The old buildings of the Visva-Bharati University, named after the Sinha zamindar family.
The prayer hall of the Visva-Bharati University. You have to exit the campus after visiting it.
The museum hall is called Bichitra. Constructed in Tagore's birth centenary year 1961.

do.d: Well-designed new addition with auditorium.
Festival of rains during August/September. Tagore was a poet of nature and some of his finest creations were about the rain.
Santiniketan's own style of Holi and it welcomes the arrival of spring. The students dance and sing their way through Amrakunja, followed by open-air variety programmes.
Anniversary of Brahmo Samaj celebrated on the 11 Magh (25 January), with prayers and songs at Chhatimtala.
The fair is held from 7-9 Poush (22/23-25 December). Tribal sports, folk songs and dances including songs by bauls, and itinerant singers, are a part of the fair and festivities.

Thane.x: Thane, formerly known as Thana, is a city in North Konkan, Maharashtra. Its biggest claim to fame is that the first railway line laid in India was from Bori Bunder to Thane station.

see.d: A historical landmark and historically a meetup place, still used as a meetup spot today.
The lake is home to a small island with a Shiv temple on it and also a Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Statue behind it.
It is one of the oldest temples in Thane. It was reconstructed by Chimajji Appa around 1750 AD.
This church is over 400 years old. St. John the Baptist Church is adjacent to St. John the Baptist High School and Junior College.
It is known for hosting the Sanskruti Arts Festival. Here one can also view thousands of Ganpati idols which are brought here for immersion on the final day of Ganeshotsav.

do.d: A sports stadium used mostly for training. Its main ground has been built for cricket with an in-built six-lane running track for athletes.
An excellent water recreation paradise which appeals to people belonging to all age groups. Spread over 11 acres.
A popular destination for picnicking families, known for its watersports, go-karting and other rides you'd find at amusement parks. The go-karting track isn't very good though.

Kalaburagi.x: Kalaburagi, previously known as Gulbarga, is a city in Northern Karnataka and the head quarters of the Kalaburagi District. Gulburga literally means "city of gardens" while Kaliburagi means "rocky land." It was once the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate and an important Sufi centre.

see.d: The fort dates back to the time of the Kakatiya dynasty. Later, the fort was turned into a mighty citadel under the Bahmani Sultanate.
Entry to the Gulbaraga Fort is through the north-west. The arched gateway is flanked by bastions and topped with battlements.
Bala Hissr is a dojon (heavily fortified central tower of a fort) located inside the Gulbaraga Fort. It was added by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, the founder of the Bahmani dynasty.
The mosque was built in 1367 by Bahmani Sultan Mohammed Shah I to commemorate the establishment of the capital in Gulbarga following the defeat Kapaya Nayaka of Warangal.
This small three domed mosque is located north of the Jami Masjid
A group of tombs of the Bahmani dynasty built during the 14th and 15th centuries. The tombs are examples of early Indo-Islamic architecture.

Kalka.x: Kalka is in Haryana, right up at the northeastern tip of the state on the border with Himachal Pradesh.

see.d: Mughal style garden with seven terraces. A museum is also located here.

Kanhangad.x: Kanhangad or Hosdurg is a city in the Kasaragod district of the Malabar region of Kerala, India.

see.d: Daily lecture sessions from 3:30PM to 4:30PM. Free food and accommodation to all visitors. Gardens, Bhajan Hall, Goshalas and Library.
An ashram in a forestlike silent place.
32 acres filled with medicinal plants, birds, insects, reptiles, amphibians, small animals and microorganisms. Popular with students of Botany and Zoology.
This temple is dedicated to Bhadrakali.
Underground caves, Meditation lessons.
Dedicated to Bhadrakali. During the temple festival in May/June and December/January, the ceremonious theyyam is performed here.

do.d: There is a Hanuman temple and Chirutheyi Cave here. Some other smaller caves are used for generating drinking water.

Kannapuram.x: Kannapuram is a small town in Kannur District, Malabar region, Kerala, India.

see.n: Ancient St. Martin de Pores Hospital
see.d: Beautiful building
One of the oldest mosques in India, built around AD.740
A very spacious hillock with several educational institution located on top of it. Famous Madayi Kavu Temple is situated here. There is a Jew' Pond on the rock.
with delightfully beautiful chira or pond.

do.d: Spectacular silent beaches. You must devout a lot of time as the area is quite big. Make sure you look at maps.google.com to familiarize this place before going.
An expanse of paddy fields can be enjoyed in the middle of the Ezhom village. You have to hurry, they are planning to build an airport in that place destroying all the landscape.
A refreshing walk in the 17 km long mangrove forest founded by Late. Kallan Pokkudan

Kannauj.x: Kannauj is a town on the Ganges in western Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: A bird sanctuary spread over two shallow lakes.
The museum has artefacts depicting the rules and common folk spanning the numerous dynasties that rules Kannauj over the millennia.

Kanchrapara.x: Kanchrapara is a railway town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal.

see.d: A historic airfield, used during World War II by British and American fighter jets. This area is used by Indian Air Force for special purposes.
One of the major workshops of Indian Railways. The workshop is open for public in the occasion of Vishwakarma Puja every year.

Kamptee.x: Kamptee is a cantonment town near Nagpur in India, near the confluence of the Kanhan, Pench and Kolar rivers.

Kanyakumari.x: Kanyakumari or Kanniyakumari is a town on the southernmost tip of the mainland of India, in the state of Tamil Nadu. It is also known as Cape Comorin.

see.d: The Rock has two Mandaps (halls); one belonging to Swami Vivekananda and the other belonging to a Holy Foot.
Thiruvalluvar Statue is dedicated to arguably the greatest Tamil poet, philosopher and saint, Thiruvalluvar.
Vivekanandapuram is the headquarters of the Vivekananda Kendra and the centre spreads over an area of 100 acres. There is a well stocked library within the premises. It is well connected.
Kanyakumari Devi Temple is the main reason for naming the place as Kannyakumari or the "Land of the unmarried girl". This temple is close to the beach.
On the shoreline of the Bay of Bengal, the 100-year-old Church of Our Lady of Ransom is dedicated to Mother Mary.
Tsunami Memorial is a monument recognizing the tragic events of the 2004 tsunami that claimed the lives of many Kanyakumari denizens. It is near the south shore.

do.d: Baywatch is a water theme amusement park at Sunset Point and is home to India's first wax museum.

Kannur.x: Kannur, formerly Cannanore, is a seaside city on the northern side of Kerala (Keralam), India. The Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary on the Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kannur (old name Cannanore) is known as Land of Looms and Lore because of the importance of the fabric industry and the concentration of Theyyam temple dance festivals.

see.d: Samples of pre-colonial art and architecture, Moplah Bay is nearby.
Built in 1505 by the Portuguese. Very good garden and view to the sea. Short footpath into the sea near Malsyafed office.
Riverside village.
The science park is a small facility containing displays of scientific and technological topics meant for school students.
2-km long footpath into the sea, fishing village. Beautiful garden and beach at Chalil village. Spectacular beach at Meenkunnu.
4-km-long beach with strong sand, the longest drive-in-beach in India. The village has about 24,000 people (2011). Another beach is available at Edakkad.

do.d: At Munderi Bird Sanctuary, near Varam. Many exotic birds can be spotted at Madayippara near Pashayangadi, 24 km.
Start walking from Caltex junction. Proceed to the collectorate and turn right to old bus stand.
You can start from Thazhe Chovva bus stop and go beyond Chovva Railway Station up the hill. There are paved roads all around the hill, up the hill and down the hill.
The hills and grounds around Sri Narayana College, Thottada are an ideal place for peaceful walking because there is very little traffic and open spaces are more in this region.
All coconut and areca nut. Beautiful bridge wide enough for a small car. Two more islands called AKG Island and Polthuruthy are nearby.

Kanpur.x: Kanpur is the largest city in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. It was known as Cawnpore in colonial times and is a major industrial centre of the Plains. The city is famous for its chemical (fertiliser, detergent), textile, and leather industries.

see.d: Biggest park in Kanpur City. This is the second best zoo in UP and third biggest zoo in India. Greenery and vastness of the zoo will capture any visitors attention.
A dam built across Ganges River near Old Kanpur. Contains Boating Club.
A cemetery of British militants near Civil Lines.
It is a Radha Krishna temple on Mainawati Marg, Bithoor Road. There is also a restaurant named Govinda's.
A museum established by Britishers. It exhibits old pictures, books, items and many other things.
A church established by Britishers. It exhibits old fountains, books, items and many other things.

do.d: Amusement park.
Amusement park.
Amusement park.
Play golf every morning by joining club.
Do boating at Mahatma Gandhi park.

Kappad.x: Kappad, or Kappakadavu locally, is famous as the beach near Calicut, India, where the Portuguese explorer Vasco Da Gama landed on May 20, 1498. A small stone monument there commemorates the landing with the inscription, "Vasco da Gama landed here, Kappakadavu, in the year 1498." It is one of the most important tourist places in Kerala, with a wide and beautiful beach.

Kappil.x: Kappil is a town in Kerala, India. It is on the border between Thiruvananthapuram District and Kollam Districts, and five kilometers from the famous Varkala beach.

Kapurthala.x: Kapurthala is a small town in the state of Punjab in India.

see.d: It is here Guru Nanak Sahib entered the Bein rivulet and stayed three days in the water.
Once home of Maharaja Jagatjit Singh, it is the most impressive building in the city, inspired by European palaces. Built in 1906. Today it houses a school.
A pilgrimage site for Indian classical musicians.
A temple, home of five small temples.
A replica of the Grand Mosque of Marrakech, commissioned by the last ruler of Kapurthala, Maharajah Jagatjit Singh to a French architect. Its construction was complete in 1930.

do.d: Man-made Wetland that subsumes the Kanjli Lake. It was created in 1870 by constructing the headworks across the perennial Bien River, a tributary of the Beas River to provide irrigation…

Karaikal.x: Karaikal district, part of the discontiguous union territory of Pondicherry, is a small enclave within Tamil Nadu. Karaikal and the other parts of Pondicherry are former French colonial territories in India. Karaikal district has a population of 200,000 and the main town is also called Karaikal.

see.d: one of the sixty three Nayanmars.
built Before Raja Raja cholan's era, now under ASI control and The temple was declared as a protected monument in 1971

see.n: Tirukadiyur Sri Amirthakadeswarer, Abirami Amman Temple
see.d: famous for 60th year marriage.
Thiruneelakandar yazhpanar serviced place.
built by Raja Raja cholan, now under ASI control.

Karjat.x: Karjat is a village in Maharastra. The river Ulhas originates in Karjat and flows westward. If you want to visit Karjat then the rainy season is best for you as Karjat has got such wonderful & beautiful waterfalls.

Karnal.x: Karnal is a city of 287,000 people (2011) in the National Capital Region (NCR) in Haryana. The city associates itself with Karna, the great donor and warrior and of one of the major characters of the Hindu epic Mahābhārata. The city has built a large statue in his honour.

see.d: Well maintained park with gardens and fountains. Travelers and local populace enjoy this park for picnics and leisurely strolls.
The Cantonment Church Tower is a church tower in Karnal city of Haryana, India. It stands near National Highway 1 of India.
There is a Dargah Nuri at village Newal on Karnal-Kunjpura road. This Dargah was built in memory of Hazrat Sufi Shah Alama Nur Mohd of Delhi, and is managed by Managing Committee, village…
A shrine of famous Sufi saint Baba Bu Ali Shah kalander. An enclosure with mosque and a reservoir with fountains.
A park
A tomb for the memory of a saint, Sayad Mohd AKA Miran Sahib, a saint who died in 899 AD.

Karnala Bird Sanctuary.x: Karnala Bird Sanctuary is a protected wildlife park in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, around 50 km from Mumbai. It is a major attraction to the visitors of Mumbai, Thane and other nearby towns. About 100,000 domestic tourists visit the sanctuary every year.

see.d: Apart from being a place of interest to the naturalist, Karnala is redolent of martial history. Karnala Fort, or the 'Funnel Hill' as it is called, stands 475 metres high.
Offers refuge to endangered birds like the peregrine falcon, king vulture and the crested serpent eagle.

Karur.x: Karur is a town of some 10,76,588 (2011 census) people in Central Tamil Nadu.

Karwar.x: Karwar is a city in Karnataka.

Kasaragod.x: Kasaragod is a city in Kasaragod District at the northern end of Malabar, Kerala in India.

see.d: 17th century fort.
Koto temple
ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute
Palaces of Kumbala Rajas. Admission is strictly restricted.
Famous Dargah, madrassa, women's college, seaside pond, cafeteria, garden and ancient mosque with exquisite wooden carvings and chandeliers.
Built by the Nileshwar Rajas.

do.d: Start from Karandakkatt junction near the new bus station. Turn east on Madhur road. After Choori and Kudla you reach Ramdas nagar and Vivek nagar.
Start from Press Club junction. Proceed to Kanhangad road, cross the Chandragiri river on the bridge and turn left after the Maruthi car showroom to Chemnad road.
Free Sattvic food, lecture sessions, very tastefully furnished meditation halls.
If you are looking for a short riverside walk inside the city, start down the hill from Muncipal Town Hall near the Government Guest House. Take the road on the right side of the Town Hall.
Beautiful views of the valley in lush green surroundings. Another added attraction is that this road is undiscovered by tourists. So you will get it all for yourself.

Kasauli.x: Kasauli is a small town in the state of Southern Himachal Pradesh located at an altitude of 1,927 m. The town is 77 km from Shimla and 70 km from Chandigarh.

see.d: Close to the bus stand, it was constructed by the British family that founded the town of Kasauli itself. It is a magnificent structure built in the shape of a cross.
A short walk up from Sunset point you will find a trail leading to another viewpoint Gilbert Hill. It's not very famous and very few travellers actually go there.
This historic Sikh gurudwara is located in Gharkhal bazaar on the main road towards Kasauli, having also lodging facilities.
This is the highest point in Kasauli, the place where Lord Hanuman is believed to have set his feet while on his way to look for the Sanjeevani buti (herb).
Situated about 1 km from the bus stand. Sunset point offers a magnificent view of the nearby hill regions. On a clear day, you may be able to view Chandigarh from up there.
At an altitude of 1,750 m, home to one of the major tourist attractions of the region, Lawrence School at Sanawar, founded by Sir Henry M.

do.d: Established in the 1820s, it is the oldest functioning producer of single malt whisky in all of Asia. It produces Lion Beer and Solan No. 1.

Kashmir Valley.x: The Kashmir Valley, or more poetically the Vale of Kashmir, is a large valley in the Himalayas and a part of Jammu and Kashmir in northern India.

Udupi.x: Most Indians know of Udupi not as a place, but as a category of restaurants that serve vegetarian food in the South Indian style. However, the town itself is not as well-known as its widespread cuisine. Still fewer know of its reputation as the location of a Krishna temple and a monastery established by the founder of one of the three main philosophical strains of present-day Hinduism.

see.d: A complex of temples and monasteries located near the Madhva Sarovara, or Madhvacharya's pond.
The unusual feature of Udupi's Krishna temple is that the statue faces west, and away from the devotees. To catch a glimpse of the deity, you need to make your way to Kanaka's window.
Madhva Sarovara is right next to the temple and is accessible from both inside and outside of it. has a "mantapa" or canopy at its centre, and the pond is often beautifully lit.
This is a temple dedicated to Parashurama, another incarnation of Vishnu, and according to legend, the creator of the landmass encompassing Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Kerala.
Right next to the Krishna temple is this temple dedicated to Shiva, to whom, according to legend, the moon (Chandra) prayed at this spot.
Visit Malpe beach where you can take fantastic pictures of the sunset in the background of St Mary's island. Nice clean beach, not inundated by tourists.

do.d: The trip takes you to Paradise Lagoon. Package includes all meals. It is not clear if packages of shorter duration are available - call to ask.
Whitewater rafting during monsoon season. Best time of visit is from July to late January. This rustic resort offers accommodations and activities.
Nice, relatively unknown beach. There is a lighthouse from which one can get a nice view. It is 22 km from Manipal, MIT.

Katihar.x: Katihar is a city in the north eastern part of the Indian state of Bihar. The city is somewhat close to the Nepalese border and is also the capital of the Katihar district.

see.d: One of the largest wetland and bird watching areas in the state. In 2019, it became Bihar's first conservation reserve.

Karmatanr.x: Karmatanr is a hamlet in the Santhal Parganas region of Jharkhand, associated with the later life of Bengali writer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

see.d: The residence of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in Karmatanr. His house is converted into a museum named "Vidyasagar Smriti", which contains a collection of his personal items, including the…

Kathgola.x: Kathgola is a small town north of Murshidabad, on the eastern bank of the Bhagirathi River, famous for the Kathgola Palace and the Jagat Seths.

see.d: Once the residence of the Dugar family, now a museum showcasing chandeliers, mirrors, furniture and other artefacts.
Though some of its early glory has been lost, the temple remains a major tourist attraction, chiefly because of the beautiful temple with an admirable work of stucco.
The Jagat Seths were a business family and were involved in the business of banking and money lending. The last Jagat Seth was Fateh Chand in 1911 and the title was no longer inherited.
About half a mile from the Hazarduari Palace is Jafarganj Cemetery. The Cemetery contains the tombs of the Nawab's Nazim, from Mir Jafar to Humayun Jah.
The palace was built by King Kirtichand Bahadur in 1865. Within the palace compound are temples: the Ramachandra temple and the Lakshmi-Narayana temple.
Nimak Haram Deorhi is the gateway to Mir Jafars palace. The palace lo longer exist but the entrance gate still stands.

Karnasuvarna.x: Karnasuvarna, an archaeological site in Murshidabad, covers the ruins of the former capital of Bengal under Shashanka.

see.d: Ruins of a Buddhist university.

Katra.x: Katra, also known as Katra Vaishno Devi, is a city in the Reasi district of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir administered by India. It is in the foothills of the Trikuta Mountains, about 42 km from the city of Jammu, and 35 km from Udhampur. The main attraction is the Maa Vaishno Devi temple.

see.d: The temple is home to a famous Hindu goddess. The temple is on a mountain, with a climb of 12 km to reach it. Following are the options to reach Maa Vaishno Devi temple from:.

Kavali.x: Kavali is a city in southern Andhra Pradesh in India.

do.d: one of famous temple in kavali geetamandram its located in railway station road kavali
don't miss seeing this temple

Kavalkinaru.x: Kavalkinaru is a beautiful village in the state of Tamil Nadu. Here, all religious people live together as one family. The village is a 45 Min drive from Thirunelveli and a 30 min drive from Nagercoil, and has a well connected road network and rail network.

Kayamkulam.x: Kayamkulam is a city and a municipality in district of the Indian state of Kerala. It is an ancient maritime trading centre and is almost equidistant from Alappuzha town and Kollam.

see.d: Palace and museum with exhibits about the Travancore kingdom. The palace was built during the 18th century by Travancore Maharaja Marthanda Varma.

Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary.x: The Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary, otherwise known as the Keoladeo Ghana National Park and originally called Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, is one of the world's most renowned bird feeding and breeding grounds. The park is over 29 km² and has 364 species of birds, including some threatened migratory birds from central Asia. It is also a major tourist centre with scores of ornithologists arriving here in the hibernal season.

see.d: The sanctuary is named after this 300-year-old Shiva temple, which is within the national park. It has a peaceful and serene atmosphere.

Keonjhar.x: Keonjhar, officially Kendujhar, is the district headquarter of Keonjhar District in Odisha (formerly Orissa).

see.d: The largest temple.
You may go by bus or by reservation. The bus fare is ₹20 from Anandpur and ₹110 from Bhubaneswar.
Dedicated to Lord Shiva.
waterfall
A small but very beautiful waterfall.
This is a beautiful waterfall on river Baitarani. Shaped like a tub (that is why named "kund", Oriya for tub), legend is that in during Mahabhatrath this was used by Bhima.

Khajuraho.x: Khajuraho, a small town in the Bundelkhand region of Eastern Madhya Pradesh, is famous for groups of Hindu and Jain temples. These temples are a UNESCO World Heritage Site for their beautiful and erotic rock carvings. Khajuraho has the Vindhya range of mountains as its beautiful backdrop.

see.d: This is the only granite temple in the Khajuraho group.
It is dedicated to Lord Chitragupta, the bookkeeper of the good and bad deeds.
Dedicated to the Goddess (devi), this is smaller and much more delicately proportioned temple and is home to some of the finest sculptures of Khajuraho.
This temple is decorated with a profusion of sculptures that are among the greatest masterpieces of Indian art.
The oldest and finest of the western group of temples, named after the ruler that built the temple.
A temple dedicated to Shiva, a huge 8ft Lingam adorns the temple.

do.d: Hatha Yoga classes can be followed in a traditional ashram lifestyle.

do.n: The Annual Dance Festival of Khajuraho
do.d: This festival happens from 1st Feb to 7th Feb. The same date goes for 2012 year also.
It is very small museum located exactly opposite to Shiv Sagar and nearby to Hotel Lakeside.
It is grand hall of more than 20 square size pillars with spectacular circular ceiling. You can spend some peaceful time here as it is one of the less crowded spots in Khajuraho.

Khammam.x: Khammam is in the Telangana state of Southern India. It gets its name from "stambhadri" which became "kambham" and the British Raj used to call the place "Khammam Mettu". The municipal corporation offers the small town experience with easy accessibility to modern amenities and entertainment.

see.d: This fort was built by Kakatiya rulers and was managed and extended by Nizam. It offers a nice view of Khammam town. There are steps constructed to facilitate climbing.
This temple of the "Narasimha Swami" deity is quite famous and also the reason for the name of "Khammam". On a hill top, it offers nice views especially in the evenings.

do.d: Danavaigudem Park is a picnic spot on the banks of Munneru river. You can check out the drinking water supply plant here, and you could also have a nice walk crossing the river on the dam,…
An evening at Tankbund near sequel resorts is a good pastime.This place is also used as walkers park in the morning.

Kinnigoli.x: Kinnigoli is a city of 17,000 people (2011) in Dakshina Kannada. It is a major suburb in the outskirts of Mangalore Tehsil (Mangalore Township) about 32 km from Mangalore City.

Lonavla.x: Lonavla or Lonavala is in the Pune district of Maharashtra, India.

see.d: A waterfall near the dam is a popular spot between Lonavla and I.N.S. Shivaji. Buses running on the I.N.S. Shivaji Road stop here.
Another point in the town of Lonavla is the wax museum founded by Sunil Kandaloor, a 37-year-old wax artist from Kerala.
Duke's Nose stands 12 km from Lonavla, clearly visible from the highway while driving towards Mumbai. This landmark in Khandala is popular with hikers.
A naval engineer training base.
Karla, near Lonavla, is a complex of cave shrines built by Buddhist monks around 3rd to 2nd century BC.
Lonavla Lake is surrounded by natural scenery, about 1.6 km from the town. The lake dries up during the winter months.

Khambhat.x: Khambhat (formerly Cambay) is in Gujarat, in Anand District at the inland end of the Gulf of Khambhat.

see.d: Visit this only after checking the tidal information for the seashore, as the gulf has pretty much silted up.
The 14th-century mosque is built with peculiar archaeological designs and structures borrowed from the Jain temples built at that time. It is one of the earliest mosques built in Gujarat.
which submerges on a high tide day.
for a picturesque view of palm trees adorning the road.
comprises shrines of all deities and a Nataraj artifact made out of stone.
A historical stepwell is located on an island in the lake. The lake is surrounded by a walkway and has children's play area.

Khopoli.x: Khopoli is an industrial town of 109,000 people (2011) in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, at the base of the Sahyadri mountains. Patalganga River flows through Khopoli. The city is called a city of waterfalls due to the number of waterfalls in the rainy season.

see.d: A mountain pass between Khopoli and Khandala on the crest of the Western Ghats.
India's largest theme park. It is split into six zones: Viva Europa, Americana, Jambo Africa, Asiana, Arabia and India. The park has three roller coasters: Nitro, Deep Space, and Gold Rush.
It has a Parashurama temple and Fire temple or Agni Mandir which was built in 1971.

Kavalande.x: Kavalande is a village near Nanjangud town in Mysore of Karnataka state, India.

Khurja.x: Khurja is a city (and a municipal board) in the Bulandshahr district in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. It is situated around 85 km from Delhi.

Katwa.x: Katwa is a town in the Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal, at the southern bank of the Ajay River.

see.d: A green park with scenic views of the Ajay River.
A temple complex near Sri Gauranga Bari. It consists of the principle Kali temple, along with the temples of Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu and Durga.
In January 1510, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu received diksha from his guru Keshab Bharati at the site of the current Sri Gauranga Bari Temple in Katwa.

Kharagpur.x: Kharagpur, the largest city in Southwest Bengal, is a major railway, industrial and academic hub of West Bengal.

see.d: A park and a picnic spot, frequented by people of all ages. It offers toy train rides within the park.
The temple was established in the early 20th century by some Bengali people working on the railways. It is famous for its Durga Puja and is very popular.
It’s a famous picnic spot in winter. There is a small deer park inside.
Built by the British for the Royal Indian Air Force during World War II. It was used to conduct raids against advancing Japanese in Burma and also for operations to transport aid to parts…
This is one of the oldest temples in the city, a Shiva temple, from which derives the name of Kharagpur.
An airbase used by the 317th Airlift Squadron of the US Air Force during World War II.

Khadikolvan.x: Khadikolvan is a historic and culturally significant village in the Sangameshwar Taluka of Ratnagiri district, South Konkan, Maharashtra, India. The village is known for its traditional temples, hot springs, and proximity to the famous Marleshwar Temple.

Khardaha.x: Khardaha or Khardah is a temple town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal. It is a pilgrimage site of the Vaishnava denomination of Hinduism.

see.d: A riverside at-chala temple complex built between late 18th century and early 19th century by zamindars Ramhari Biswas and Ramkrishna Biswas.
Nityananda Mahaprabhu chose this building for kirtan at the order of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.
A nine-pinnacled (navaratna) temple housing the idols of Jagannath, Chaitanya and Nityananda, three Mahaprabhus of Gaudiya Vaishnavism.
A holy place associated with Ramakrishna and Swami Vivekananda. It is decorated with colorful light, kadamba flower made of sola and birds during the Ras festival.
A temple established by Birbhadra Goswami, son of Nityananda Mahaprabhu. Birbhadra was born in 1457 at Kunjabati. At the time, Buddhism and Tantra were popular religions in Bengal.

Katni.x: Katni is a city in Eastern Madhya Pradesh.

see.d: A historic 19th-century fort that became a prominent hotspot during the 1857 Rebellion.
The geographic centre of modern post-partition India is marked by a replica of an Ashokan Pillar.
An over-100-ft waterfall surrounded by jungle.

Kodikunnu.x: Kodikunnu is in Central Kerala, India.

Kolhapur.x: Kolhapur is a city in the south west of Maharashtra. It has a population of around 619,000. It is situated on the banks of river Panchganga and is famous for the Mahalakshmi Temple as a pilgrimage city and is also famous for having 2 sites that are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, namely, the Panhala Fort and the Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary.

see.d: The puranas have listed 108 sites where Shakti (the goddess of power) is manifested.
Residence and a museum about memories of The Great Lokraja Shahuji Maharaj.
A gateway of higher education of international level to regional masses but surrounded by rich nature.
Temblai hill is a famous spot in Kolhapur. There is a temple of Goddess "Temlabai" and other small temple on this Hill.
Beautiful rainy hill station, lot of clouds and beautiful waterfall.
This site is revered by both Hindus and Jains. Devotees flock here to pay respect to the 28 feet tall marble statue of Bahubali and visit the temples of the 24 tirthankaras or saints.

do.d: It's very beautiful place, where various birds come every year.

Kolkata.x: Kolkata, formerly and still fondly called Calcutta, is the largest city in eastern India and the capital of the state of West Bengal. Once the capital of the British Raj till 1911, Kolkata is said to have been built on three villages along the Hooghly River, a distributary of the mighty Ganges. The city has seen tremendous growth during and after the partition of India in 1947.

Kollam.x: Kollam, previously Quilon, is a city in southern Kerala (Keralam), India. West and slightly north of the town some 5 km (3.1 mi) lies a beach, on the north end of which are various European colonial-era relics, including the ruins of a fort and a few churches. There are also some old colonial buildings scattered about the town.

see.d: Scenic place, with blue green stretches back water, coconut palms, back water cruise, house boats, Ayurvedic treatment centers.
Pilgrim centre, old trade route for merchants from either sides of western Ghats, famous for shrine of Lord Sastha, fine sculptures and mural paintings.
Famous for the mineral sand and place of Catholic saint Sister Alphonsa.
It is believed that old Kalayan royal family were ruled from this place, hence the name Kalayapuram.
Famous mosque and dome of martyrs, a unique pilgrimage center. Old military station of Kayamkulam Rajas.
Erstwhile capital of Elayadathu Swarupam, a ruling family. Famous for Kath Kali (a dance drama).

do.d: Vijeesh runs canoe tours which are an excellent way to explore Munroe Island. You get to go places that the house boats can't and will literally be going through the village and get to see…
A fishing harbour.

Konkan.x: Konkan is a coastal region of Western India, consisting of the coastal areas of Maharashtra and Goa. Some definitions include the entire western coast of India, from Gujarat to Kerala.

Koraput.x: Koraput is a city in the state of Odisha, near the borders of Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh states. It has enchanting hills, verdant forests, winding streams, exotic wildlife and a rich tribal way of life.

see.d: River Kolab forms three waterfalls of about 9 m (30 feet). The last 5 km of the road from Khandaguda is 'kutcha road' (dirt track). There is a rest house near the falls.
The highest & largest mountain peak of Odisha.
The Machkunda River forms the 175 m high waterfalls, with facilities for generation of hydroelectricity at Machkunda Power Station.
Cave shrine of Lord Shiva on the banks of the River Shabari. The place name literally means 'hidden God'. Odisha Tourism has a lodge at Gupteswar.
It is across the Kolab River, 900 m (3,000 feet) above sea level with facilities for hydroelectricity generation.
It is the highest broad gauge tunnel in India. It is on the Visakhapatnam-Kirandaul line.

do.d: "Parab" is a tribal festival organised by Unicef every year from 16 to 18 November, where one can find different tribal cultures at one place who demonstrate their dance and art forms.
Ratha yatra is the main annual event.

Koravangala.x: Koravangala in Karnataka has the Buchishwara temple built by Hoyasalas. The temple is in good condition.

Korba.x: Korba is a city in Chhattisgarh. Korba is the power capital of Chhattisgarh. The district comes under Bilaspur division and is inhabited mainly by tribals including the protected tribe Korwas (Pahadi Korwa).

see.d: It was constructed by Raja Pratwidev First. Archeologists consider it as one of the strongest natural fort.

Kota.x: Kota is in the Hadoti region of Rajasthan, which is in the southeastern side of the state. The Chambal river flows through the town, because of which the city of Kota is unlike the arid climate prevalent in the state.

see.d: (25 km) An archeological area with ancient Indian stone carvings.
This garden stretches along the banks of the river Chambal. It houses a pond with rare gharial and crocodiles, which can be crossed via a teetering suspension bridge.
(50 km) - One of 3 wildlife sanctuaries in Rajasthan with large tracts of forests and a variety of wildlife
Palace and fort complex often visited by tourists.
It is a Hanuman temple at few km from Chambal garden.
Right in the center of the artificial Kishore Sagar tank (Lake Pichola) stands the beautiful red sandstone monument, Jagmandir.

do.d: Take a boat safari on the Chambal river and observe crocodiles at close quarters. It starts from Chambal Garden.
A beautiful and ancient temple dedicated to Lord Shiva constructed more than 200 feet below ground level. The temple is constantly showered by a natural waterfall.
