Kottayam.x: Kottayam is a city in Kerala, south India. It is near to Kochi. The city is India's first 100% literate city, also known as Letter Capital of Kerala, due to headquarters of more than a dozen publishing houses and newspaper companies as well as several famous colleges and university.

see.d: A hill station with large hills around high. Beautiful hillocks named Mankunnu, Kudayathoormala, Thonippara and Poonchira are here.
Important pilgrimage centre for Hindus and Muslims.
Famous for having an ancient Shiva temple. Wall paintings in the temple are thousands of years old.
The place is famous for its bird sanctuary, house boats, backwaters, canals and the bungalow of Henry Baker (now run as part of a resort managed by the Taj group of hotels).
St. Mary's Shrine here attracts people of all faiths. Various kinds of offerings are made here devotees.
This is a small white sand island. It gets its name from the brilliant reflection of moonlight from the sand.

do.d: Kottayam also has an annual food and flower show. These events are quite popular and are worth a visit, if you are in town when it happens.
Lots of boat races with traditional boats of different sizes - around 50 types - in the months of July, August and September during Onam.
Local food, children's park and hiking options, very green surroundings.
Trekking facility in snowy mountains above sea level, organized by Peruvanthanam village council. You can see the Alappuzha sea on clear days.

Kovalam.x: Kovalam, a fishing village in southern Kerala, is famous for its beaches, among the most pristine in India. About 17 km (11 mi) from Thiruvananthapuram, Kovalam is extremely popular among westerners due to shallow waters and low tidal waves. This article also covers the nearby Vizhinjam, which is best known for the international seaport and the tidal power station.

see.d: The granite cave encloses a one-celled shrine with a loose sculpture of Vinadhara Dakshinamurthi.
Head down to the harbour at sunset for some spectacular shots of the area with the seaside mosque in the background.
The old lighthouse, at the southern beach is a local landmark, for being one of the oldest lighthouses of Kerala, guiding ships to the nearby Vizhnjam port.
The Tamil-style koil is known for the tall Gangadhareshwara sculpture, the tallest Shiva sculpture in Kerala.
The largest and southernmost beach of Kovalam, known for its 35-m-high lighthouse which towers over it atop Kurumkal hillock. Most of the foreigners stay on Lighthouse Beach.
The second-largest beach of Kovala, and it takes less than five minutes to walk from Lighthouse Beach. It is named for the topless European women who used to throng there.

Kovilpatti.x: Kovilpatti is a city in Thoothukudi District of Tamil Nadu. It's nicknamed as "City of Matches".

Kongu Nadu.x: Kongu Nadu in western Tamil Nadu consists of 10 districts, namely Coimbatore, Dharmapuri, Dindigul, Erode, Karur, Krishnagiri, Namakkal, Nilgiris, Salem and Tiruppur.

Kotdwar.x: Kotdwar aka Kotdwara is a town in Garhwal district of Uttarakhand. It is one of the main gateways to Uttarakhand.

see.d: Kanva Ashram is an important historical and archaeological place.
Approximately 2 km from Kotdwar, this renowned temple is dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Large numbers visit year round.

Konanur.x: Konanur (Paduvalamarahalli) is a village near Nanjangud in Mysore district of Karnataka state in India. .

Kotkapura.x: Kotkapura is a city of 92,000 people (2011) in Punjab (India). It is the largest city in the Faridkot District. Kot Kapura has also been called the 'City of White Gold' due to its cotton market, which was once the largest cotton market in Asia.

Kondapalli.x: Kondapalli is a village 16 km (9.9 mi) west of Vijayawada in central Andhra Pradesh. The village is known for making toys with light-weight wood sourced from the hill forest.

see.d: Built on a hill, this fort features an impressive three-storeyed rock tower and was witness to the glory of many dynasties. This fort was built by King Krishna Deva Raya.
Spread over an area of , the forest is home to several carnivores like leopards, wild dogs, and a few others like, jackals, wolves and civet cats.

Kolaghat.x: Kolaghat is a popular picnic spot in the Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal, along the Rupnarayan River.

Kishangarh.x: Kishangarh is a town near Ajmer, in central Rajasthan. Founded in 1609-1611 by Kishan Singh, the town is home to the Rathore clan of the Rajputs, as well as the marble slurry dumping yard turned into a snow-themed park.

see.d: This former waste disposal site for marble processing byproducts is now a snow-themed park by the Kishangarh Marble Association (KMA).

Kozhikode.x: Kozhikode, formerly Calicut, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Kerala (Keralam) after Kochi.

see.d: Near Town Hall.
Vallikkattu Kavu is a 27-acre sacred grove in a swamp at Edakkara near Elathur. You can see monkeys, peacocks, wild boars, porcupines, wild hens, different kinds of butterflies and many…
A sprawling park with many beautiful statues. Entrance is free but the gate is open only after 2P.M There are many historic buildings like the Commonwealth Company near the park.
7 mangrove species, 29 mangrove associates and fauna ranging from protozoa to Otter. It is also a congenial habitat for 20 types of water birds.
Tribal Research Station maintained by the government.
Ideal place for students of Indian history.

do.d: Start from Fathima Hospital, take the narrow line opposite the hospital. Walk past Kerala NGO Union, Lakshmi Printers and Oyisca Youth Centre.
Start from the bus stand. Take the road opposite to it, walk past Markaz Mosque and Samastha centre. Turn right towards More Supermarket, Planetarium and Science Centre.
Take a bus to Govindapuram from Mananchira pond. Walk up the hill to Central School. Very good view of the entire city and Arabian Sea.
Take a bus to Kovoor on Medical College route. Ask for the Iringadan Pally road. Walk in the company of spectacularly spacious expanse of paddy fields hidden between four main roads of the…
Start from the Nalam Gate, and as soon as you cross the railway gate the road forks into three. Choose the third one, walk past Caffe Coffee Day and Gateway Hotel.

Kuchesar.x: Kuchesar is a village near Bulandshahr in western Uttar Pradesh.

Kufri.x: Kufri is a tiny hill station in Southern Himachal Pradesh, India.

see.d: Established in 1992, it is home to native species such as the great Himalayan snow leopard, and varieties of the musk deer.
One can hike through thick forest around Kufri to the Mahasu Peak- the highest peak in Kufri.
The Indira Tourist Park is near the Himalayan Nature Park and provides panoramic view of the locations around.

Kumaranalloor.x: Kumaranalloor is a city in Kerala in India.

see.d: The place of Goddess Madurai Meenakshi at Kumaranalloor, Kottayam. Considered one of the most important Devi temples among the 108 durgalayas (devi temples) in Kerala.

Kumbakonam.x: Kumbakonam is a town in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. The town is popular for the Betal Leaf Combination (Vettrilai Cheeval) and for the thick-strong coffee. Nearby Darasuram is famous for Airavatesvara Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

see.d: A temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, where he is worshipped as Adi Kumbeswarar.
A temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and a . Built during the Chola era, the temple is named after Lord Indra's elephant Airavata.
Named after the famous temple in Varanasi, this temple worships Lord Shiva as Vishvanatha and his consort Parvati as Vishalakshi.

Kumta.x: Kumta small town on western coastal part of Karnatka, India. The best time to visit is in the month of October to January. Kumta is known for its betelnut, cashew, coconut, banana cultivation and fisheries.

see.d: 15th century fort.

Kundapur.x: Kundapur is a popular town in Udupi district of Karavali refion of Karnataka, India, known for its unique dialect of Kannada and great food.

see.d: A very lovely beach with white sands and absolute privacy.
A rather unusual beach with the Arabian Sea and the Suparnika River flowing in parallel. The river makes a U-turn and goes westward to join the sea after a journey of nearly more than .

see.n: Sri Hatti yangadi siddi vinayaka temple

do.d: It is a popular local traditional theatrical art.

Kunnamkulam.x: Kunnamkulam is a city in India. It is 24 km from Thrissur, on Kozhikode highway. It can also reached from Guruvayoor, which is 8 km away.

Kurnool.x: Kurnool is a city in Rayalaseema, Andhra Pradesh state. It is home to the 16th-century Konda Reddy Fort.

see.d: Located in the outskirts of Kurnool (5 km).
Remains of old Kurnool Fort.
Ghat on the banks of Hundri River in Kurnool Town, named after the former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh state.
Small park with igneous rock formations and a cave museum. This site was used in the making of several Indian movies.
The premises of the temple are very pleasant.
There are many temples along the banks of the Tungabhadra River. This river is heavily polluted. It flows through three states: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

Kurukshetra.x: Kurukshetra is a holy city in Haryana.

see.d: The centre has around 10 male and 10 female mugger crocodiles which you can see up close. The guides are very knowledgeable.
The memoirs of Al Beruni, called 'Kitab-ul-Hind' mentions this sacred water tank. The water tank is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
The Sikh Gurus visited Kurukshetra from time to time. Pilgrims go to the Pundits of their area and sign in their register after taking a bath.
A pilgrimage site, where the Bhagavad Gita was spoken.
Situated at a distance of 3 km from Kurukshetra Railway Station on Pehowa Road, Sannihit Sarovar is believed to be the permanent abode of Lord Vishnu.

Krishnanagar.x: Krishnanagar, formerly Krishnagar, is a city in the Nadia district of West Bengal. At the bank of the Jalangi River, Krishnanagar is an important centre for culture and literature.

see.d: The Bangalore-based Deccan Herald has written, "“We have clay dolls, toys and even clay sculptures in different parts of India.
It stands out for its distinctive architecture. There are 27 oil paintings describing the life of Jesus Christ. There also is a Protestant church in the same compound.
The Rajbari has a beautiful Durga temple in the courtyard. Jhulan Mela is celebrated in July-August, Baro Dol is held 12 days after Dol Purnima in March-April.

Koyilandy.x: Koyilandy or Quilandy/Quilandi is a town in Kozhikode District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, India. The population is 72,000 (2011).

see.d: Vasco de Gama arrived in India at this place. There is a memorial and a park in this beautiful beach.
This 480-metre bridge is the longest bridge in Kozhikode district. Completed in 2015, it has 13 spans. The surroundings are lush, green and very photogenic.
With beautiful pond.
Non-profit organization intervening in health, education, relief work and rural development. Established in 1915 by Swamy Nirmalananda of Kolkata.

do.d: Beautiful views of the river and valleys down. Fogs are common.

Lakhimpur.x: Lakhimpur is a district of Upper Assam and one of the greenest districts in India. It is home to many historical temples and is full of local culture-- seeing a mixture of Aryan and non-Aryan culture. Namghars, temples fill this place.

see.d: Padumani Than is a visit worthy temple in Lakhimpur, which has a story to tell. Not far away from North Lakhimpur town, it can be reached via the national highway that passes through…
Basudev Than is located in the Dhakuakhana sub-division. Established in the 17th century, this place is worth visiting for history lovers, religion lovers and anyone interested in visiting…
This is a home for many migratory birds, thus making it worth visiting by nature enthusiasts and also for those who simply want to enjoy nature, or have a picnic nearby.
see lord Ganesha on a ship! Shiva Mandir and Durga Mandir are also worth visiting.

Lakkundi.x: Lakkundi is a small village in Karnataka state in India. It is a historical place This small village has many temples with magnificent architecture of Kalyani Chalukya, Hoysala period.

Krishnarajanagara.x: Krishnarajanagara or K.R. Nagar is a riverside paddyfield township in Mysore District in Karnataka, India. It was home to 36,000 people in 2011.

see.d: The old railway station of the British period is not forgotten because that area is still known by the same name. The buildings have all fallen down and only a few walls remain.
Beautiful paddyfields and cute little railway station where only slow trains stop six times a day.
Beautiful village surrounded by Krishnarajasagara Lake
Garden, fountains, restaurants, lodges and much more.
Four beautiful mosques and dargahs in the middle of the paddy field. Very photogenic.
Beautiful picnic spot on the bank of Kaveri River. Picnic benches are provided with provision of entire joint families to spread their picnic baskets.

do.d: Sanyasi Park is surrounded by nine templesː Lakshminarayana Temple, Chandramouleshwara Temple, Srikrishna Temple, Raghavendra Temple, Kalikamba temple, Sathyanarayana temple, Ayyappa…
Begins from the riverside temple of Arkanadha. Ends at Kandenahalli bridge near the Railway Station.
The cement benches in front of the railway station is a popular hangout of older people. Parking is not allowed in this area. This is a very small circular shaped garden.
Beautiful trekking tracks on all the four sides of the temple.
Begin from the KSRTC bus station. Head east on C.M.Road. After two kilometers, turn left on Kandenahalli Bridge. After 2 km, turn left and reach the old railway station area.

Upper Assam.x: Upper Assam is a region in Assam, India. This consists of Biswanath, Golaghat, Lakihmpur, Majuli, Jorhat, Sivasagar, Dhemaji, Dibrugarh, Charaideo and Tinsukia districts.

Lalitpur (India).x: Lalitpur is a city in the Northern Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: The sanctuary has a variety of fauna including many kinds of deer, monkeys and leopards.
A group of 31 Jain temples, built between the 8th century and the 17th century. The most famous of the temples is the Shantinath temple, which was built before 862.

Latur.x: Latur is a town in central Maharashtra.

see.d: Twelve caves featuring sculptures of a Jain tirthankara, Narasimha, Shiva-Parvati, Kartikeya and Ravana.

Lakhisarai.x: Lakhisarai or Luckeesarai is a pilgrimage site in the Magadha region of Bihar.

see.d: A temple complex with the Shiva temple at the centre, surrounded by three Parvati temples.
A nearby temple where devotees come here to get their children's head shaved after their wishes are fulfilled. The mountain waterfalls and ponds here enhance the beauty.

Lohgad.x: Lohgad, literally meaning the iron fort, is a hill fort located in the Pune District in South Maharashtra near the hill-station of Lonavala. The fort stands on the edge of the Sahyadri Range and lies between the Indrayani and Pavana river basins. Because of its strategic location the Lohagad Fort is often considered as the strongest and most famous Deccan forts.

see.d: Winding stairways and paths with sharp hairpin bends lead through the top of the fort. The path passes through four massive gateways consisting of thick spiked wooden doors.
This is the first of the four gateways of Lohagad Fort. It was constructed by Nana Fadnavis in 1789.
The second gate, Narayan Darwaja, was also an addition of Nana Fadnavis in 1789. It is approached by a narrow flight of stairs and is strategically very important.
Hanuman Darwaza is the third gateway of the Lohagad Fort. This is probably an older gateway and is said to have been constructed by Aurangzeb in the late 17th century.
Maha Darwaza, literally meaning the grand gate, is the last and final gate of the Lohagad Fort.
It is located slightly north-west of the Maha Darwaza. It is the largest standing structure in the fort complex. The square structure is topped with a dome.

Loutulim.x: Loutulim is a town in South Goa.

Lucknow.x: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh and one of the most populous cities in northern India. Lucknow, the "City of the Nawabs", thrives along the banks of Gomti River. The city along with the rest of Awadh fell to the British during the colonial era.

see.d: A massive church and school. Lot of celebrations take place around Christmas time and is packed.
A must see place with great architecture. It was built in 1896 and named after British Indian colonial administrator Sir Auckland Colvin.
The Oxford and Cambridge of India author/poet Shibli Naumani. For more details see the book Ul Farangi Mahal by Francis Robinson
One of the three crocodilian breeding centres in India, including the freshwater gharials (Gavialis gangeticus), one of the 3 native species of crocodilians in India.
Beautiful Gomti river-side and monumental structures view for fun with family and friends. Best time to visit is 4–6PM, during the sunset.
The remains of an 18th-century house built in the English baroque style. The house was shelled during its involvement in the Siege of Lucknow in 1857, and only a few towers and external…

do.d: A popular hangout place among the locals, the public park has two rows of large elephant statues as its main attraction.
They offer some great heritage walks including a culinary walk.
A building in the shape of Saturn.
A small park on the side of a noisy congested road in Lucknow. A statue of the Buddha gives the park its name. The park features fun rides and boating facilities.

do.n: Nawab Wajid Ali Shah Prani Udyan
do.d: The central zoo of Lucknow, established in 1921, and popularly known as Banarasi Bagh (बनारसी बाग़ Banārasī Bāġ) or Chidiya Ghar (चिड़ियाघर Ciṛiyāghar).

Ludhiana.x: Ludhiana is an important industrial town in Punjab. It lies on the banks of the Sutlej river. It is also one of the cities on the historic Grand Trunk Road that formed an important trade route.

see.d: A park with well-landscaped lawns and flowers, fountains, picnic area and a children's playground. Dog friendly.

see.n: Museum of Rural History of Punjab

Machilipatnam.x: Machilipatnam or Masulipatnam is a port city in central Andhra Pradesh. It is a small fishing town; has a carpet-weaving industry; other products include rice, oilseed, and scientific instruments. The town is a railway terminus and an educational center.

Madhupur.x: Madhupur is a city in Deoghar district of Jharkhand. It is considered a health resort because the water there is said to cure digestion ailments. Historically, many notable people, particularly from Bengal, owned a house in Madhupur.

Madurai.x: Madurai, formerly Madura, is the third-largest city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is on the banks of the river Vaigai and has been a major settlement for two millennia. It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

see.d: This museum houses Gandhi's bloodstained dhoti and little else by way of artifacts.
Boating, swimming, and Fishing in Melamadai Vandiyur Lake provides some more ever green memories. These are only allowed if the Madurai Corporation authority provides permission.
These rocky hills are home to various Jain and Hindu monuments dating between the 2nd-century BCE and the 12th-century CE.
The remains of the palace of the 17th-century ruler Thirumalai Nayak who contributed extensively to the Meenakshi Temple.
The name Goripalayam comes from the Persian word Gor which means Grave. This area is called as Goripalayam because the Graves of the two famous saints of Islam and rulers of Madurai Hazrat…
This traditional mosque (masjid) is at the heart of Madurai city, within 500 m of the Periyar (Central) bus stand and within 1 km south east of the Madurai Railway Junction.

Mahad.x: Mahad is a town in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, India. So many people have this wrong impression that it is famous for Ganesh Temple which is one of the 8 Ashtavinayak temples, but there are two cities having similar names. The town which comes in Raigad district is not a place among the Ashtavinayak.

see.d: Samadhi (tomb) of the great Maratha warrior, Shivaji Maharaj, who brought the Hindu revolution to Islamic India.
A group of 30 Buddhist caves.

Maithon.x: Maithon is a town in northern Jharkhand. The Barakar River east of Maithon forms the border with West Bengal at Asansol.

see.d: A popular weekend picnic spot and its main attraction is the Barakar River. The Maithon Dam has created a massive reservoir with hills in the backdrop.
The temple complex at the Barakar River consists of four temples, with the fourth being the oldest. It is amongst the oldest rekha-deul temples in West Bengal.
A 500-year-old centre of Shakti worship. Legend has it that human sacrifices were offered at Kalyaneshwari in the remote past.
one of the four dams of DVC with a huge water reservoir. The Reservoir has small islands. These islands can be reached by row boats. The most famous island is Sabuj Dwip.

North Bengal.x: North Bengal is the northern region of West Bengal, known for its mountains and its wide range of animals and forests. It houses many ancient landmarks of historical significance. It is well-known for its tea gardens, especially Darjeeling Tea.

Maihar.x: Maihar is a city of 40,000 people (2011) in Maihar district, Madhya Pradesh. Maihar is a religious pilgrim place for Hindus. Having the temple of Goddess Sharda, the deity of learning.

Mahanandi.x: Mahanandi is a picturesque village surrounded by thick forests east of the Nallamala Hills near Nandyal, Kurnool District, Andhra Pradesh, India. Within 15 km of Mahanandi, there are nine Nandi shrines known as Nava Nandis. Mahanandi is one of the Nava Nandis.

Mahe (India).x: Mahe is a little beach town enclave of Pondicherry near Kannur. It is effectively a town that is Kerala, but retains some French influence as it was a colony of France.

see.d: Very photogenic steps
1893 French-built lighthouse. It stands atop the Moopenkunnu Hillock, located on the south side of the Mayyazhi River meeting the Arabian Sea.
The Mahe River Side Walkway is a picturesque 2 km scenic pathway stretching along the banks of the Mahe River to the Arabian Sea. It features well-lit paths and bencheshes.
Tagore Park is a scenic and peaceful waterfront park situated right at the estuary where the Mahé River meets the Arabian Sea.It serves as a recreational hub and offers great sunset views.
A shrine dedicated to Saint Teresa of Ávila. Consecrated in 1736, it is recognized as one of India’s oldest shrines.

do.d: There are a small number of government offices that occupy colonial buildings. Visitors are not entertained.

Madhubani.x: Madhubani, in the Mithila region of Bihar, is known for its unique art.

Mahoba.x: Mahoba is a historic city of 95,000 people (2011) in the Northern Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is known for the 9th-century granite Sun temple built in Pratihara style, and for the 24 rock-cut Jain tirthankara images on Gokhar hill.

see.d: A Shiva temple made from granite and built in a Khajuraho-like architectural style.
An artificial lake made by the Chandela kings in the 11th century.

Mahudi.x: Mahudi is in North Gujarat.It is a pilgrimage centre of Jains and other communities visiting the temple of Jain deity, Ghantakarna Mahavir and Padmaprabhu Jain Temple.

see.d: It was established by Jain monk, Buddhisagar Suri in 1917 CE. There is an inscription in the Brahmi script of it. The 22-inch marble idol of Padmaprabh is a central deity.
is dedicated to Krishna and is kuldevta of Khadayata community.
is another Jain temple nearby in shape of pyramid.

Mahabubnagar.x: Mahabubnagar is a town southwest of Hyderabad, in West Telangana.

see.d: One of the famous tourist attractions of West Telangana with a Veerabadhra temple called Koil Konda. Every year, there is a celebration (Jathara) held by nearby villagers.
A hilltop shrine of Lord Venkateshwara. There is also a temple of Lord Shiva. The ideal time to visit this temple is at the time of Jaathara, celebrated every year during January or…

Maibang.x: Maibang or Maibong, a town on the hills of Assam, is an ancient capital of the Dimasa kingdom. The Stone House near the river is the only intact relic of the kingdom there, though other artifacts have been discovered during construction and are on display.

Lothal.x: Lothal in Central Gujarat is one of India's Indus Valley sites.

see.d: The site is well-planned and divided into distinct zones: the Acropolis (Upper Town), Raised on a high platform to protect against floods, housing civic rulers with paved baths and…
Located adjacent to the ruins, this ASI-maintained museum houses around 800 artifacts recovered from the site.
An ambitious world-class heritage complex being developed adjacent to the site to highlight India's maritime history. Phase I is under construction.

Malabar.x: Malabar, a region of the Indian state of Kerala (Keralam), is historically famous as a major spice trade centre, and was the port of first call for Vasco da Gama on his maiden voyage on the Cape Route.

Malayalam phrasebook.x: Malayalam belongs to the Dravidian language family, and is mostly spoken in Southern India in the state of Kerala (Keralam), as well as the Lakshadweep Islands. Around 36 million people use this language, which is one of the 22 official languages of India. A Malayalam speaker is called a "Malayali".

Malda.x: Malda, officially English Bazar, is a city in the northern West Bengal.

see.d: The Museum dates back to 1937 and is under the West Bengal Directorate of Archaeology. The museum was started as a place of exhibits of artifacts found in the Malda district.
Nimasarai Minar is a collapsed tower with projected spikes. Namasarai literally means halfway inn. It lies halfway between Gour and Pandua in Malda.
There is a restaurant inside. You can also take a boat riding.
Visit this pious Hindu Kali temple.
You can visit the place during the evening, experience the chanting and the prayer.

do.d: Read newspapers and local classifieds for free. The library is open from noon-7PM.

Mallapally.x: Mallappally is a taluk in the Pathanamthitta district of Kerala state in Southern India. The major populations are Christianity and Hinduism. The land derived its name from mallan (meaning "strong people") and pally (meaning "place"), and is believed to have a community of brave aggressive people from the nearby communities.

Mandya.x: The city of Mandya is the headquarters of the Mandya district in Karnataka. It is an agricultural town. Sugarcane is the main produce.

see.d: Beautiful gopura.
Good place for trekking.
12 feet high deity.
Magnificent temple with an ornate gate near a lake
Remains of Tippu's Fort, Tippu's Summer Palace, Sangam, Tippu's shrine (Gumbaz), the famous Ranganatha Temple and other places of historical importance
Trolley ride to reach the small hill with a power station

do.d: This little town is an ideal place to spend two days eating very good food and walking in the gardens around.

Mangalore.x: Mangalore officially Mangaluru, in the coastal Karavali region of Karnataka, is a blend of new and old. With the increasing influx of students from various states of India and different parts of the world, Mangalore has become a "melting pot" of cultures, given the various communities that make up the social framework of Mangalore: the Tuluvas, the Brahmins, the Konkani Catholics, the Bearys, the Devangs and many others. It is the fifth-most populous city in Karnataka with a population of about half a million in 2011.

Mannargudi.x: Mannargudi is a municipality in Thiruvarur district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is also known as Raja Mannargudi, Dakshina Dwaraka (Dwaraka of the South) or Mannai.

Mapusa.x: Mapusa is a town in North Goa. It is the main commercial centre in North Goa (outside of Panjim, which is larger). It is basically a town for locals, who throng to it for their shopping and commercial requirements.

Marathwada.x: Marathwada is a region of Maharashtra, India. It is usually a drought-affected area. But nowadays the situation is changing.

Margao.x: Margao is the second largest city in the Indian state of Goa, 33 km from the state capital Panaji. It is Goa's cultural and commercial capital, and is close to the central coast. The long white-sand beach stretch was rated by an early-1970s UNDP study as potentially one of the ten best beaches in the world.

see.d: perched between two luxury hotels

Mathura.x: Mathura is a Hindu holy city at the banks of the Yamuna River, in the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is a famous pilgrimage city as Krishna was believed to born here as an avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu.

see.d: Biggest and richest in Asia for Mathura and Gandhar sculpture. It has one of the finest collection of archaeological interest.
In memory of the victory of Basantar (1971 war).
Built in 1814, it is the main temple in the town. During the festive days of Holi, Janmashthami and Diwali, it is decorated on a grandiose scale.
The temple carving and painting are a major attraction.
Constructed by great saints Baba Jai Gurudev. It resembles the Taj Mahal, built with white marble. It is a unique temple in that you are prohibited from donating if you are a non-vegetarian.
Built by Abo-inNabir-Khan in 1661 AD, the mosque has 4 lofty minarets, with bright colored plaster mosaic of which a few panels still exist.

do.d: Boating in the holy river Yamuna and a visit to Durvasa Rishi Temple, which is on the other side of the river.
A play act based on the story of Ram. In this act the main play is Ram Barat. In Ram Barat you can see fun sword fighting and other fighting styles in the Akhadas.

Mayapur.x: Mayapur is a small town in the Nadia district of West Bengal and the headquarters of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), which is known informally around the world as the Hare Krishnas.

see.d: A cowshed which takes care of more than 200 cows and bulls. A veterinary doctor performs timely health checks.
The magnificent memorial shrine of Srila Prabhupada is the largest of its kind in India.

do.d: Attend the early morning Mangal Arati held in the Sri Radha Madhav Temple. Summer and winter timings may differ by a couple of minutes, however, the reception near the main gate and inside…

Mayiladuthurai.x: Mayiladuthurai is a town in Tamil Nadu.

see.d: One of the famous temples where Perumal is in reclining poisture. One of 108 Divya Desams.
A temple that is supposedly the place where Lord Shiva protected Markandeya from Yama (Lord of Death) when he was about to take the boy's life.

Mancherial.x: Mancherial is a city and headquarters of the Mancherial district of the Indian state of Telangana state in Southern India. Mancherial is located on the banks of Godavari River. It is 253 kilometres (157 mi) north-east of the state capital, Hyderabad.

see.d: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple
Constructed on river Godavari
Satyanarayana Swamy, Ayyappa temples
Covers and is famous for Blackbuck, otherwise known as Indian antelope.

Malampuzha.x: Malampuzha is a village in Palakkad district of Kerala, India. The water reservoir, Malampuzha Dam and gardens near to the dam are major attractions of Malampuzha.

Malbazar.x: Malbazar is a small city that serves as a hub for travellers visiting the Dooars of West Bengal.

see.d: A well-maintained park on the northwest edge of the city.

Manjeshwar.x: Manjeshwar is in Malabar, in Kerala, India.

see.d: Kote Shree Veeranjaneya Temple, Ikkeri fort, Hanujman Nagar, Arikkady.
Four majestic churches and a school on spacious grounds.
Scenic campus
Prayers in Tulu language

pilgrim centre for the Madhawa Brahmins

do.d: Slow trains are called Passenger Trains in India. They are very cheap and punctual.
If you want a pleasant walk in Manjeshwar town with an opportunity to photograph many period building, you can start from the back side of Manjehwar railway station.

Maynaguri.x: Maynaguri is a twin of Jalpaiguri, across the Teesta River in North Bengal.

see.d: Border crossing with northern Bangladesh.
The massive 126 feet high and 120 feet wide Shiva temple, built in the 9th century, was actually destroyed and rebuilt many times.
One of the oldest temples in Jalpaiguri district. The main temple was built around 320–600, by a feudal chief of the Gupta Empire.
This temple is dedicated to the Divine Mother Shakti as Kamakshi Amman.
Sekkizhar built this temple 1,000 years ago.

do.d: A Chola-era reservoir built by Rajendra Chola I.

Meerut.x: Meerut is a city in the west of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is 60 km from the capital Delhi.

see.n: Basilica of Our Lady of Graces
see.d: Basilica of Our Lady of Graces, also known as Churches among the Churches, is dedicated to Virgin Mary.
An edifice built by Nawab Mohammad Ishak Khan in memory of his father Nawab Mustafa Khan Shefta, a poet and critic.
The oldest garrison church in Northern India, built from 1819 to 1822. Its cemetery contains graves of David Ochterlony and Rollo Gillespie.

Mettupalayam.x: Mettupalayam is a municipality of Coimbatore district. It is situated at the foothills of Nilgiris on the bank river Bhavani on Coimbatore-Guddalor State Highways. Mettupalayam Municipality was formed in the year 1948.

Mirzapur.x: Mirzapur is a city in the heart of North India, nearly 650 km between Delhi and Kolkata and also equidistant from Prayagraj and Varanasi. Located in the state of Uttar Pradesh, Mirzapur has a population of a little over 230,000 (2011 census) and is renowned for its famous carpet and brassware industry. It is a city with several spots around it including many hills such as Rajdari, Devdari, Lakhaniyadari, and Windom fall range and Sirshi.

see.d: See the scenic beauty of The Vindhyas from this temple.
See the old stone carving at Pakka Ghat and Budhenaath Temple
It is one of its own kind.The stone carving of the tower will make mesmerize you. The clock is very old and is one of the sisters in Big Ben family.

see.n: Vindham, Sirsi and other water falls
see.d: There are various water falls surrounding the city.Vindham, Sirsi, Sidhnath ki dari being most famous in them

do.d: Mirzapur is situated at the bank of Ganges. You can enjoy a serene evening at one of the Ganges Gahts.

Mithur.x: Mithur is a small village in the "Idkidu grama" area of Bantwal Taluk, which is in the Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka, a state in India.

Moga.x: Moga is a city in Punjab, India.

see.d: Literally meaning the "park of the martyrs", on 25 June 1989 26 RSS volunteers were gunned down by terrorists.

Mohali.x: Mohali, officially Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar (SAS Nagar), is a satellite city of Chandigarh and is also an administrative district of the Punjab, state in the Plains of India.

see.d: Fateh Burj is the tallest victory tower (minaret) in India, at 328 feet tall.

Mondaikadu.x: Mondaikadu (Mandaikadu) is a city in Tamil Nadu in India.

see.d: Mondaikadu is situated on the coast, northeast of Colachel port. It is connected with Nagercoil and Thiruvananthapuram by a motorable road.

do.d: It is 16 km from Nagercoil and 32 km from Kanniyakumari. The seashore looks majestic and rugged because of the huge beautiful rocks jutting out into the sea.

Moradabad.x: Moradabad is a city in Uttar Pradesh in India. It is situated at a distance of about 167 km from Delhi and is also known as Brass City or Pital Nagri.

do.d: Enjoy the delicacies of Moradabad, such as biryani, kebabs, paya, etc. at Gulshan-e-Karim. Get good tea right in front of Gulshan-e-Karim.

Mormugao.x: Mormugao is a region of South Goa on a peninsula at the mouth of the Zuari River.

see.n: Religious Museum of The Blessed Joseph Vaz

Mumbai.x: Mumbai, formerly known as Bombay, is the largest city in western India and the capital of the state of Maharashtra. A cosmopolitan metropolis, Mumbai was built on seven islands on the Konkan coastline which over time were joined to form the island city of Bombay. The island was in turn joined with the neighbouring island of Salsette to form "Greater Bombay".

do.d: organised by two architects, these walks take you around various historic and architecturally significant areas of the city.
(Jan) The musical festival is organised by Maharashtra Tourism (MTDC) annually at Banganga Tank on Malabar Hill.
(March) Organised by Maharashtra Tourism, the festival of music and dance at Elephanta Caves has in the past seen performances by renowned artists like Alarmel Valli, Sanjeev Abhyankar, and…
The arts and crafts festival is held in the last week of Jan or first week of Feb annually in the historic precinct of Kala ghoda in Mumbai.

Munger.x: Munger is a town in Bihar, once called Monghyr in colonial times. Historically, Munger is known for its manufacturing of iron articles such as firearms and swords. It is the ancient city of Mahabharata legend Karna, the eldest son of Kunti and Sun Lord.

see.d: A wildlife sanctuary in Bihar. There several hot springs located here as well as several places of interest nearby. This area of grasslands and forest contains a mixture of flora.
Chandika Sthan is a Hindu temple, one of the fifty one Shakti Peethas, places of worship consecrated to the goddess Shakti.
This is a pond. The temple is positioned in the middle of the pond. A famous for the tourist attractions. One of the best place for one day travelers.
This is a temple of Shiva (Shivling). The temple is positioned in the middle of the pond. And is very beautiful. Macchli talav also has a garden.
This fort; built on rocky hills, traces its history from about 1330 AD. It contains several important monuments.
It has a very interesting ancient story about this place, which belongs in the period of Ramayana.

Murdeshwar.x: Murdeshwar is a town in Uttara Kannada region in southern India. The name "Murdeshwar" means Shiva or Eeshwara.

Northwest Odisha.x: Northwest Odisha covers the north-western region of Odisha.

Midnapore.x: Midnapore or Medinipur, a town in southwestern West Bengal on the Kangsabati River, is the headquarters of Paschim Medinipur district.

One of the rare churches in Southwest Bengal.

Mehsana.x: Mehsana is in North Gujarat, India. The city does not have many places of interest for tourists but can serve as a base for excursions.

see.d: A stepwell built in 1674 CE during the reign of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. It has unique twin wells. It is now polluted and in poor condition. The oldest surviving monument of the city.
Built in 1904 by Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda State, it was used as the government office and later as the court until 2017. It has three floors and 130 rooms.
Redeveloped in 2019, the lake has a children's playground, yoga centre, food court, jogging tracks and boating facilities.
A garden.
A garden with children play area. It has another small stepwell known as Badiyashi Vav built by Shah Virchand Jadavji.
Built in 1971, a large Jain temple dedicated Simandhar Swami, a Jain Tirthankara. A fine example of Maru-Gurjara temple.

do.d: Enjoy at game and adventure zone for kids and adults. Indoor games, arcade, bowling, trampoline, zipline and many more. A multicuisine restaurant Multi Menu is also there.

do.n: Swimming Pool at Atal Sports Centre
do.d: Enjoy an hour of swimming pool in summer heat. Confirm timing.
Enjoy a cricket match at local stadium during tournament seasons.
Watch Bollywood or Gujarati film. Online Ticket booking available.
Enjoy a movie with popcorn

Morbi.x: Morbi a city and a municipality in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, India.

see.d: The former residence of the queen and later converted into the Willingdon Secretariat in 1936. After independence of India, it served as the local government office.
The city gate was inaugurated in 1925 by Sir George Lloyd, the then Governor of Bombay. It was then known as Lloyd Gate. Subsequently post independence, it was renamed as Nehru Gate.
The new two-storey palace has beautiful Art Deco architecture and Art Nouveau interiors.
The town square and the main market of Morbi. You may see several shops of watchmakers who are at work here. It is approached by series of three gates.
Green Tower is built in European architecture and is topped with a three-floored cast iron frame structure with a dome.
The old bridge known as Pada Pul because the large bulls are erected on the entry to the bridge. It is a 700-m long masonry arch bridge.

Mira-Bhayandar.x: Mira-Bhayandar is a suburb north of Mumbai, in the North Konkan region of western Maharashtra.

see.d: Built in 1613 this is one of the oldest churches of North Konkan.
Built-in 1544, ten years after the Bombay-Bassein coastal tracts were ceded by the Sultan of Cambay, Bahadur Shah, to Portugal by the Treaty of Bassein. The present structure is not old.
A fort in a dilapidated condition and is declared 'endangered'.
Medieval fort built by the Portuguese between the 16th and 18th centuries. It was later occupied by the Maratha Empire and then served as the district headquarters of the East India…
Mainly known for its fishing activities. It is not very clean. An early morning visit can provide an insight into the life of the local fishing community.

do.d: A nature retreat of about , and a unified campus run by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The retreat is developed in the memory of the RSS founder Dr. Keshav Baliram Hegdewar.

Mehsi.x: Mehsi is an important industrial and commercial town in East Champaran district, Bihar. The Government of Bihar identifies the Mehsi Shell Button Cluster as one of the district's existing manufacturing clusters. Mehsi is nationally known for its pearl button industry, described by the Government of Bihar as the only industry of its kind in India.

see.d: A Sufi Islamic shrine visited by locals of different faiths for prayers and community gatherings.

Motihari.x: Motihari, a commercial centre in northwestern Bihar, is famous for Mahatma Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha movement, as well as the birthplace of George Orwell, the author of dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

see.d: An oxbow lake.
A museum dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha movement, with wide collection of relics and photographs.

Musiri.x: Musiri is a city in Chola Nadu.

Muzaffarpur.x: Muzaffarpur is a city in the Mithila region of Bihar, India. It is known as the "lychee capital" of the country. It is one of the oldest and most important commercial and educational centres of Bihar.

see.d: About 40 km from Muzaffarpur, Ambara Chowk is situated in Saraiya Block on the Muzaffarpur - Rewa road.
Baba Garibnath Temple situated in the center of the Muzaffarpur town is undoubtedly one of the most famous "Lord Shiva" temples.
This temple, which is almost 300 years old, attracts many Tantric Hindus, especially on Navratri.
This is a temple with an interesting back story. It is said that in 1303, in a village called Turki, a big idol of Lord Chaturbhuj was found.
About 40 km from Muzaffarpur is the famous temple, Hathilwa-Mathh dedicated to Radha-Krishna. While the Badi Masjid at Company Bagh and the Gurudwara at Ramna are definitely worth a visit.
This great temple is an icon of faith, worship and belief on Ma. It is situated on the south coast of "Gandak" river.

Mysore.x: Mysore or Mysuru is the second-most populous city of the state of Karnataka after Bangalore. It was the capital of the Wodeyar dynasty and is considered to be the cultural capital of Karnataka. Mysore is among the cleanest and best-planned cities in India.

see.d: The zoo was established under royal patronage in 1892, making it one of the oldest in the world.
Definitely the number one attraction in Mysore. Intricately carved rosewood doors and ceilings, some with inlaid ivory work, marble figurines, collections of caskets, paintings of the…
It was built by Maharani Regent Vani Vilasa Sannidhana, wife of Chamaraja Wodeyar, for her daughter Jayalakshami.
Another palace that has been turned into a five-star hotel. It served as a royal summer residence for the Viceroy of India in the late 19th and early 19th century.
A beautiful temple of Goddess Chamundeshwari (or Chamundi Devi) with marvellous architecture. Wheelchair access is available.
One of the old temples of Mysore, Jwalamukhi Tirupparasunadri, is also an incarnation of Goddess Parasakthi, the creator.

do.n: Climb the Chamundi Hills by steps
do.d: Only for fitness freaks. Start early in the morning to get a good view of the city as it rises from slumber while getting good exercise at the same time.
Yoga classes, meditation practice and free food. Many beautiful buildings set in a lush green surroundings. The Mysore facility is the south India headquarters of the Brahmakumaris.
Take any bus going to Bangalore side and get down at St. Philomena's college. You can walk inside the Banni Mantap grounds which is extremely spacious.
Hardinge Circle has been renovated with marble seats on three sides and cement seats on three sides.
The state festival of Karnataka, carried over from when it was celebrated by the Wodeyars in grand style.

Nabadwip.x: Nabadwip is a pilgrimage site in the Nadia district of West Bengal and the birthplace of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, a Vaishnava saint.

see.d: Poramatala is one of the sacred religious centers in Nabadwip. A colossal banyan tree covers this place like an umbrella.
This is the centered temple in Poramatala. Goddess Porama is actually the deity of Maa Kali (some scholars also refer to Maa Saraswati, so her name is also known as "Maa Nil Saraswati".).
Bhabatarini Mata Temple is located on the left side of Maa Porama Mandir. The architecture of the temple is Char-Chala on a Bengali Dalan type architecture with Pankha style artistry.
Bhabataran Shiv temple is situated on the right side of Maa Porama temple. This temple is a rare octagonal peak temple in architecture.
It is the birth place of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, located in the north side of Nabadwip. It is a Naba-Ratna type temple architecture.
In the Narahari Dham Asram, a beautiful 60 ft tall Chaitanya Mahaprabhu statue situated. It is the highest Mahaprabhu statue in the world.

do.d: Matches, exhibitions and varied events.
Take a walk.

Nadiad.x: Nadiad is a city in the Kheda district of Gujarat, in Western India.

Nagaur.x: Nagaur is a city of 111,000 people (2012) in Rajasthan, India. It is the capital of Nagaur District. Another name for it is the village "Khatwan".

see.d: Nagaur Fort is one of the finest examples of Rajput-Mughal architecture. Built in the early 12th century and repeatedly altered over subsequent centuries, it witnessed many battles.
A 500-year-old fort in the middle of the Thar Desert; turned into a hotel furnished with modern facilities.
Also known as the Charbhuja temple; 400 years old; evidence how total surrender helps attain godly qualities; how deep faith converts poison to 'Amrit'.
10th-century Jain temples are rich with historical attraction. Jain Vishva Bharti University is a centre of Jainism; a school of thought; a centre of spirituality & purification; and a…

Nagercoil.x: Nagercoil is a city in Tamil Nadu, India. It's the southernmost city on the Indian mainland.

see.d: The namesake of Nagercoil, with Nagaraja as its principal deity. The devout traditionally offer milk to this "King of Snakes".
St. Francis Xavier Cathedral, in the Kottar locality, was established in 1600 AD. St.Francis Xavier stayed here and the church was built on the land which St.

do.d: very scenic village with rivers and hills all around

Nagpur.x: Nagpur, a major city in the Indian state of Maharashtra, is famous for its Nagpur oranges and also widely considered to be the city at the center of India. Nagpur is also the state's winter capital, as the winter session of the Maharashtra Legislature is held here, along with some administrative functions.

see.d: A heritage building from the British era. It is in the heart of city and pride of Nagpur.
A unique marvel of engineering that exists in a very few places of the world. The double lines crossing from the north to the south and those from east to west form a square shape and is…
The botanical garden of Nagpur with several rare plant species. The garden is also popular among bird enthusiasts.
The winter residence of the Governor of Maharashtra.
The seat of the winter sessions of the Maharashtra Legislature. It was built in 1912 to house the government of the Central Provinces of Berar, as Nagpur was its capital.
A monument marking the geographical centre of colonial India. It was built by British during the 1907 Great Trigonometrical Survey of India in Nagpur.

do.d: Central India's largest spiritual - cultural tourism park which houses all Hindu deities under one roof.
A lake created by a dam.
Khindsi is a picturesque lake 40 km from Nagpur city and is famous for the natural beauty and water-sports.
Evening host for food in exotic lake view.
Migratory birds can be seen in winters.

Nalanda.x: Nalanda is the site of a famous Buddhist university or mahāvihāra in the Indian state of Bihar. The university complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

see.d: Remains of the stupa has terraces and smaller stupas. ₹600 for foreigners. The ticket office is just across the road from the entrance. Mind the beggars and shopkeepers.
The museum houses a significant collection of Pala and Mauryan statues. The six air conditioned (!) rooms show off stone and metal statues that were found during the excavations of Nalanda…
Xuanzang, also known as Hiuen Tsang, was a 7th-century Chinese Buddhist monk and teacher.

Nalgonda.x: Nalgonda is a city in Telangana state in Southern India.

see.d: A good place to hang out. This holds the record of largest rock built dam in the world.

Nalhati.x: Nalhati is a remote village in the central region of West Bengal and one of the 51 Shakti Pithas. It is believed that Parvati's throat (Nal) fell here, when Vishnu severed her body, with chakra, to stop Shiva from the Tandav nritya. That is why the name Nalateshwari is used as a synonym for the Peeth.

Vasai-Virar.x: Vasai-Virar, formerly Bassein or Baçaim, is a city in the North Konkan region of Maharashtra. Previously a Portuguese colony, Vasai-Virar is known for its fort and scenic coastlines. It is often compared to and referred to as Mini Goa due to its resemblance to the sun and sand capital of India.

see.d: A fort on an island off Vasai-Virar. The main entrance of the fort faces approximately north. The solid stone doorway is adorned with pictures of tigers and elephants.
Very powerful Hindu temple founded by great astrologer, Param Pujya Dadasaheb Hate of Vasai.
A Shiva temple in a strangely beautiful garden. In the dome, a trident (triśul) stands impressively against the horizon.
A migration corridor between Sanjay Gandhi National Park and Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary. It rises to about above sea level, making it a very popular destination for trekkers.
Portuguese mariners exploring the north Konkan Coast discovered the Arab Sultanate of Khambhat or Cambay, built or renovated or expanded the fort in the early 1400s and attacked it in a…

Nagda.x: Nagda is in Malwa, near Ujjain.

see.d: This temple with a huge garden is one of the major attractions of Nagda. The well-maintained garden provides a peaceful and relaxing aura to the area.

Naina Devi.x: Naina Devi is a town and a municipal council in Bilaspur district in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh.

see.d: The temple of Shri Naina Devi Ji is situated on a hilltop in the Bilaspur District. There are several mythologies associated with the temple's creation.

Naihati.x: Naihati is a major city in northern North 24 Parganas, West Bengal.

see.d: A football stadium hosting games of Calcutta Football League, Naihati Gold Cup and I-League.
The most noteworthy religious spot in the city. It came up in 1923, when a young Brahmin built a tall Kali idol after visiting Nabadwip and witnessing the grandeur of the idols there.

see.n: Rishi Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Residence and Museum
see.d: The birthplace of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, a Bengali novelist known for composing the patriotic song Vande Mātaraṁ.
A former rail bridge over the Hooghly River.

Nadia.x: Nadia, a district of West Bengal, is known for the two Hindu pilgrimage sites Mayapur and Nabadwip, and also the royal heritage of Krishnanagar. Once known as the "Oxford of Bengal", Nadia has made many contributions to Indian philosophy, such as the Navya-Nyaya system of logic and is the birthplace of the Vaishnava saint Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

Nagapattinam.x: Nagapattinam is a port town in Tamil Nadu.

Narmada Valley.x: The Narmada Valley of Madhya Pradesh consists of the fertile river valley sandwiched by the Vindhya and Satpura mountains.

Namakkal.x: Namakkal is a small historic city in Tamil Nadu in Southern India.

see.d: A rock fort built by the Madurai Nayak dynasty during the 17th century.
A temple dedicated to the Hindu got Hanuman built in the classical Tamil architectural style.
8th century rock-cut temple constructed by the Pandyas with Vishnu's Narasimha ("man-lion") avatar presiding as the main deity.

Nanded.x: Nanded is a city in Marathwada.

Nandyal.x: Nandyal is a town in Andhra Pradesh.

Nanjangud.x: Nanjangud is a town in Karnataka State.

see.d: One of the biggest Hindu (Shiva) temples in India. Shiva took poison to save the universe and the poison got stuck in his throat turning it blue.
This is the oldest railway bridge of India. The pillars are built of limestone in neo-Gothic style. There are three new bridges on both sides of the old bridge.
The riverside Sathyanarayana temple and bathing steps are located on the opposite side of the main Nanjundeshwara temple complex.

do.d: You can take a train to this little railway station surrounded by lush greenery and cute little farmer huts.
Thandavapura has Agni Nethramma Temple with sylvan backgrounds suitable for a picnic. This temple has three other temples nearby. Ask for the temple near the highschool.
River Kapila is very suitable for fishing and riverside walking. Very scenic surroundings
There are two Punjabi Dhabas with private huts on the highway. They serve meat dishes of north Indian flavour.
Paddyfields, canals, temples and riverside huts. Women wash their colorful clothes from the canal steps.

Nashik.x: Nashik is a city in the state of Maharashtra with a population of about 2.3 million people (2023). This is an ancient holy city, also known as the Wine Capital of India, part of the Mumbai - Pune - Nashik so-called "golden triangle of Maharashtra", a city of pilgrimage for many Hindus, important for Hindu rituals for the afterlife offerings, and also famous for the Hindu pilgrimage Kumbh Mela, gathering hundreds of millions of pilgrims every 12 years.

see.d: Located near Trambakeshwar, it is well known for waterfalls during monsoon season.
Artillery centre - Deolali camp's, Lahawit market is for shopping, Deolali South has Khandoba temple hill, golf course, sun rise & set point as well.
Texture painting by needle on canvas.
A bird sanctuary near Niphad. It is a mesmerizing place for nature and bird lovers alike.
A sacred place where five sacred Banyan trees are still present. All important temples are in this area.
Excellent views, landscape, musical fountain, video songs, Buddha smaarak, water park. located on foot of Pandav Caves hill.

do.d: Features go karting, artificial rock climbing, rope activities, archery and various other activities.

Navi Mumbai.x: Navi Mumbai, formerly New Bombay, is a planned city near Mumbai, India. It was founded in 1971, as a satellite township to take the pressure off the core city. Although it has been only partially successful in this sense, this has been changing with many IT and ITES industries setting up shop here.

see.d: India's longest sea bridge, also known as Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link (MTHL). Named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, the bridge connects Sewri in Mumbai to Nhava Sheva in…
Mango Garden, a must-visit place for couples and children. It is a small garden for almost all age group people.
Boating, toy train and lot of fun, bhel puri, pani puri, gola etc.
A very cool place on hilltop. People prefer to come here for morning and evening walk. Youngsters come here to have fun and just chill out.
Lots of temples for doing Pooja and meditiation, and a good trek.
Has beautiful views of Navi Mumbai

do.d: The project of Central Park is to make a public park with Navi Mumbai's ethos reflected into the future. It is under construction but is open to public.
The cricket stadium in the Navi Mumbai area hosts several international cricket matches and domestic championships such as the Mumbai T20 league and Times Cricket Shield.

Nellore.x: Nellore (also called Simhapuri in previous centuries) is one of the more prominent cities in southern Andhra Pradesh in Southern India.

see.d: The most famous temple on the southern bank of the River Pennar, the Galigopuram of the temple is 29 m high and has seven gold Kalasams.
Located on the banks of the Swarnala Cheruvu lake. The shrine is dedicated to twelve martyrs (Sufi saints/warriors) who are believed to have sacrificed their lives in battle centuries ago.

Nizamabad.x: Nizamabad is a city in the state of Telangana in India. The city falls in the category of a developing town with many famous monuments which are in ruins. This district is famous for the Tramaric crop and the large number of monkeys within its limits.

see.d: Built in 10th century by the Rashtrakuta dynasty.

Nilambur.x: Nilambur is a town in Kerala in India.

see.d: Famous for its plendor of the wooded jungle surrounding it. This cascade is a spectacle of unrivalled grandeur.
This is one of the four central forest nurseries in Kerala and was established during the year 1997, at Valluvassery by the Kerala Forest Department.
The plantation is named in honor of H.V. Conolly, the then Collector of Malabar during the British rule who was instrumental in planting teak in the entire Nilambur area with the help of…
Noted specially for its rich rain forests. The wooden rest house built here by the British offers a panoramic view of the elephants and deer grazing in the forest near by .
The world's first Teak Museum. In the Teak Museum, a visitor can have a first hand information on all aspects of teak.
Vavul Mala peak is in this mountain and it is at an altitude of 2339m. The hill ranges are accessible by foot from Muthappanpuzha, near Anakkampoyil.

do.d: Land of potters and pottery works. The village has become famous for the presence of its potters.
Cholanaicker tribals in Valamthode, can be reached through the Areekode-Mukkam road, a half hour journey from Nedumkayam, or 27 km from Nilambur).
Koviliakams-Residences of the local Rajas are famous structures. Nilambur town is also famous for housing a cluster of kovilakoms, the residences of the local rajas or rulers of earlier…

Noida.x: Noida, an abbreviation of New Okhla Industrial Development Authority, is a satellite city of Delhi just across the state line in Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: A hub for films and television in India. It has been the location for many Bollywood and Indian films.
Established in January 2010, it is India's first private museum of art exhibiting modern and contemporary artworks.
An art gallery where you can see and buy art pieces by various new as well as established talented artists. Open to public, this gallery has interesting exhibitions every month.

see.n: Rashtriya Dalit Prerna Sthal and Green Garden
see.d: The green expanse along the banks of river Yamuna includes a mini-museum called the Rashtriya Dalit Smarak (National Dalit Memorial).
The garden that hosts the annual Noida Flower Show.

do.d: A haven for over 300 bird species, especially waterbirds.
There are three sections within the modern theme park complex: a water park, an amusement park and a go-karting track.

Nurpur.x: Nurpur is in Himachal Pradesh, India.

see.d: An ancient temple 25 km away.
A complex of 25 temples carved out of one rock
temple and monastery.
is old fort built by Tomar Rajputs, was destroyed in earth quake, only ruins remain...

Oachira.x: Oachira (or Ochira) is a coastal town in Kerala in India.

see.d: A Hindu pilgrimage centre for worshipers of Mata Amritanandamayi Devi.
Very old temple.
Visit during festival times which is March and April.
Of archaeological interest.

Nandura.x: Nandura is in Vidarbha region of Maharashtra.

Nileshwaram.x: Nileshwaram or Neeleswaram/Nileshwar is a small town in Kasaragod District in Malabar, Kerala, India.

see.d: Spectacular view of the valley below with the railway track, railway station and passing trains.
frequented by Sabarimala pilgrims.
ideal place for people with a socialist bend of mind.
The mysterious lamps of the kanhiram tree are lit on Tuesdays and Fridays after 10PM.
Beautiful pond and temple

do.d: The autorikshaw drivers of Nileshwar are in a class of their own because they have formed a small group of anti-mainstream-communist socialist group and worship rebel leader…
Two footpaths of 800 m each length into the sea are available at Cheruvathur Fishing harbour.
Azhithala, a picnicker's delight, is the place where River Tejaswani mouths the Arabian Sea.
The boat station is 2 km from market junction on the highway. Boat services are available to Payyanur, Valyaparmba and Trikaripur.
Start from the railway station. Head South. Turn left to the hill on the eastern side. You reach the highway where there is a view point.

New Delhi.x: New Delhi, the capital of the Republic of India and the seat of its three branches of government, is characterised by its wide boulevards, roundabouts (traffic circles), colonial mansions and government buildings. A part of the larger National Capital Territory of Delhi (NCT), New Delhi is not just a political centre; it's a thriving melting pot where people from different parts of India work and live. Connaught Place and Khan Market are popular shopping centres and the nearby Paharganj area has many inexpensive hotels.

Naukuchiatal.x: Naukuchiatal is one of the most beautiful hill stations in Kumaon in Uttarakhand. It is known for its breathtaking smoky mountains, 175-foot-deep Nine Corners Lake, paragliding and other adventure activities.

see.d: A small village (Gaon) near Pandeygaon on Naukuchiatal Road, surrounded by lush-green smoky mountains and home to hundreds of bird species, this village is about 800 m away from Bhaktidham…
Jungaliagaon is a small village 7500 ft above sea level, popular amongst nature and paragliding lovers and home to more than 200 bird species.
An interconnected group of seven freshwater lakes in the Lower Himalayan Range.
52-foot-high statue of the monkey god Hanuman. It has a Vaishno Devi gufa (cave) as well. A separate Durga temple allows elderly folks to have darshan without going through the gufa.

Naya Raipur.x: Naya Raipur, also known as Atal Nagar, Nava Raipur or New Raipur, is the planned capital of Chhattisgarh, near Raipur.

do.n: Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium
do.d: Opened in 2008, it is the second largest cricket stadium in India and the fourth largest cricket stadium in the world by seating capacity.
A beautiful coverleaf interchange as you zip around Raipur and Naya Raipur.

Nilgiris.x: The Nilgiris are a range of mountains in western Tamil Nadu. It is a part of the Western Ghats, connecting the mountain range to the Eastern Ghats.

Narmadapuram.x: Narmadapuram, formerly Hoshangabad, is a city in the Narmada Valley of Madhya Pradesh, along the Narmada River.

see.d: Famous for its prehistoric rock paintings.
A 19th-century ghat along the banks of the river Narmada, considered to be one of the largest in the country.

Ooty.x: Ooty, short for Ootacamund and officially Udhagamandalam, is a popular hill resort in the state of Tamil Nadu in Southern India. The name Udhagamandalam is derived from the Toda word "othakal-mund" which means "house in mountains". Ooty stands at 2,240 m (7,347 feet) above sea level in the Nilgiri Mountains.

see.d: This place has grown as a famous temple of Lord Muruga, and is known as 7th Hill house of the lord. The view from the temple is great.
The peak of Dodabetta (literally meaning the big mountain) stands at an altitude of 2,623 m. It is the highest peak in Nilgiri and the second highest peak of South India.
Some call it the "Lamb's Rock", as it naturally took the shape of a lamb. Go through a very small forest and then you can see the rock.
Be sure to visit this palace-turned-hotel of the Mysore Maharaja. Extremely beautiful place and quite affordable tea-snacks and slightly expensive buffet dinner.
If you are on a sightseeing tour to Ooty, you might want to visit the Government Botanical gardens, which were laid out in 1847.
Todas were the original inhabitants of Ooty region. They are one of the tribes of the Nilgiri region. The Toda temple consists of an inverted U-shaped structure made of Bamboo.

do.d: Paddle and speed boat rides in the lake. There are various rides like pirate ship, flying saucer, toy train, etc. There are other activities like haunted houses.
It's popular here. In one hour you can go around the lake or longer rides you can visit countryside around Ooty.

Orchha.x: Orchha is a town in Madhya Pradesh near the banks of the Betwa River. The medieval city of Orchha seems to have frozen in time, its palaces and temples still retaining their original grandeur. Orchha had the distinction of being the capital of one of the largest and most powerful kingdoms of Central India.

see.d: There are 14 Chhatris or Memorials to the rulers of Orchha, grouped along the Kanchan Ghat of the river Betwa on the south end of town.
Built upon a massive stone platform and reached by a steep flight of steps, the temple was specially constructed to enshrine the image of Rama that remained in the Ram Raja Temple.
The fort complex is a great place to visit; hit this first to obtain an all-day ticket good for all the sights in Orchha. Divided into 3 parts, it consists of:
The style is an interesting synthesis of fort and temple moulds. The interiors contain the most exquisite of Orchha's wall paintings.
Laid out as a formal garden, this complex testifies to the refined aesthetic qualities of the Bundelas. A central row of fountains culminates in an eight pillared palace-pavilion.
This is the centre around which the life of Orchha revolves. The presiding Deity here is Lord Ram.

Osiyan.x: Osiyan or Osian, popularly known as the "Gateway to The Thar Desert", is a small town in Rajasthan, India known for its ancient temple ruins and as a base for camel safaris into the dessert. The ancient town was a great trading center between 8th and 12th centuries. Today it is a desert oasis with 16 Hindu and Jain temples that are beautifully sculpted and designed, most of which have stood the ravages of time.

Palakkad.x: Palakkad is a city in Central Kerala in India. Palakkad is known for its historical background and the remnants of Tippu Sulthan's Fort are still maintained. Palakkad is famous for the ancient Palakkad Fort, which is in the heart of the city and was captured and rebuilt by Hyder Ali in 1766 which later fell into the hands of Zamorin in 1784.

see.d: Tribal villages. 38 km Home of Irulas and Mudugars
The first peafowl sanctuary in Kerala.
15 km
Colonial structure.The Government Victoria College in Palakkad is an institution of higher learning in the Malabar region of Kerala
15th century Jain Temple
The Kanjirapuzha Dam, a masonry earth dam built for providing irrigation to a Cultural Command Area (CCA) of 9,713 hectares (24,000 acres), is located in the Palakkad district in the Indian…

do.d: The biggest chariot in Kerala.
A spectacular festival.
The celebrations commemorate the victory of the Chittur Nairs over the militia of nearby Konganadu during 918 AD.
Colourful Temple car festival where all the streets of the village will be lightened and the procession of Rathas will take place.
A traditional Indian festival.

Palampur.x: Palampur is a town in the Himalayan foothills in Himachal Pradesh. It is famous for its mountain scenery and tea gardens.

see.d: A tourist place worth seeing: it is filled with fountains and caves and there is a temple of Lord Shiva. It is 25 km from Palampur on Andretta Road.
About 16 km from here. It is a historic temple of Lord Shiva and it is there from the reign of pandavas, one will find it amazing. It has beautiful monuments which are worth seeing.
Another famous temple which is about 35 km from Palampur. It is situated in the heart of Kangra city.
A temple 4 km from the town on the Nuegal Cafe Road. It is a worthseeing place full of nature's blessings.
About 17 km from Palampur and is very popular destination for Indian tourists. It is believed that it is a place where Devi Chamunda killed two evils named Chand and Mund.
A temple at nature's paradise 5 km from the Bundla Mata temple and also 5 km from palampur via chandpur village.

Palani.x: Palani is a town in Tamil Nadu. The Palani Murugan Temple, dedicated to Lord Murugan, sits on a hill overlooking the town. The temple is visited by more than 7 million pilgrims each year.

see.d: This is another beautiful hill station about 64 km from Palani.
Located near Pappampatti; Palani, it has a water falls at the back of the dam. Once you reach the dam, one can find the way to go to falls with the help of the local villagers.
This is but one of the famous temples in the surrounding area. This temple is about 1 km from the bus stand.
This is the prime attraction in Palani. One has climb 670 steps to reach the temple.

see.n: Periyanayaki amman kovil or Aanai Kovil
see.d: This is one of the oldest temples in Palani. This temple is carved out of stone. There won't be a very large crowd in this temple.
Another small water falls near the Palani. Water from this place is taken into Palani through pipes and stored in Palani Hill Water Tank named as Water dam, which then distributed to Palani…

Pali.x: Pali is a city of 230,000 people (2011) in Rajasthan state. It is located north of Bandi river, a tributary of Luni river. It is known as "The Industrial City".

see.d: A small museum with a good collection of stone artifacts acquired from different places of Rajasthan. It exhibits ancient, historical and artistic items such as costumes, coins, and arms.

Palitana.x: Palitana is a city and a municipality in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, 50 km south-west of Bhavnagar city. It is a major pilgrimage centre for Jains.

see.n: Palitana Jain temples on Mount Shatrunjaya hill
see.d: Palitana has over 850 temples atop sacred Mount Satrunjaya (the “hill that conquers enemies”), which makes it most of any temple city.
Exhibits ancient manuscripts, idols, history of Jainism, life of Jain Tirthankara Mahavira, models of incidents and legends from Jain universal history. Some information is in English.

see.n: Jain Cosmic View Show at Jambudweep Temple
see.d: The temple has a large model of Jain cosmic world. Large number of explanatory notes in Gujarati is there with art explaining Jain view of the world.

Palolem.x: Palolem is a village in South Goa, India. Palolem has one of the most beautiful beaches in all of Goa. It is a natural bay surrounded by lofty headlands on either sides, resulting in a calm, idyllic sea with a gently sloping bed which allows you to walk up to 100 m out from the beach.

do.d: The alternative to the legendary but almost extinct goa-parties. Big crowds of children gather every Saturday for serious partying and dancing underneath the starry sky.

Panchkula.x: Panchkula is a city in Haryana.

see.d: This is the largest succulent botanical garden of Asia. Situated in the heart of the city of Panchkula, it covers a total area of 7 acres.

Panagarh.x: Panagarh is a town in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal. Being close to Durgapur, Panagarh is fast emerging as the industrial hub of West Bengal.

see.d: The airfield was constructed in 1944 during World War II as a British Royal Air Force Airport.
An archaeological site with a large stupa. The stupa was built during the Pala period. The stupa was built by bricks and stones in the Pancharatha style, with a base area of .
A picnic spot at the bank of the Damodar River. In 1932, the Anderson weir was constructed in the village, which resulted to the availability of irrigation facility in the lower Damodar…

Ottapalam.x: Ottapalam is a small town in Palakkad District in Malabar region, Kerala, India.

see.d: Chinakathoor Pooram festival is conducted here every year.
Famous 21 day festival with costumes and animal shapes on show.

Pandavapura.x: Pandavapura is a town near Mysore city. It is part of Mandya district in Karnataka state, India.

see.d: Twin Lakes, Many hillocks, paddy fields, coconut plantations, cute temples
Ideal for trekking trips. A beautiful view from above
Ancient temples, ancient buildings, beautiful views
Picnic spot, Lakes, temples
Beautiful paddy fields, cute huts and people living in the nineteenth century
A 12th century temple that was submerged in during the KRS dam project. This old temple was eventually moved and restored to a new location Restoration was completed in 2011.

do.d: Very photogenic.

Palakollu.x: Palakollu is a small colourful town in central Andhra Pradesh, with a population of barely a lakh or a hundred thousand.

Orai.x: Orai is a medium-sized city in the Northern Bundelkhand region of India's most populous state, Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: A square-shaped landmark comprising of nine domes and 84 arches. Built in an Indo-Islamic architectural style, it is believed to house a tomb of one of the Sultans of the Lodi dynasty, who…

do.d: A water park full of swimming pools and slides.

Palashi.x: Palashi, historically spelt Plassey, is a village in the Nadia district of West Bengal.

see.d: The monument dedicated to the Battle of Plassey. A memorial stone was erected in 1883 to mark the victory of the British in the battle.

Palanpur.x: Palanpur is in North Gujarat, India.

see.d: 18th-century stepwell which is four-storey deep. Now neglected but still an attraction, it was probably built from material from previous monuments.
According to local legend, the Chaulukya king Siddhraj Jaisimha was born in Palanpur so his mother Mayanalla Devi had ordered to build a stepwell.
Old palace of Nawab. There are beautiful paintings in the courtroom and the stair has fine sandalwood decoration. Photography with permission.
A private sports club now. Nawab Sher Mohammed Khan built it to commemorate coronation of British King George V in 1913.
Beautifully carved marble Jain temple.
Beautiful large garden built by Nawab Taley Muhammed Khan dedicated to his Australian wife Begum Jahanara aka Joan Falkiner.

do.n: Check Photo collection of A. L. Syed (1904-1991)
do.d: He was an official photographer of Nawabs of Palanpur. Contact his son Azmat Syed.
Watch Gujarati or Bollywood films. Snacks and beverages are available too.

Palnadu.x: Palnadu is a cultural region in southern Andhra Pradesh.

see.d: The water here is used for crocodile breeding.
A small village near Madhira and Wyra. It has approximately 1000 houses, which includes the 700 houses of Kammas (Chowdaries) and 150 houses of members of Scheduled Castes and 150 houses of…
A place of deep mystery attracting many tourists to explore.
One of the sites on the Godavari-Krishna delta region where some of the most famous diamonds were found, collectively called the "Golconda diamonds" after the diamond trading centre in…
One of the Buddhist sites in Andhra Pradesh, on an island created by the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam.
A Shiva temple atop a sacred hill. Its original name is Kondakavuru, but is more popularly known as Kotappakonda or Trikutaparvatham, a three-peaked hill nearby.

Pakur.x: Pakur is a mining town in the Santhal Parganas region of Jharkhand, close to Birbhum and Murshidabad districts of West Bengal.

see.d: A memorial park dedicated to the twin leaders of the Santal Rebellion: Sido and Kanhu.

Old Malda.x: Old Malda is a small heritage town near Malda in North Bengal, at the confluence of the Mahananda and Kalindi rivers. Most of the town is developed along parallel streets lined up by old homes.

see.d: The gurudwara was established in 1996 to mark the legendary visit of Guru Nanak who halted at Malda on his way to Puri.
Although the original mosque was built during the rule of Bengal sultan Hussain Shah, the present building was built during the rule of Mughal emperor Akbar in 1004 AH.
A 400-year-old temple with a stone altar. The Shyam Rai deity is placed on the altar every year during Holi (Doljatra) and Krishna Janmashtami.

Panipat.x: Panipat is a city in the state of Haryana in the Plains region of India. An industrial city in modern times, its main claim to fame is that the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was a key step in establishing the Mughal Empire.

see.d: The site of the Third Battle of Panipat between the Marathas and Afghans. According to legend, it was marked by a black mango tree which has since disappeared.
A mosque and garden built by first Mughal emperor Babur to commemorate his victory over Ibrahim Lodi.
The last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, Ibrahim Lodi's tomb is quite a simple looking rectangular tomb with a small flight of steps.
A memorial to 16th century King Hemu, who defeated the Mughals in October 1556 and briefly took control of Delhi before being defeated in a repeat battle around a month later.

Papanasam.x: Papanasam is near to Tirunelveli and Tenkasi at about 40 km, in Tamil Nadu, India. It is famous for a Sivan kovil (a type of temple) and the river Tamirabarani flows here.

Paradip.x: Paradip or Paradeep is a major port town in the North Coast of Odisha.

see.d: You can visit in the Evening Only

Paravur.x: Not to be confused with North Paravur, which is approximately 175 km to the north. Paravur is in Quilon/Kollam district, Kerala, Southern Travancore, India. It is a municipal town connected to Thiruvananthapuram and Quilon by trains and bus.The population is around 44,000 (2011).

see.d: A famous religious place. This church's festival takes place at the last week of October every year. Sunday mass is 7:30AM.

Parumala.x: Parumala is a small town in Pathanamthitta district in Kerala in India. This is an island in Pampa River. Mannar is a small town across the Pampa river near Parumala.

see.d: It is here that Geevarghese Mar Gregorios, the first declared saint of The Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, is entombed.
Temple considered one of the oldest in Kerala.

Paschim Medinipur.x: Paschim Medinipur or West Midnapore is a district of West Bengal. It was once a part of Midnapore district until 2003, which got split into two districts: Paschim Medinipur and Purba Medinipur.

Pathankot.x: Pathankot is a city and district in the Indian state of Punjab.

see.d: Fortress built by the Pathania Rajputs, more than 900 years ago. It was damaged due to the great earthquake which struck this region early in 1905 AD.
The fort is one of the main attractions of Pathankot city. It was built in 1505 AD by a Rajput chief, by the name of Jaspal Singh Pathania.
An important ancient Shiva temple 30 km from Pathankot towards Indora/Chanour (HP).

Patiala.x: Patiala is a city in Punjab, India. Patiala is a lively city known for its production of handcrafted goods. The juttis, traditional embroidered shoes for women and men alike, are exported all over the world to the Punjabi diaspora.

see.d: The gardens were designed in 1876 by Kaur Sahib Ranbir Singh, the younger brother of the Maharaja. They surround colonial buildings and a marble statue of Maharaja Rajindera.
