The Palace, built in the mid-19th century, was the seat of the Patiala royal family. With over 1,000 rooms it's one of the largest royal residences in the world.
Qila Mubarak was the official residence of the Maharaja till 1862. The complex comprises 10 courtyards and several historic built structures.

do.d: A 620-ha reserve protecting home to wild boars, partridges, hares, owlets, jungle cats, and hog deer.

Parassinikkadavu.x: Parassinikkadavu is a small riverside tourist town in Kannur District, Kerala, India. This is the only temple where the mild alcoholic drink called 'Toddy' is offered to the God at the temple.

see.d: You can get an auto (₹20) for a ride down the winding road to the temple. Alternatively there is a direct footpath with wide steps. The temple has a simple layout and cute look.
You can go across the Vellikkeel Bridge by hiring an auto-rickshaw from Bakkalam to Pattuvam (₹200). Very beautiful mangrove swamps and an estuary.
Scenic mosque in the middle of a paddy field.
Traditional blacksmith workshop is the main attraction. There is a lighthouse in this island.
Tourist spot
Photogenic Place

do.d: All coconut and arecanut. Beautiful bridge wide enough for a small car.
Take the road left immediately before the Parassini bridge. Climb the little to the centre of the town. (4 km)
Bakkalam is an ideal village for a leisurely stroll. There are coconut plantations and paddy fields wherever you look.
Parking facility for 100 cars, several rides, shops selling swimming clothes etc. This business venture is owned and managed by the local Communist Party.
Theyyam is performed in the temples of Parassinikkaavu and surrounding cities during certain times of the year.

Pattambi.x: Pattambi is a small town inhabited by 28,000 people in Palakkad District of Malabar region, in Kerala state, India. The town is famous for its rich lineage in literature.

do.d: A unique and terrific festival, which is celebrated by all residents of Pattambi harmoniously. It is held in memory of Aloor Valiya Pookunjikoya Thangal, a Muslim saint of Malabar.

Panitanki.x: Panitanki is a village in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, India.

Panihati.x: Panihati, or colloquially Peneti, is a heritage town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, on the Hooghly River.

see.d: A row of 12 Shiva temples along the Hooghly River.
Founded in 1921 by Satish Chandra Dasgupta, a close aide of Mahatma Gandhi. The institution occupies an important place in Indian independence movement and which Gandhi himself called it…
A "pancharatna" (five-pinnacled) temple dedicated to Radha-Krishna. The temple premise resembles that of Dakshineswar with a row of Shiva temples at riverside and a ghat at the middle, but…
One of the elegant edifices on the Hooghly River. It originally belonged to Asutosh De or Chatu Babu, one of the figures of the 19th-century Bengali Renaissance.

Pandua (Malda).x: Pandua, also known as Adina, is a medieval citadel in the Northern Plains‎ of West Bengal, India. It is known for its massive Adina Masjid along with the ruins of a couple of mosques, tombs and darghas. A trip to Pandua can be combined with a trip to the nearby citadel of Gour with Malda as the base.

see.d: Built in 1369 by Sultan Sikander Shah and during that time it was the largest mosque in India. The courtyard measures by . The entrance is through an insignificant door.
Eklakhi Tomb or Mausoleum houses constructed by Sultan Jalaluddin Mohammad Shah in around 1425 at a cost of rupees one lakh (hundred thousand) and hence the name.
Locally known as Chota Sona Masjid, the Qutb Sahi Mosque is built in honour of Saint Nur Qutb-ul-Alam.
A well-preserved wildlife sanctuary with spotted deer and nilgais. This is controlled by the West Bengal Forest Department and one can witness migratory birds during winter.
This hammam was once part of the royal complex of the Illiyas Shah dynasty. Nothing much remains of the royal hammam.
This too is located near the deer park. This minar standing on a small mound was part of the defensive system of the royal enclosure of Pandua during the Illiyas Shah dynasty.

Paschim Bardhaman.x: Paschim Bardhaman, literally "West Bardhaman", is the western coal-rich industrial district of West Bengal. Fondly known as the "Ruhr of India", Paschim Bardhaman is home to two steel cities, a coal mining centre, and a locomotive workshop.

Panskura.x: Panskura, a town along the Kangsabati River in West Bengal, is famous for the state's "Valley of Flowers". It's a popular weekend getaway for Kolkata residents in spring.

see.d: A secluded village, often called the "Valley of Flowers" of West Bengal. During the months of January-March, the fields are full of flower species like marigolds, chrysanthemums, tuberose…

Pandhurna.x: Pandhurna is a small town on the banks of the Jam River in Madhya Pradesh, India. It's not a place that shows up on the usual India tourist trail, and honestly, most of the year there's not a whole lot happening here. But once a year, for one single evening, this quiet orange-farming town turns into the site of one of the strangest and most talked-about festivals in the country.

do.d: Celebrated every year on Bhadrapada Amavasya (new moon) on the second day of Pola festival.

Pandya Nadu.x: Pandya Nadu consists of the homeland of the Pandya dyansty as well as the southernmost point of mainland India.

Prayagraj.x: Prayagraj, formerly Allahabad, is one of the holiest cities in India, is in Uttar Pradesh. The city is famous for being the site of the confluence of the holy rivers Ganges and Yamuna; and also the Hindu pilgrimage Kumbh Mela, the largest gathering of humans on the planet holding hundreds of millions of pilgrims every 12 years.

see.d: The Allahabad Fort, built from the year 1583 onwards by Akbar, stands at the junction of the two great rivers.
It is the seat of Justice in Uttar Pradesh, and is the oldest high court in the country with largest strength of judges.
It is the place to experience the British era of Indian history. The park came up in 1870 during the visit of Prince Alfred (second son of Queen Victoria) and was named after him.
Victoria Memorial is not a memorial but a canopy, which once housed the imposing marble statue of Queen Victoria.
The marvelous monuments is perched in Company Garden. The monument served as the house of the legislative assembly during the British era, when Allahabad was the capital of United…
Khusro Bagh is a walled Mughal styled garden and burial chamber located just south of the Allahabad (Prayagraj) Junction station.

do.d: A dip in the holy Sangam of the Ganges, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati is a must for the spiritually inclined. It is a sacred holy site for Hindus.
Spiritual and refreshing. Sitting along the river banks and seeing the flowing water is also worth to be done. However sitting alone in aloof areas is risky for women and foreigners.

do.n: Walk in the Magh/Kumbh Mela area
do.d: The days which are best to visit Prayagraj falls in the Hindu month of 'Magha'. A stroll in the make shift streets of Mela area is blissfully energizing.
Various water sports can be enjoyed in the waters of Yamuna. Skiing, para-sailing, kayaking, canoeing, wind surfing enterprise, yachting boat, optimist sailing, water snookering, shallow…
A place for those who are interested in astronomy. Shows are at every hour and charges are nominal. Children under age of 7 are not allowed.(Closed on Mondays).

Pawapuri.x: Pawapuri, 101 kilometers from Patna and 38 kilometers from Rajgir, or Pava is a holy site for Jains.

see.d: A marble temple, the Jalmandir, was later built in the middle of the tank, and is now a major pilgrimage spot for Jains.

Pettavaithalai.x: Pettavaithalai is in the Central Tamil Nadu region of India. It is located between Kulithalai and Tiruchirappalli. The town is an important pilgrimage location.

Pilibhit.x: Pilibhit is a city in Uttar Pradesh in India. It is 48 km from Bareilly and is the greenest area.

see.d: The protected forest holds an amazing ecosystem of over 400 square miles and provides a good prey base for the elegant cats.

Plains (India).x: The Plains of India are the country's heartland. Also called the Hindi Belt, this region contains the large and politically significant states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and the country's capital, New Delhi. With an area of about 400,000 square kilometres (150,000 sq mi), the Plains are the home of about half a billion people (about one in every sixteen people alive today), including the densely-populated cities of Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi and Patna.

Pollachi.x: Pollachi is a town and a municipality close to the foothills of Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, 40 km south of Coimbatore. It is picture perfect for the nomenclature — Mini Kodambakkam. Though prominently known for cash crops, coconuts and second biggest ‘sandhai’ (market) in the country, the town has now become famous for cinema shootings and consequently a huge tourist attraction.

see.d: It is the home of the Vethathiri Maharishi Kundalini Yoga and Kayakalpa Research Foundation, founded by Shri Vethathiri Maharishi in 1985.
Aliyar (ஆழியார் azhiyar) Dam is a reservoir 27 km away from pollachi on the foothills of Valparai, in the Anamalai range of the Western Ghats.
This place is 20 km from Thirumoorthy dam. One must take the left road near Chinnar check-post (Tamilnadu side) along Udumalpet - Munnar road, to reach this place.
Masani Amman Temple is situated at a distance of 15 km from Pollachi. This sanctified shrine attracts large number of devotees. Here, one can see Goddess Masani Amman in the lying posture.
Monkey Falls is located at the 29th KM junction on the Pollachi-Valparai road. An entry fee of ₹15 per head must be paid at the check post located along Aaliyar - Monkey Falls route.
Lying adjacent to the Indira Gandhi Wild Life Sanctuary, the 285 sq km stretch of forest known as Parambikulam Tiger Reserve (formerly Parambikulam Wildlife Sanctuary) is one of Kerala’s…

Pondicherry.x: Pondicherry, also known as Puducherry or Pondy, is a city in Southern India. There is a strong French influence on the architecture of the city, especially in the old quarters, with rues and boulevards lined with Mediterranean-style houses and bakeries, although the city remains very much Indian. French is still understood, and the whole city makes for a pleasant mix of the East and the West.

see.d: There's a white monument at the centre of the park called Aayi Mandapam. It was built during the time of Napoleon III.
You can take a motorboat to Paradise Beach from here. It is crowded on holidays and weekends.
The largest lake of Pondicherry and home to around 200 species of birds. About 40 species of migratory birds visit the sanctuary after November annually, including golden oriole, open-bill…
A nice park, though a little in disarray. An aquarium, maintained by the Directorate of Fisheries, is also a must-see while in the garden.
A lighthouse was constructed in Pondicherry in the nineteenth century by the French rulers. A new lighthouse was constructed in the 20th century by the Government of India.
A war memorial dedicated to the French Indians who died for the country during the First World War. A bronze plaque lists the names of soldiers who died during the First World War.

do.d: The latter is a factory outlet of the former.
A beach known for its white sands, clear waters, and surrounding coconut groves.Activities include swimming, jet skiing, kayaking, nature trails, bird watching, etc.
You need to hire a motorboat for pick up and drop to the beach from Chunnambar Boat house which will cost you around ₹200.
A 1.2-kilometre-long stretch in Pondicherry, which starts from War Memorial and ends at Dupleix Park on Goubert Avenue.
Scuba diving club. There is a great range of corals, lion fish, grouper, kingfish, moray eels, eagle and manta rays, parrot fish, sea snakes, triggerfish, butterflies, angels, bannerfish,…

Pondicherry (union territory).x: Pondicherry, officially Puducherry, is a union territory in Southern India. It consists of four enclaves in three different states, which came under French occupation before they were peacefully handed over to India. Each enclave shares a mixed cultural heritage, combining its South Indian roots with a French colonial past.

Porbandar.x: Porbandar is a city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, India. It is the historical birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, and the mythical birthplace of Sudama, the childhood friend of the Hindu god Krishna. The majority of the people here belong to Kharwa community which mainly deals with fishing as their profession.

Pragpur.x: Pragpur is a small heritage village situated in Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh.

Pudukkottai.x: Pudukkottai is in Tamil Nadu. Pudukkottai is also known as Archaeologist's Paradise. It is one of the oldest human settlements in south India.

see.d: The most ornate temple in Pudukkottai district, full of bursting baroque sculptures. It is the temple of Athmanatha.
The museum was opened in 1910 by the Thondaiman Rulers. It is one of the largest museums in Tamil Nadu.
The temple complex includes a 1000-pillared hall and has many inscriptions by the Pallava king Mahendravarman including a treatise on music.
Living places of Jains. The place is almost 800 years old. Nearby lake and boating. Nicely landscaped garden.
A fort constructed by Vijaya Raghunatha Sethupathi, the Raja of Ramnad in 1687. The fort has three entrances; one on the north, another on the south and third on the east.

Puliangudi.x: Puliangudi is a city in Tenkasi District on the NH 208 highway connecting Thirumangalam (near Madurai) with Kollam in Kerala. Located on the foothills of the Western ghats, is one of the fast emerging options as a base for the Sankaran Kovil-Courtallam tourist circuit midway between the two. It is also known for lemon cultivation.

Punalur.x: Punalur is a town and a municipality in Kerala in India.

see.d: An important pilgrim center. Famous for its Sastha temple with a Sastha installed several centuries before the Christian Era.
Known for its cattle market.
Famous as Muslim pilgrim center.
Huge rock. Legend says Jatayu, the giant bird in the epic Ramayana, fell after failing in its attempt to stop Ravana from taking sita away. Ideal place for trekking.
One of the famous waterfall in Kerala.
Famous for its ancient Bhagavathy temple.

Pune.x: Pune, formerly Poona, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Often considered as the cultural capital of Maharashtra, Pune is known for its educational tourism and has a blend of cultural, business, health, and cuisine tourism background. The city also houses fantastic restaurants, good museums, and hill forts which offer panoramic views.

Pulwama.x: Pulwama is a town in Pulwama district in the Kashmir Valley, in central Jammu and Kashmir in India.

Payyanur.x: Payyanur is a town on the Perumba river in Kannur District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, India.

see.d: Curvaceous palm fringed beach with rocky surroundings. Near Kannurgate of Naval Academy.
Majestic white building in a sprawling campus
very scenic place.
Rich people live here.
Big and beautiful temple.
very green and scenic

do.d: Ancient dance festival
Silent island of the local elites
Slow trains are called Passenger Trains in India. They are very cheap and punctual.
Take a slow train ("Passenger Trains") from Payyanur railway station to Chandera railway station. This is a very rural railway station without any road access.
Look for select temples during the right season

Poovankurichi.x: Poovankurichi or Poovan Kurichi is a hamlet in the district of Tirunelveli near Ambasamudram, Tamil Nadu, India. The village is located 50 km west of Tirunelveli town and 30 km from Tenkasi.

Pileru.x: Pileru (also known as Piler) is a town in Annamayya district of the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is located on the banks of the Pileru River and serves as a connecting point between Tirupati and Rayalaseema. The town is surrounded by small hills and greenery and is known for its peaceful rural vibe.

Poovar.x: Poovar is a small coastal village at the southernmost tip of Thiruvananthapuram district in Southern Travancore in Kerala, South India. Its name is derived from the Malayalam words poo (flower) and ar (river) which translates as "River of Flowers," a name bestowed by Marthanda Varma, the 18th-century king of Travancore, in recognition of the fragrant flowers that once floated down the Neyyar River to reach the sea here. What makes Poovar genuinely singular is a rare geographical convergence: the Neyyar River, a freshwater lake, the backwater canals, and the Arabian Sea all meet within a few hundred metres of each other.

Punjab (India).x: This article covers the Indian state of Punjab. For the Pakistani province, see Punjab (Pakistan). For a general background on the pre-partition region, see Punjab.

Punjabi phrasebook.x: Punjabi/Panjabi is the language of the Punjab/Panjab regions of Pakistan and India. In India, it is written predominantly in the native Gurmukhi alphabet. In Pakistan, it is written in a slightly modified version of the Urdu alphabet called Shahmukhi.

Purba Medinipur.x: Purba Medinipur or East Midnapore is a coastal district of West Bengal. It was once a part of Midnapore district until 2003, which got split into two districts: Paschim Medinipur and Purba Medinipur.

Puri.x: Puri, also known as Jagannath Puri (the Abode of Lord Jagannath) or Purushottama Puri, is a seaside pilgrimage town in the Indian state of Odisha. It is a major tourist destination with the famous temple of Lord Jagannath (means Lord of the World) and a very long beach offering beautiful and pleasant sights. There are many hotels; most overseas tourists stay near the beach.

see.d: The 8-km long beach of Puri is ideal for surfing and cool for a dip. The beach is covered in golden sand. The waves can also be high and rough during the full moon.
This road is in superb condition. It is peppered with deserted beaches and many rivers flow into the sea in places visible, if not accessible, from the road.
Literally, "the gateway to heaven", Swargadwar is the site of the cremation of almost all famous Odia people. There are good hotels and restaurants near the crematorium.
Great views of the sea along with the town of Puri.
Located in the ancestral home of Netaji. Displays an impressive collection of rare photographs, handwritten letters, journals, and personal artifacts.
A park by the beach, complete with a lotus pond and ornamental plants. IFamily friendly place with toy train and other activitires for kids.

Purulia.x: Purulia is the headquarters of the Purulia district of West Bengal.

see.d: An abandoned airfield used by the United States Army Air Forces during the Burma Campaign (1944-1945) of World War II.
Good place for relaxation.
A research centre and library. It was inaugurated in 1960 by central minister Humayun Kabir in 1960. It displays exhibits collected from different areas of Purulia District.

Pushkar.x: Pushkar is a holy city in Rajasthan, India famous for its Brahma temple, lake, ghats, and bazaar.

see.d: Pushkar Lake is a beautiful, sanctified spot in the centre of Pushkar. It is said to have been created by Lord Brahma and is therefore a place of pilgrimage for the Hindus.
A temple dedicated to Shiva with an underground component.
A beautiful Shiva temple.
One of the very few temples in the world dedicated to Brahma. Read up on Hinduism to learn why this temple is such a rarity! No matter where you stay in Pushkar, you will hear the daily…
A beautiful temple on a hill dedicated to Gayatri, one of the 2 consorts of Brahma.
A Vishnu temple built in South Indian style that is very different from other temples in North India. Poojas are performed here by Iyengars of Tamil Nadu.

do.d: Runs 4 classes per day, each 90 minutes in length. Courses deal with all aspects of yoga from stretching, workout, and philosophy.

Puttaparthi.x: Puttaparthi is the place in Andhra Pradesh, India where the guru Sathya Sai Baba lived until his death in 2011. He is considered as "God Incarnate" by many of his followers. It is a beautiful valley between the hills.

Puttur.x: Puttur is a city in Dakshina Kannada, a coastal region of the Indian province of Karnataka.

see.d: chocolate factory

do.d: This place is one of India's rare hot water springs.

Raipur.x: Raipur is the largest city in Chhattisgarh. It had been the seat of government of the state until the formation of Naya Raipur. There is not a great deal for visitors to see with most tourists visiting the surrounding region.

see.d: A small but well maintained museum with exhibits on the history of the state and an impressive collection of carvings, upstairs has a display of tribal artifacts and models.
A large statue in the center of a somewhat shabby lake (under refurbishment). Built in honour of Swami Vivekanada who was chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna and is…

Rajahmundry.x: Rajahmundry, officially Rajamahendravaram, a city in central Andhra Pradesh, is the state's cultural capital. The city is the birthplace of Nannayya, a Telugu poet.

see.d: Art gallery of a famous artist Damerla Ramarao now managed by State Government of Andhra Pradesh.

Rajapalayam.x: Rajapalayam is a city in Tamil Nadu. It attracts travelers seeking seeking an authentic South Indian experience, particularly the scenery of the Western Ghats foothills.

Rajgir.x: Rajgir (or Rajagriha) is a city in Bihar in India. It is 15 km from the ruins of Nalanda University, and 100 km from Patna, the capital of the state.

see.d: This archeological site is believed to be the jail in which King Ajatshatru imprisoned his father Bimbisara.
The Chariot Route and shell inscriptions consist of two parallel furrows cut deep into the rock ground for about thirty feet and are believed to have been made by Lord Krishna's Chariot.
Believed to be 2500 years old, these Cyclopean walls are a 40 km long and 4 metres wide fortification running around the city.
The place is atop a small hill and believed to be a meditating place of Buddha. You can continue on to the top of Ratnagiri hill, there is a Viswa Shanti Stupa (Peace Stupa) built by the…
This is the shrine of a Muslim Sufi Saint Makhdum Shah and has warm springs similar to Tapodharma.
Dating 1st century CE, the Maniar Matth is said to be a monastery of a cult which worshipped snakes. Several snake and cobra figurins have been found in the vicinity in excavations.

do.d: Take a deep bath in a hot spring (Kund).
Enjoy the ride on the ropeway.

Raichur.x: Raichur is a city of 232,000 people (2011) in Northern Karnataka.

see.d: A hill fort surrounded on three sides by a double row of low circuit walls. It was built without the any cementing material.
A town 5 km from Raichur city, known for its historically important fort, Vishnu temple, two life size elephants carved in white granite and other monuments

Raiganj.x: Raiganj is a town in northern West Bengal, famous for the bird sanctuary along the Kulik River with different species of birds.

see.d: Several types of migratory birds arrive here each year from South Asia and coastal regions. They start arriving in June.
One of the significant historical buildings of Uttar Dinajpur, on the banks of the Nagar River and near the border of Bihar.
A Mughal-style mosque built in 1425 and owned by the Mohanta family.
A dargah of Syed Burhan, built around 1758. Syed Burhan was a leader of the Fakir-Sannyasin rebellion of the late 18th century.
The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Raiganj and one of the few churches in sub-Himalayan North Bengal.
The museum has a collection of pottery works, terracotta sculptures and Surjapuri (a Bengali/Maithili dialect) manuscripts.

Purba Bardhaman.x: Purba Bardhaman, literally "East Bardhaman", is a fertile district of central West Bengal. It is bordered by Birbhum and Murshidabad on the north, Nadia on the east, Hooghly on the south, Bankura on the southwest, and Paschim Bardhaman on the west.

Raghunathpur.x: Raghunathpur is a town in the Purulia district of West Bengal.

see.d: A hill that became popular for being the location of Satyajit Ray's various films, including Gupi Gayen Bagha Bayen and Hirak Rajar Deshe.

Puthanathani.x: Puthanathani is a census town in the Malappuram metropolitan area. It is also one of the major commercial towns under the Malappuram urban agglomeration of Malappuram District in Kerala, India. The town lies on the National Highway 66, between Kottakkal and Valanchery.

do.d: waterfall.
Village.
Street
Communal Harmony Village.
Bypass (road).

Rajkot.x: Rajkot is a city in the state of Gujarat in Western India. Rajkot rather appeals to spiritual tastes. As in Ahmedabad, many ashrams, that offers the teachings of yoga and meditative retreat, are located in the city and its surroundings, amidst forested hills and beautiful lakes.

see.d: The Watson Museum was established in 1888 and was named after the British Political Agent of Kathiwad, Colonel John Watson.
The library has an extensive collection of old books and a repository of reference material linked to the colonial era.
Where Mahatma Gandhi got his primary education. The buildings were built by the Nawab of Junagadh and took the name of the Duke Alfred of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
Mahatma Gandhi's childhood residence. It has now been converted in to a memorial called "Gandhi Smriti".
This unique museum gives an overview to the culture and traditions of the world at large through a medium of various dolls
Founded in 1921 by Mahatma Gandhi, the centre supports small industries such as Khadi spinning. A centre for patola sari weaving is also located here.

do.d: This small amusement park includes a wave pool, a high pendulum slide and a rain discotheque for kids only.

Rajpura.x: Rajpura is a city in the Malwa region of Punjab state in India.

Rameswaram.x: Rameswaram is a town on Pamban Island, in Southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It's known for Ramanathaswamy Temple, a Hindu pilgrimage site with ornate corridors, huge sculpted pillars and sacred water tanks. Together with Varanasi, it is considered to be one of the holiest places in India for Hindus and part of the Char Dham (four abodes) pilgrimage.

see.d: Renowned for its magnificent prakaras or corridors with massive sculptured pillars on either side. The longest corridor in the world is here, 197 m (646 ft) long and 133 m (436 ft) wide.

see.n: House of Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
see.d: The house of former President Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam is an interesting place to visit. His residence has been converted into a museum that stocks his childhood memoirs.

see.n: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memorial
see.d: A very beautiful and grand building. It was inaugurated on the second death anniversary of Dr Kalam.
A temple for Devi Durga.
the deity of Hanuman drawn withsenthooram. Idols of Lord Rama, Sita and Hanuman brought from Dhanushkodi during the 1964 cyclone were placed here.
is a hillock situated 3 km away and is the highest point on the island. Here one can see the imprint of Lord Rama’s feet on a chakra.

do.n: Glass boat ride at Pamban Bridge
do.d: There is one glass boat at the government boating centre on the other end of the bridge.

Ranaghat.x: Ranaghat is a small town along the river Churni in the Nadia district of West Bengal. The name Ranaghat comes from the name of a Dakat Rana. This is the great character of Vande Mataram by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

do.d: A boat cruise in Churni during moonlight is a treat. The place is ideal for a day picnic.

Ranchi.x: Ranchi is the capital of the Indian state of Jharkhand.

see.d: An aquarium, game parlour and food court are worth seeing and good values.
It gives an excellent 360-degree view of the city. A must visit.
Tagore Hill is about 90 m (300 ft) above its base. The elder brother of Rabindranath Tagore, Jyotirindranath Tagore purchased the hillok Morabadi and built up an ashram after the suicide of…

see.n: Yogoda Satsanga Society of India- Ashram
see.d: Paramahansa Yogananda, the author of Autobiography of a Yogi, began his life's work here. The natural beauty and peaceful atmosphere offer refreshment to mind and spirit.
The first science museum established in the state of Jharkhand. It houses several exhibits on astronomy, evolution and topics connected to the area such as coal mining.
An arts and cultural heritage museum showcasing Jharkhand's rich history.

Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary.x: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is near Srirangapatna, Mandya District, Karnataka, India.

Rangia.x: Rangia or Rangiya is a city of 96,000 people (2017) in Assam, not far from the Bhutanese border. Rangia is also known my multiple names , including as the City of Colors, Plantation Valley of Assam, Transportation Hub of Assam, Gateway to the Indo-Bhutan Border. The Baralia River flows through the heart of the city, Rangia is also the sub-district and divisional headquarters of North-East Frontier Railway.

Raxaul.x: Raxaul or Raxual is a border town in the Bhojpur region of the state of Bihar, India.

Tarapith.x: Tarapith is a temple town in the central region of West Bengal, India. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre and several thousand devotees visit the temple every day.

see.d: Named after Sadhak Banakshyapa.
It is an auspicious place well known for its tantric rituals.
You can see a graceful environment at Bamdev Sangha Ashram.

Ramanattukara.x: Ramanattukara is a town in Kozhikode District, in Kerala. Ramanattukara is a busy junction where the roads coming Palakkad and Trivandrum meet and join together towards Kozhikode.

see.d: 1,000 m above sea level.
Beautiful little temple in a very photogenic riverside location.

do.d: Begin from the small road on the left side of Rolex Restaurant near the Bus Station. Continue walking past Aptech Computers and reach a scenic road in the middle of paddy fields.
Start from Annapoorna Restaurant on Kallayi Road. Get into the Krishi Bhavan Road on the right side of the restaurant. Continue walking for two kilometres and never take any right turn.
Pay ₹4 per head and you can cross the Chaliyar river and reach the scenic villages of Chaliyam and Kadalundi.
Vehicles are not allowed on the sea walk.
Ten acre hill with scenic sunrise. Suitable for cycling and trekking. Ottamaram or 'single tree' is the highest point.

Ratanpura.x: Ratanpura is a village in Rajgarh tehsil of Churu district in Rajasthan. This village was established in 1848. It is situated 45 km northeast of Churu city and 17 km southwest of Rajgarh.

Ratnagiri.x: Ratnagiri is in the South Konkan region of Maharashtra, Western India.

see.d: An old harbour, no longer in use as such but, instead, as a good white sand beach. A good beach with black sand is Mandvi Bundar.
An area where river meets to sea. The village near this place is Bhatye, so known as Bhatyachi Khadi. The place is beautiful with a view of river & sea both.
A clean seashore and Ganpati temple, about 30 km North from Ratnagiri. This temple is reconstructed in Rajasthani stones and look.
The monument and the home of a man who set off the 'Swadeshi Movement' and spearheaded the fight against the British Raj
The temple built by Swatantryaveer Savarkar for patit class of people.
A fort covered by sea on 3 sides, with a temple of Goddess Bhagwati inside.

Ratlam.x: Ratlam is a city in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh.

see.d: The garden is not very big but well maintained and is quite different from most other gardens you are likely to come across.
A major Jain temple centred around the first tirthankara (spiritual teacher) of Jainism, Adinath.
A Jain temple dedicated to Lord Parshvanath, the 23rd tirthankara (saviour) in the religion.

Raniganj.x: Raniganj is a town in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal.

see.d: The brass chariot used in the Ratha Yatra celebration of Raniganj.

Rajnagar (Bihar).x: Rajnagar is a historic town in the Mithila region of northern Bihar, India, near the town of Madhubani. Once a prominent seat of royalty and architectural innovation, it is now known primarily for the sprawling ruins of the Rajnagar Palace Complex, built during the early 20th century by Maharaja Rameshwar Singh of the Darbhanga Raj family. Though now in a dilapidated state, the palace ruins remain a symbol of the grandeur and cultural sophistication of the Mithila region.

see.d: The primary reason to visit Rajnagar is to witness the hauntingly beautiful ruins of the once-grand palace.

Rejinagar.x: Rejinagar is a town in Murshidabad, West Bengal.

see.d: Mir Madan was one of the generals of Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah who died in the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

Rayagada.x: Rayagada is a town in South Odisha, close to Andhra Pradesh. It is one of Odisha's many hilly spots.

see.d: A suspension bridge over the Nagavali River, with scenic views of the river and the surrounding hills.
A beautiful temple with Ratha Yatra organised every year.

Rasikbil.x: Rasikbil, a lake in North Bengal, is popular among birdwatchers for migratory birds. There's an aquarium, deer park and a gharial rehabilitation centre as well.

Ramanathapuram.x: Ramanathapuram or Ramnad, a town in southern Tamil Nadu, is the gateway to Rameswaram and Dhanushkodi.

see.d: The palace of the Sethupathi family.

Rewa.x: Rewa is a city in northeastern Madhya Pradesh, India, with a rich history and cultural significance. The city is home to the White Tiger Safari, a major tourist attraction. Additionally, The city hosts several historical sites, including the Rewa Fort and Govindgarh Palace, which reflect its architectural and cultural heritage.

Rewari.x: Rewari is a city in Haryana, 80 km south of New Delhi.

see.d: This museum holds the oldest surviving steam locomotives, including the Fairy Queen.

Rishikesh.x: Rishikesh, a small town in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, is famously known as the "yoga capital" (or "Yog Nagari"). Scenically located where the Ganges comes down from the Himalayas, Rishikesh catapulted to Western fame when the Beatles dropped by for a visit to Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram.

see.d: One of the temples set up by 'Adiguru Shankaracharya' during the 12th century. This temple is a real tribute to Vishnu, the idol of which is carved from a sole piece of Saligram.
Place of Guru Shri Ram Sukh Daasji (the great thinker of his time) and popular among the Hindu Brahmin community. Twice a year people gather at this ashram to read the Ramayana together.
One of the most sacred temples in Rishikesh. Located on hill over Swarg Ashram at a height of 1,675 m.
One of the few ashrams left in India where children get the Vedas education. A must-visit in the evening for the Pooja/Aarti, at 5PM in winter and 6PM in summer.
Swargashram (Heavenly Abode), as the name connotes, is a beautiful place situated in picturesque surroundings at the foot of Himalayas on the left bank of the Ganges between Rishikesh and…
It is 13 stories high, with different deities throughout.

do.d: Centre for learning palmistry and astrology.
Personal horoscopes and palm reading from Dr. Gaurav Agrawal and the astrologer B.P. Uniyal. The horoscopes can be made on a distance, using your place and date of birth.
Run by soma a local reiki master which is in Gita Ashram.
Maayaa offers sound healing, reiki, chakra healing, numerology, Tarot reading, physic counselling, aromatherapy, Kundalini meditation, dowsing, chakra balancing.
Panchakarma, Ayurveda, Physiotherapy, Yoga & Ayurveda retreat.

Robertsganj.x: Robertsganj is a city in Uttar Pradesh in India. The town was named after the British soldier Frederick Roberts, 1st Earl Roberts. As with much of the Indian plains, the best time to visit is during the cooler months from October to March.

see.d: A lookout and a picnic area. Great views of the Son Valley.
The 25 hectare park contains fossils of stromatolites, algae and ancient trees that are around 1.4 billion years old, dating to the Proterozoic period.
The split stone structure has its origin in a folklore love story. The hero Veer Lorik demonstrates his love for Manjari by cutting the stone with his sword in a single swipe.
The fort is believed to have existed in the mythological times of the Mahabharata. In the 11th century, it was upgraded by Maharaja Vijay Pal.

Roha.x: Roha is a small city in the Raigad district of Maharashtra.

see.d: Dhavir Maharaj is the prime deity of Roha. Every year the town celebrates Navaratri Festival by having a 10 day Festival at the Dhavir Temple which ends on the 10th day - "Dasra" during…
The fort is believed to have been built during the Shilahar dynasty and was reconstructed by the great Maratha king Shivaji.

Rohtak.x: Rohtak is a city in Haryana. It is the political capital of Haryana, and ainly famous for reputed educational institutes, cloth market and dairies.

see.d: The Tilyar lake is spread over 132 acres. To attract people, there's a restaurant and a mini zoo with bears, tigers, panthers, deer, birds monkeys etc, a toy train for children, a small…

Roorkee.x: Roorkee is a small town in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is approximately 170 km from the capital of India, New Delhi.

see.d: It is one of the largest yoga institutes in India, possibly the whole world. Named after the Rishi Patanjali, the institute is Baba Ramdev's flagship project.

Rourkela.x: Rourkela is the main centre of trade in the Sundergarh district and state of Odisha (formerly known as Orissa).

see.d: This is the highest waterfall of Odisha and among the highest of India. Khandadhar means the edge of a sword. The fall looks like a hanging sword from a distance.

Sagar.x: Sagar is a university city in Madhya Pradesh. There are also many temples, lakes and waterfalls in the vicinity, which has helped establish the city as an important site on the Indian tourist circuit.

Sagara.x: Sagara is a city in Central Karnataka, most famous for its proximity to Jog Falls.

see.d: Temple built by Keladi dynasty, 6 km from Sagara.
From Shimooga; the nearest District headquarters, you can reach Sagara by train then lot of government buses are available.
A large waterfall 30 kilometres (19 mi) away, created by the Sharavathi River falling from a height of 253 meters (829 ft), the highest plunge of an Indian waterfall.

Sainthia.x: Sainthia is an economically important city in West Bengal. According to the 2011 Indian census, it is the 4th most populous city in Birbhum district; the city had a population of 44,601.

see.d: This temple is part of the famous Shakti Peethas in Indian Subcontinent.
This is an urban park/municipal park.
is an urban park/municipal park near "Birbhum Vivekananda Homeopathic Medical College and Hospital" and an amazing view of the Mayurakshi river.
A temple of Goddess Kali.

Salcete.x: Salcete or Salcette is a taluka in South Goa with the business capital Margao as its centre.

see.d: "dedicated to restore and preserve motoring and motorcycling gems of historical interest in Goa". You can find cars ranging from Mercedes Benz, to Peugeot, Morris, Chevrolet and Volkswagen.
Big Foot is an attempt to illustrate and recreate Goa's traditional past.

Salem (India).x: Salem is a city in Tamil Nadu. Nicknamed the Steel City, it is best known in modern times for its steel plant and manufacturing industry. It is also a short trip away from the hills of the Eastern Ghats, offering natural scenic beauty.

see.d: A well preserved 300 year old famous Fort
52 km from Salem.
water place
An old famous fort in Sankari.
Built by Tippu Sultan.
Atop 863 steps.

do.d: Lord Balamurugaa temple; suyambhu form is not to be missed.

Sambalpur.x: Sambalpur is the biggest city in western Odisha (formerly known as Orissa). It is a historically important place, mainly because of the number of freedom fights against the British, Veer Surendra Sai being one of the many who died fighting the British.

see.d: Longest earth dam in the world. The reservoir forms an artificial lake with an area of 746 km² having a shoreline of over 640 km. The drive on the 21-km dyke is majestic.
Famous for its Shiva temple, Huma contains the only leaning temple of Odisha. The Mahanadi river flows close by.
The temple of Vidala-Nrusimha stands at the foot of the picturesque Gandhamardan hill believed to be part of the hill which Hanuman carried on his shoulders from the Himalayas for saving…
The Pradhanpat hill with its waterfalls offers a rare scenic beauty. These falls are close to Deogarh town which is 96 km from Sambalpur on NH.6.
Erected by the Chauhans in the mid-16th century. Samaleswari Temple is dedicated to the goddess known as 'Maa', also known among the natives as samalei maa, meaning Mother Samaleswari.
It stands out amongst all the wildlife sanctuaries in Odisha in terms of sighting wild animals, particularly in summer when trees shed their leaves.

Sanchi.x: Sanchi is a village in central Madhya Pradesh in India, about 9 km southwest of Vidisha and 46 km from Bhopal. It is the site of a great Buddhist stupas listed on UNESCO World Heritage List.

see.d: The events of Buddha's life are carved in stone on the four gates at east, west, north and south sides of the Stupa. The site is very well maintained by the Archaelogical Survey of India.
They have some wonderful artifacts there. The history and historical artifacts from places around Sanchi.

Sangli.x: Sangli is a city in South Maharashtra.

Sanguem.x: Sanguem is in South Goa. It had a population of about 6400 in 2011.

see.n: Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park
see.d: 240 km² (93 sq mi) protected area in the Western Ghats along the eastern border with Karnataka, near the town of Molem, 57 km (35 mi) east of Panaji.
One of the highest waterfalls in India with a height of 310 m (1017 feet) and an average width of 30 metres (100 feet). It is in the Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park.
On the Salaulim River, a tributary of the Zuari River, is a component of the Salaulim Irrigation Project.

Saharanpur.x: Saharanpur or Saharunpore is in Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: Nau Gaja Peer roughly translates to the "Nine Gaja Saint" (Gaj is a traditional unit of length in India equivalent to about 0.91 metres or 3 feet).

Rupnagar.x: Rupnagar, formerly called Ropar or Rupar, is a city in the northern part of the Malwa region of the Punjab state of India. It is on the south bank of the Sutlej River and has a population of 50,000.

Saharsa.x: Saharsa is a city in the state of Bihar, beside the city of Darbhanga. Saharsa has many colleges.

see.d: The U-shaped lake next to Matsyagandha Temple sometimes has boating services available.
A dam that was constructed close to the India-Nepal border. north of the dam is a freshwater wildlife reserve, where you will find the Gangetic Dolphin among other species.

Sarnath.x: Sarnath is a holy town in Uttar Pradesh, India, about 13 km north-east of Varanasi. It's famous as the site of the deer park where Gautama Buddha first taught the Dharma and also where the original Sangha was formed. Consequently, it is one of the 4 main Buddhist pilgrimage destinations, and since 2026 the Chaukandi Stupa and the Archaelogical Remains of Sarnath are listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

see.d: Only the base remains. The base of the pillar has been enclosed in a glass enclosure. The lion capital, which topped the pillar has been displayed at the nearby site museum.
Constructed by king Ashoka in 249 BCE to commemorate his pilgrimage to the Deer Park.
The ruins of the temple where the Buddha spent his first rainy season.
Dharmarajika Stupa dates back to the time of Ashoka. Sadly it is in complete ruins and only its base remains.
The structure consists of four arms and hence the name. It was constructed in the 4th - 5th century CE, during the Gupta period.The stupa marks the spot where the Buddha met the five…
A standing Buddha statue, 24.3 metres (80 feet) in height, inspired by the Bamiyan Buddha is located inside the temple complex.

Sasaram.x: Sasaram is a city in the Bhojpur region of Bihar, India. The town contains three tombs of Sur kings and a couple of related monuments. Sasaram lies on the Grand Trunk Road, which was refurbished by Sher Shah Suri.

see.d: The Tomb of Sher Shah Suri follows the Indo - Islamic form of architecture. It was constructed by Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan and was constructed between 1540 - 45.
Hasan Shah Suri was Sher Shah's father and his tomb lies just east of his son's tomb.
Islam Shah, also known as Salim Shah, is the son of Sher Shah. He is the second ruler of the Sur Dynasty, and ruled from 1545 - 54.
Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan (Alawal Khan) was the architect of the tombs of both Hasan Shah and Sher Shah.
This small fort like structure is located in the vegetable market area of Sasaram.
Maa Tara Chandi Temple is one of the "52 Shakti Peetha". The right eye (Netra) is said to have fallen here. It is dedicated to Maa Durga or Maa Shakti.

Satara.x: Satara is a city in South Maharashtra. It was the last seat of the Maratha Empire and contains several of its historical monuments and forts. It is an old city reflected by cobbled streets and old buildings perched upon the hills of the Western Ghats.

see.d: Ajinkyatara is a (prominent) fort on one of the seven mountains surrounding Satara.
A memorial in Satara honoring Rango Bapuji Gupte. This memorial is located on a hill offering a view of the city on one side and Ajinkyatara Fort on the other.
A UNESCO World Heritage (Biodiversity) site famous for wildflowers.
A replica of the original in Tamil Nadu built in the 1980s. This temple for Sri Nataraja has several towers and four gateways as well as several shrines (temples) within the complex.
About 10 km from Satara city in the village Degav, the place of God Mahadev. Place is surrounded by around 300,000 pindis (sacred stones or tree stumps).
This is 18 km from the city. Not only is it a fort and the final resting place of Sant Ramdas; it is a pilgrimage site

Satna.x: Satna is a small town in Madhya Pradesh in India. It has a population of around 300,000. It is famous for its cement factories.

see.d: The place where Ramcharitra Manas was written. Very nice place to visit for greenery and to see ancient caves where Lord Ram spent around 12 years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshman.
Sharda Mata temple.
Not many people know, but it is a wonderful place with greenery all around and a peaceful meditative atmosphere.
Ancient remains of temples and Hanumanji Mandir

Sattur.x: Sattur is a small town in Southwestern Tamil Nadu, India.

Saurashtra.x: Saurashtra, a peninsular region in Gujarat, is the lower jaw of the lion-shaped state in western India.

Shankarpur.x: Shankarpur is a beach town in Purba Medinipur, West Bengal.

see.d: Well-developed beach with a park.

Wardha.x: Wardha is a city of 126,000 people (2011) in Vidarbha. Founded in 1866, the town is now an important center for the cotton trade. It was an important part of Gandhian Era.

see.d: This temple is situated in Gopuri near Vishwa Shanti Stupa. This is a unique temple in India which has no deity and roof.
The Kelzar Ganpati Temple is situated about 26 km from Wardha on Nagpur Road. This temple is situated on a hill and is surrounded by the scenic beauty of forests and hills.
This museum was inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1938. It is situated in Maganwadi near Centre of Science for village.
This ashram was established by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1934 on bank of river Dham with spiritual purpose. He also establish Brahma Vidya mandir in it. He started Bhoodan movement from here.
Old name of village Sevagram was Shegaon. After leaving Sabarmati ashram, Mahatma Gandhi stayed a few days in Wardha City at Bunglow of Jamanalal Bajaj.
Vishwa Shanti Stupa was a dream of Fujii guruji as called by Gandhiji. It is beside Gitai Mandir. It is a large stupa of white color.

West Bengal.x: West Bengal, a state in Eastern India, presents some of the marvellous landscape features and natural scenic beauty, from the picturesque hills of Darjeeling to the mangrove rainforest of the Sundarbans. Here, you can also find man-made structures with varying tastes, from the terracotta temples of Bishnupur to the colonial structures of Kolkata.

Sankarankoil.x: Sankarankoil, or Sankarankovil, is in Tenkasi district in Tamil Nadu.

see.d: The main deity is half Shiva and half Vishnu to emphasis the equality of both gods. The temple has many good and interesting sculptures.

Sawai Madhopur.x: Sawai Madhopur is in the Bharatpur Division of Rajasthan.

see.d: Ancient temple, dating back to 1299.
A Jain temple.

see.n: Rajiv Gandhi Regional Museum of Natural History

Shahdol.x: Shahdol is a small town located in Eastern Madhya Pradesh, India.

Santipur.x: Santipur is a historical town in the Nadia district of West Bengal, India.

Sevoke.x: Sevoke is a small town in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal.

see.d: You can see the turbulent Teesta roaring below. Near the bridge is a temple of Kali, the goddess of destruction, considered very holy.
Goddess Dakshina Kali is worshipped here, atop a steep flight of stairs. Views over Coronation Bridge and Teesta River. People from far off places come here to pray and worship her.
First officially declared a sanctuary in 1949, with a total area of , it's home to Asian elephants, forest boars, sambar deer, leopards, mountain black bears, and various types of birds.
A railway bridge, about long, connecting Siliguri to Malbazar and Alipurduar.

Serampore.x: Serampore is a town in the Hooghly district of West Bengal, on the western bank of the Hooghly River. One of the rare Danish colonies of India, Serampore is unique for its Danish-British-Bengali heritage.

see.d: The former seat of government of Serampore, originally a home of Ole Bie, who built the Danish colony.
The Protestant church was once the centre for all European social and religious events. The church never had a Danish pastor, and was instead being managed by the Serampore Trio.
The first college in Asia to award a degree. It was built in 1818 by the Serampore Trio. The college compound contains a museum dedicated to William Carey.
The cemetery where the Serampore Trio and their relatives are buried. The graves of William Carey, his wife Dorothy, and son Felix are lying side by side. Need a prior permission to visit.
An old temple where Henry Martyn lived for some months. He was a Cantabrigian priest, who arrived in Calcutta (Kolkata) as an East India Company chaplain.
The famous Jagannath temple in Serampore, known for organising the oldest Ratha Yatra in Bengal, after the Puri Ratha Yatra. It is said to have been celebrated since 1396.

Sanjay Gandhi National Park.x: The Sanjay Gandhi National Park, formerly the Borivali National Park, is the lungs of Mumbai. It is famous for its leopards and the caves inside the park.

see.d: A complex of 109 Buddhist temples cut out of rock, and a nice place to visit for history enthusiasts.
Widely visited by the Digambar sect of the Jain community. It has three huge idols of Lord Adinath and his two sons, Bahubali and Bharat.
The second-largest lake in Mumbai and supplies part of the city's potable water. It is inhabited by mugger crocodiles (Crocodylus palustris).
A group of picturesque hills, an unspoiled and pollution-free area, carpeted by natural foliage and fauna.

Sargachi.x: Sargachi, a village in the Murshidabad district of West Bengal, is best known for its Ramakrishna Mission campus, with its science museum and zoological park.

Sattal.x: Sattal is a cluster of seven interconnected freshwater lakes in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, India. Nestled at an altitude of 1,370 m within dense oak and pine forests, it is a tranquil haven for birdwatchers, nature lovers, and those seeking a quiet alternative to the bustling hill stations of Nainital and Bhimtal.

see.d: The largest and most accessible lake. A boating jetty, a small café, and a short walking path encircle its shore.
Connected to Purna Tal by narrow channels. These smaller, shadier lakes are surrounded by thick foliage and offer secluded spots for birdwatching. Often less crowded.
A tranquil pair, ideal for quiet contemplation. Nal‑Damayanti Tal is the deepest, with clear water reflecting the surrounding hills.
Sukh Tal (“Happy Lake”) is a shallow, lily‑covered pool. Garud Tal is the smallest, often dried up by summer’s end.
Established in the 1930s by Dr. E. Stanley Jones, this serene estate houses a chapel, a guesthouse, and a library. The Sunday service (in English and Hindi) is open to all.
A beautiful stone church with stained‑glass windows, set amidst tall pines. The quiet churchyard is a place for meditation.

do.d: Kayaks and pedal boats are available for rent at the main jetty (approx ₹150–300/hr). Paddle to the quieter corners of Purna Tal, especially at sunrise when the mist rises.
A well‑known trail leads from the ashram through oak forest to a viewpoint offering a panoramic glimpse of the Himalayan peaks (on clear days).
With over 100 recorded species, Sattal is a butterflying paradise. Post‑monsoon (September–October) is peak butterfly activity. The forest edges and stream beds are excellent spots.
With a permit from the Forest Department (available at the Bhimtal office), catch‑and‑release fishing for mahseer is possible in certain stretches.
Sattal is one of India’s premier birding destinations. Walk the forest paths at dawn to spot red‑billed blue magpie, orange‑flanked bush robin, black‑headed jay, and migrant flycatchers.

Saraikela.x: Saraikela or Seraikella in South Jharkhand served as the capital of the Singh Deo dynasty. The town is known for the Saraikela version of the famous Chhau dance, a unique style of masked tribal dance.

Shimla.x: Shimla, previously spelt Simla, is the capital of the state of Himachal Pradesh in India. It is a very popular holiday retreat during the summer months and is well known for its Victorian architecture, which is reflected in certain areas of the Mall and the Ridge. It is also a famous holiday spot for honeymoon.

see.d: The waterfall is at its most beautiful just after the monsoon. But for much of the year it can be quite dry, and not as impressive.
Constructed in 1846, this is the second oldest church in North India. The stain-glass windows,representing charity, faith, patience, hope, fortitude and humility, and 19th century organ are…
An amusement offering adventure activities like Burma bridge crossing, Flying Fox, rock climbing, boating, various rides, indoor golf & video games.
Shops open M-Sa. The Lower Bazaar is home to the city's less expensive hotels, cheaper restaurants and shops, and a congested wholesale vegetable market.
The Mall is the main shopping centre of Shimla. This shopping centre has a good number of banks, restaurants, post offices, clubs, bars and tourists offices.
The Ridge is the center of Shimla's cultural and social life - an excellent place to view the surrounding mountains.

do.d: At a distance of 25 km from center of Shimla, Junga village offers paragliding for adventure enthusiasts.

Shimoga.x: Shimoga or Shivamogga is a town in the state of Karnataka. The name originates from Shiva-mukha i.e., face of Lord Shiva.

see.d: Situated on the banks of the River Tunga in the busy lanes of Shimoga is a 16th-century place built by Shivappa Naik of Keladi. A good architectural piece built with rose wood.
Known for being one of the earliest railway stations in Karnataka. The second railway line of the Mysore Kingdom was a meter gauge line between Shimoga and Birur.
Situated in the heart of city, the church was renovated and is said to be second largest church in India with an area of 1800 m² (18000 square feet).
This place comprises a zoo and animals in the wild. Not a safari in the true sense of the word because the lions and tigers are housed in fenced enclosures and a sighting is guaranteed.
On the way to Thirthahalli from Shimoga, you can hear elephants reciting their lessons.
you can hear the birds chirping. This place is a spot for birds migrating from places around the world.

Simultala.x: Simultala is a hamlet in Bihar in India. It is a relatively undeveloped rural area, so may be of interest for tourists looking for a quiet, out of the way place with a pleasant climate.

see.d: A Hindu temple on a hill above sea level.

Shirdi.x: Shirdi is a town in the Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra, India. It is located 185 km east of the Arabian Sea shoreline. Shirdi was where the saint Sai Baba lived till his samadhi in 1918.

do.d: Immersive theme park dedicated secular saint Saibaba. Attractions depict the holy lands of India and pilgrimage sites like Badrinath, Dwarka, Siddhivinayak, Jagganath Puri.

Shivpuri.x: Shivpuri is a city in Madhya Pradesh in India.

see.d: Madhav National Park lies between Agra-Bombay road and Jhansi-Shivpuri Road. It is spread over an area of 157.58 km2.
Famous for Golden Bird.
Shivpuri is famous for graceful,intricately embellished marble chhatries (cenotaphs) erected by Scindia Princes.
Natural spring which is a picnic spot.
Man-made spring and a picnic spot.
9th century fort famous for the love story of king Nal and queen Damyanti.

Sibsagar.x: Sibsagar or Sivasagar is a city in Upper Assam. Sibsagar is famous for its monuments of the Ahom kingdom. It also houses the burial sites of Ahom kings, known as Moidam, a UNESCO World Heritage Site Heritage Site.

see.d: Gourisagar Tank is an artificial lake dating back to the Ahom dynasty. It was excavated between 1715 and 1719 by Queen Phuleswari, the chief consort of Ahom King Siva Singha, also known as…
The biggest of the group, consecrated to Goddess Durga. The temple consists of a garbagriha (sanctum sanctorum) and mandap.
Very similar to the nearby Devi Dol but smaller in size. It follows a similar floor plan with a similar spire.
This is located west of the Shiva Dol and has a similar floor plan. The spire differs from the other two, and the honeycomb design is similar to the one in Kamayakha.
The Ahom-era stone bridge was built in 1703 by the Ahom king Rudra Singha. It runs over the Namdang river, a tributary of the Dikhou river.
Construction of the temple began in 1773 during the reign of the Ahom king (reign: 1769 – 80) and was completed during the reign of Gaurinath Singha (1780 – 94).

Silchar.x: Silchar is the largest city of the Barak Valley region of Assam, India.

see.d: The Capital of Old Cachari Kingdom. Beautiful place with the ruins of the fort used by the Cachari Kings.

Siliguri.x: Siliguri, the largest city in northern West Bengal, is a liberal and cosmopolitan city that is known for its vibrant music scene and strong youth culture. On the banks of the Mahananda River and the Teesta River at the foothills of the Darjeeling Hills, Siliguri is the third-largest urban agglomeration in West Bengal. It is known as the "Gateway of North-Eastern India" as it connects North-Eastern India with the mainland through a narrow strip of land, making it a major trading and transport hub.

see.d: A monastery established by the Nyingma yogi, Chatral Sangye Dorji Rinpoche
A large Buddhist monastery in the Nyingma tradition.
It houses many beautiful idols of Advaita Acharya, Lord Narasimha, Lord Chaitanya and many more.
A monastery is in the Nyingma tradition of Tibetan Buddhism. Accommodation available at the compound.
Inaugurated by the Dalai Lama in 1999, and belongs to the Kagyu tradition of Tibetan Buddhism.
A monastery in the Nyingma tradition of Tibetan Buddhism

do.d: An amusement and theme park.
The Siliguri section of the Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary with tigers, leopards, elephants, and herbivorous. Elephant rides. Forest park setting.
Dagapur (near Darjeeling More). An amusement and water park among tea plantations.
A river runs along this park with kids’ rides, play equipment, shade trees and a miniature train. It also hosts many alternative energy exhibitions and picnic areas.

Sirkazhi.x: Sirkazhi is a small town in the Southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is situated near the banks of the river Kollidam (Coleroon). This picturesque town has a beautiful and spotlessly clean Shiva temple.

see.d: Vishnu Temple, one of the 108 divya desams. Trivikraman, the deity here is Vishnu in his avatar as Vamana, wherein he asked for 3 footsteps of Land and went onto measure all 3 worlds.
There are 12 Divya Desams (temples of Lord Vishnu) which are situated in and around Thirunangur, which is about 20 km from Sirkazhi.
One of the most important Saivite shrines of southern TN. It's enclosed within tall granite walls, in the centre of the town.

Sitamarhi.x: Sitamarhi is a city in the northern part of Bihar in India. A part of Gangetic Plains of north India, Sitamarhi is located around 50 km from Nepal. The city and places around are very active culturally and politically but one of the poorest in India based on almost all social indicators.

see.d: 8 km from Pupri on Madhwapur road. A proposed girl's high school is coming up. Has one of the oldest middle schools in Bihar. Choraut is 5 km from here.
18n km north east to Sitamarhi.

Sitapur.x: Sitapur is a city in Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: A popular temple. Durga Pooja (10 days) is celebrated here.
huge temple of Lord Shiva
a famous temple

Sivakasi.x: Sivakasi is a town in Tamil Nadu, India.

Solan.x: Solan town is a city in Himachal Pradesh. Located on the Punjab-Himachal Border, Solan is nestled in the Shivalik hills of the Himalayas. Solan has ancient temples and monasteries, and the city has one of the oldest breweries in the country.

see.d: A Lord Krishna temple.
About 7 km from D.C. office, this is the temple near Apple weldmesh industry. Major attraction on Rajgarh road
A small park providing greenery and pretty mountain views.
The park spreads over 40 acres of land on the right bank of river Ashwani. It lies in Hart Village which takes a detour of around 6 km from the main highway after Salogra.

Sidhbari.x: Sidhbari (pronounced Sidh-badi meaning "The valley of sages") is a scenic village and bazaar on the outskirts of Lower Dharamshala along the feet of the Himalayan Dhauladhar mountain range in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. According to ancient scriptures, Sidhbari has been home to numerous saints which is how it got its name as a place for the Siddhas or those who are enlightened. Swami Chinmayananda established his ashram here in 1977 called Sandeepany Himalayas and is also the site of his samadhi.

Shornur.x: Shornur (Shoranur) is a small railway town in Palakkad District, Malabar, Kerala, India. Shornur is three kilometers from Kalamandalam, a cultural centre where the dance forms Kathakali and Koodiyattam are performed.

Sivasailam.x: Sivasailam is a village in the district of Tenkasi near Kadayam, Tamil Nadu, India. The village is located 55 km west of Tirunelveli town and 25 km from Tenkasi.

see.d: A temple dedicated to the God Siva.

Siddhpur.x: Siddhpur is in North Gujarat, India.

see.d: Ruined temple was dedicated to Rudra, a form of the Hindu deity Shiva. It was built by the Chaulukya (Solanki) rulers of Gujarat and took nearly 175 years and three generation of rulers…
Opened in 2017, it has three galleries presenting religious and ritual significance as well as history and society of the region.
Mansions in European influenced architecture are largely belonging to Dawoodi Bohra trading community and spread over 18 mohallas or neighbourhoods in Najampura and Hassanpura.
A small artificial tank considered pious by Hindus. According to Hindu theology, there are five sacred lakes; collectively called Panch-Sarovar; Mansarovar, Bindu Sarovar, Narayan Sarovar,…
An ancient place associated with Natha Sampradaya.

see.n: Siddheshwar Mahadev temple and Moksha Peepal tree
see.d: The Saraswati river is nearby and the riverfront has been developed for rituals.

South Konkan.x: South Konkan is the southern coast of Maharashtra, India.

Shyamnagar.x: Shyamnagar is a town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal.

see.d: A temple complex consisting of a nine-pinnacled temple and three Shiva temples. It was built by Gopimohan Tagore, a relative of Rabindranath Tagore, in May 1813.

Sikar.x: Sikar is a town at the southern part of Shekhawati in Rajasthan.

Srikalahasti.x: Srikalahasti is located near the pilgrimage town of Tirupati in southern Andhra Pradesh, and is visited by thousands of pilgrims. This temple is also associated with Rahu and Ketu of the nine grahams or celestial bodies in the Indian astrological scheme, also known as the moon's nodes in astronomical terms.

see.d: Sri Kalahasti is one of the five Panchaboota Sthallas i.e. place representing one of the five elements of nature. Kalahasti represents Vayu (Wind).
Lord Ganapathi in a temple below the earth.

Solapur.x: Solapur is a city in Maharashtra in India. It is famous for its textile products and leads in beedi industries (a traditional type of cigarette), and has been a major trade city due to its routes from Karnataka and Maharashtra. It is home to a famous temple, the Shri Siddheshwari Temple.

do.d: Dattatraya devastan, Sangam

Sonipat.x: Sonipat or Sonepat is an ancient town in South Haryana.

see.d: Baba dham' is the main attractive religious temple and status symbol of Sonipat. It is a very neat and clean temple with many small temples within such as Sani Mandir, Sai Mander, Radha…
Red sandstone and 'kankar' block monument with highly decorated floral ceiling.
Religious followers have visited here for centuries in order to pray at the lotus feet of Mata Shri Chhinnamastika Devi.
At the outskirts of the city one can enjoy the site of Mughal Buildings which lie unprotected.
A very religious site as well as a popular tourist destination.
One of the oldest temples in Sonipat.

do.d: Mojoland is a picnic destination with a lot of adventures, such as a water park, amusement park, aero sports park, snow park, and theme park.

Sri City.x: Sri City or Sricity is a business city at Tada about 55 km north of Chennai on NH 5 along the border of Andhra Pradesh (AP) and Tamil Nadu (TN) States of India. Much of Sri City lies in Chittoor District and a small part in Nellore District of AP, adjacent to Tiruvallur District of TN. The Satish Dhawan Space Centre (aka SHAR), India’s satellite and rocket launching centre is situated at Sriharikota, which is on the eastern side of the Pulicat Lake separating Sri City and the satellite launching station.

see.d: 100m waterfalls

Srikakulam.x: Srikakulam, a city in northern of Andhra Pradesh, is known for its Buddhist sites. It was known as Chicacole in colonial times.

see.d: One of the few sun temples in India.
Sri Kurmam is a small village just outside the city, which has a famous temple dedicated to Sri Kurmanatha, second avatar of Lord Vishnu.
A Buddhist site with stupas, said to be associated with the Battle of Kalinga by Ashoka, as Danthavarapukota was the capital of Kalinga.

Srinagar.x: Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley is the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir and the largest city in the Kashmir region.

see.d: Dal Lake is one of the prime attractions of Srinagar. At the very centre of the city, the lake covers an area of 21 km², which includes 3 km² of wetland.
Unlike the other three parts of Dal Lake the Nagin Lake is a separate lake connected to the Dal Lake by a narrow water channel.
Rupa Lank, literally meaning silver island, is in the Dod Dal (central area of Dal Lake). The man-made island was constructed by Murad Baksh, brother of the last Mughal emperor, Aurangzeb.
Sona Lank, literally meaning gold island, is located in Lokut Dal, in the northern part of Dal Lake. It is next to the shrine of Hazarat Bal.
A well-maintained park with lake by Dept of Floriculture with organised parking lot next to the park.
Located on the eastern side of the Dal Lake, the Tulip Garden covers an area of 30 ha (74 acres) and is the largest tulip garden of Asia.

do.d: The musical fountain along with laser show was inaugurated in April 2019. It runs three times a day after 7 pm and consists of a 15-minute show.
Home to the critically endangered Kashmir stag (hangul). Grasslands, alpine meadows, waterfalls and craggy cliffs provide a home for various species of mammals such as the Himalayan black…
A Ramsar site and a bird sanctuary.

Srirangam.x: Srirangam, an island 10 km (6.2 mi) north of Tiruchirappalli in Central Tamil Nadu, is famous for the Ranganathaswamy Temple, one of the largest Hindu temples in India.

see.d: The deity of the temple is the sleeping form of Lord Vishnu. It has 21 gopurams and the biggest of them is 73 m high. The temple complex area is .
Famous Shiva temple and one of the five "pancha bhuta" sites (five elements namely water, earth, air, fire and ether). This one is appu sthala (representing water).

do.d: Large park featuring a glass butterfly house, landscaped gardens, a fountain and an eatery.

Srirangapatna.x: Srirangapatna, anglicised to Seringapatam during the British Raj, is a town in Mandya district of Karnataka, India. On an island in the Cauvery River, the town of Srirangapatna was once the fortress capital of the region controlled by Hyder Ali and his son Tipu Sultan.

see.d: This is the biggest attraction. Entrance from 9AM to 4PM. It was constructed in 1784 and is made of teak. Today, it is a museum devoted to Tipu Sultan.
This tomb and mosque were built by Tipu Sultan as a tribute to his illustrious father Hyder Ali (1722 - 1784), after his death. The dome is at the eastern extreme of Srirangapatna.
Confluence of holy rivers. Coracle riding facility. Very green surroundings. Salted fruits are available.
Beautiful viewpoint and ancient temple 2,697 feet above sea level.
Beautiful surroundings with an ancient temple. Cute cafe in the middle of sugarcane fields.
Beautiful church built in 1802.

do.d: The lawns of the summer palace are extremely spacious and peaceful. Ideal for a picnic. There are many big trees giving a lot of shade.
Take the third left street on the right side of the KSRTC bus station. The road goes to Wellesley Bridge and there is a cute little seating place just before the bridge.
The front and back sides of the railway station are suitable for silent walking as they are not touristy places. The railway station itself is very silent as it is not used by the tourists.
The Juma Masjidh Junction has beautiful stone seats which are suitable for sitting and enjoying the lifestyle of the local people. This junction also has two temples.
₹150 for one round. The track on the opposite of the first parking lot.

Srivilliputhur.x: Srivilliputhur is a temple town, 75 km (47 mi) from Madurai, 20 km (12 mi) from Sivakasi near the Western Ghats in India.

see.d: This is a Shiva Temple dedicated to Sri Vaidhyanatha Swamy.
A wildlife sanctuary on the foot hills of the Western ghats.
A popular Hindu temple and one of the 108 Divya Desams, and the most important abodes of Lord Vishnu.
A Vaishnav Temple on the hillock near Western Ghats - attracting good crowds during Saturdays, especially in October / November.

Sultanpur National Park.x: Sultanpur National Park is in Haryana state of India.

Sunabeda.x: Sunabeda is one of the coldest region of Odisha, ideal for summer seasons holiday spenders. The small township is spread across 10 square kilometers and house only families that are directly or indirectly associated with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. The entire township is well planned and is a neat place.

see.d: National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO) is Asia's largest integrated aluminium complex, it draws its raw material, bauxite, from Panchapatmali mines nearby, NALCO has a smelter at Angul.

Surat.x: Surat, a bustling commercial city in South Gujarat, is a major gemstone centre with over 92% of the world's diamonds being cut here. On the banks of the Tapi River, Surat was a major port in medieval India as well as the early British colonial times till the formation of the city of Bombay (present-day Mumbai). It is the second-largest city in Gujarat with a population of nearly seven million (2025), and an example of both the boom in Gujarat's development and a continuation of the state's historical role as a centre of the mass production of high quality textiles.

see.d: The Jain temple was constructed during the regime of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in 1699 AD. It is at Muglisara, near mausoleum of Mirjan Sami.
at City Light Road near Parle Point. Has a planetarium, science models, art gallery & museum (shifted from Chowk Sardar Patel Museum.)
Surat is largely recognized for its textile and diamond businesses: 92% of the world's diamonds are cut and polished in Surat. Lots of diamond factory at Varachha road.
on Karatgam Road
The ancient Dutch gardens, the Dutch cemetery and Makaipul, the old original port from where the ships sailed to other parts of the world are other attractions.
People can spend some private time there with their loved one. Lake View Restaurant is also good one

do.d: Visit for water sports. Causeway is a low level check dam build on the River Tapi. Water sports facility is available in the upstream water.

Surathkal.x: Surathkal is a suburb of Mangalore city in Karnataka state of India. Surathkal used to be a separate town, but is now merged to Mangalore city corporation. Surathkal lies in revenue district of Dakshina Kannada.

Surendranagar.x: Surendranagar is a city and a district in the Saurashtra region of the state of Gujarat in India.

Susunia.x: Susunia is a hill in the Bankura district of West Bengal and a place of archaeological interest and a rock climbing centre. It is a picnic spot for people residing in the surrounding areas.

see.d: The spring water is believed to have medicinal properties
Rivulet flowing over the rocks
4th century stone inscription of King Chandravarman

Suri.x: Suri or Siuri is the headquarters of the Birbhum district of West Bengal.

see.d: One of the oldest and the finest temples in West Bengal.

Sukna.x: Sukna is a cantonment town in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, close to Siliguri.

see.d: A spacious park known for its manicured lawns, pathways and children's play areas.

Sribhumi.x: Sribhumi, formerly Karimganj, is a border town in the Barak Valley region of Assam.

Central Travancore.x: Central Travancore is in Kerala in India.

Northern Tamil Nadu.x: Northern Tamil Nadu consists of Chengalpattu, Chennai, Cuddalore, Kallakurichi, Kanchipuram, Ranipet, Tirupathur, Tiruvallur, Tiruvannamalai, Vellore and Viluppuram districts. The northeastern part of the region forms the Chennai Metropolitan Area (CMA).

Swamithoppe.x: Swamithoppe (alternate spelling Swamithope) is a town that lies southeast of the City of Nagercoil, the capital of the District of Kanyakumari in the State of Tamil Nadu, at the extreme southern tip of India. Swamithope lies about half-way between the cities of Nagercoil and Kanniyakumari on the Nagercoil-Kanniyakumari road. It also lies 8 km (5 mi) north-west of Cape Comerin.

Tada.x: Tada is a town on the Chennai-Nellore highway, just over 65 km from Chennai, India and 80 km from Tirupathi. It is in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh and is about 1.5 km north of the Andhra Pradesh border.

Taliparamba.x: Taliparamba or Thaliparamba is a town in Kannur District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, India.

see.d: Established in 1905 by Sir Charles Alfred Barber, this is the oldest continuously-operating government farm in Kerala. The farm has a rich bio diversity in 56 acres.
Riverside Temple, Snake Park, Water Theme Park.
Magnificent campus with many gardens and laboratories. Visitors can make an appointment with the Principal over the telephone.
Syed Nagar village is a very beautiful place with cute undulating open landscape ideal for a peaceful evening walk.
Scenic surroundings.
A temple mentioned in many Malayalam devotional songs.

do.d: Access from the Pacheni Road and come back through the Mukkola Road. You have seen all the greenery now.
All coconut and arecanut. Beautiful bridge wide enough for a small car.
Take a bus to Payangadi, then to Mattool and then to Madakkara and Irinavu. A lot of water bodies and scenic places can be seen on the way. You can come back through the Dharmasala route.
Wide, wide stretch of paddy fields. Take a bus going to Payangadi via Kuppam junction. Get down at the most beautiful spot. Continue the journey in another bus.
Turn left at Kuppam before the bridge

Tamil Nadu.x: Tamil Nadu, the land of Tamils, is a state in the south of India known for its temples and architecture, food, movies and classical Indian dance and Carnatic music. It is the historical home of the famous Chera, Chola, Pandya and Pallava kingdoms which thrived in ancient and medieval India.

Telangana.x: Telangana, a state in Southern India, is the youngest of the country; having split from Andhra Pradesh in 2014. However, don't let the newness of the state deceive you, as Telangana is rich in cultural heritage, with its history being marked by a succession of dynasties and cultural influences; from the Kakatiyas and Bahmanis to the Qutb Shahis and Mughals, and finally the Nizams of Hyderabad. The state of Telangana is bordered by the states of Maharashtra to the north and north-west, Karnataka to the west, Chhattisgarh to the north-east, and Andhra Pradesh to the south and east.

Thalassery.x: Thalassery (or Tellicherry), is a city in Kannur District. Thalassery is known as the political and cultural capital of Malabar. It is the centre of progressive political and literary movements.

see.d: The 5-acre (20,000 m²) island covered with coconut palms and dense bushes is a beautiful sight from the Muzhappilangad beach.
Residence of Rev. Dr. Herman Gundert, a German missionary and great scholar, author of first Malayalam dictionary. He settled in the bungalow in 1839 and stayed there for two decades.
Built by Rev. Dr. Herman Gundert in 1839. The church building represents an amalgamation of Kerala architecture and colonial style.
The name literally translates into Garden Mosque as it was built on a sugarcane plantation purchased from the Dutch East India Company.
Multi-level landscaped recreational park which commands sweeping views of Arabian Sea. It was an initiative of E.N.

Thiruvananthapuram.x: Near the southern tip of mainland India, Thiruvananthapuram, formerly and often still known as Trivandrum, is the capital city of Kerala in Southern India. Tirupati.x: Tirupati is the spiritual capital of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is most famous for its Sri Venkateswara Temple dedicated to Vishnu, also known as Balaji in Northern India and Govinda in Southern India. The temple is on top of Tirumala hills, while the town is in the foothills.

Tiruppur.x: Tiruppur is a city in Tamil Nadu, south India. It is known as the knitwear capital of India because the city accounts for 90% of India's cotton knitwear exports from the country.

Tirur.x: Tirur is a town in Malappuram District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, in India. The town is 43 km south of Kozhikode. It is a major trading centre of fish and betel, and is known as the birthplace of the poet Thunchath Ezhuthachan.

see.d: Birth place of the great poet Thunchath Ezhuthachan, considered as the Father of the Malayalam literature.

Tiruttani.x: Tiruttani is in Tiruvallur district of northern Tamil Nadu, India. It is most famous for its Sri Subramanya Temple dedicated to Murugan, on top of Tiruttani hills, while the town is on the foothills.

Tiruvallur.x: Tiruvallur is a town in the southern state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is nearly 45 km west of Chennai, the capital city of Tamil Nadu. It is en route to Tirupati, the abode of Lord Balaji.
