The hill here is considered to be a manifestation of Shiva. Tiruvannamalai is one of the Panchabhoota Stalams signifying the 5 elements of wind (Kalahasti), water (Tiruvanaikkal), fire (Tiruvannamalai), earth (Thiruvarur) and space (Chidambaram).

Thiruvarur.x: Thiruvarur, the headquarters of the Thiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu, was an important Chola town, as Manu Needhi Chola ruled from here. It is also the birthplace of Carnatic musicians Tyagaraja, Muthuswamy Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri.

Thoothukudi.x: Thoothukudi, formerly Tuticorin, is a city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Tripura.x: Tripura, one of the seven north-eastern states of India, is one of the least explored regions of India by tourists, but it offers immense natural beauty and an intriguing cultural heritage. A mix of Bengali and tribal populations, Tripura is bordered by Bangladesh in the south, west, and north, Assam in the northeast, and Mizoram in the east.

Tulu phrasebook.x: Tulu is a regional language spoken in coastal districts of Karnataka, i.e. Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and some areas of Kasaragod District . It is the 24th most populous Indian language according to the 2001 census of India.

Udaipur.x: Udaipur is the capital of the district of Mewar in Rajasthan, India. Udaipur is famous for its lakes, palaces, forts, temples, gardens, and romantic backdrops. It was the setting of many movies, including the 13th James Bond film, Octopussy.

Varanasi.x: Varanasi, also known as Banaras or Kashi, is a holy city at the banks of the Ganges River in Uttar Pradesh, India. see.d: This Gothic church was raised to the status of a basilica in 1962 by Pope John XXIII. A beautiful museum is attached to the church.

Vellore.x: Vellore is a city of 505,000 people (2011) in Tamil Nadu, India. Visitors are drawn by its large 16th-century fort, which is known for its grand ramparts, wide moat and robust masonry. Apart from Fort tourism, Christian Medical College due to its esteemed position in the country, both as a medical college and a hospital, invites many students, medical practitioners, and patients from around the country.

see.d: A large forested area near Javathu mountain. Amirthi Falls and Amirthi Zoo can be found here.
Dedicated to Sri Lakshmi Narayani or Maha Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, in 2007. The temple has covered in intricate work done by artisans specialising in temple art using gold.
This temple to Lord Shiva is a fine example of Vijayanagaram Architecture. The temple has exquisite carvings on its gopuram (tower), richly carved stone pillars, large wooden gates and…
Temple dedicated to Lord Murugan with a huge statue of him also nearby
These are abandoned cliff top remains of forts built by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. This is recommended only for those with strength as it's accessible only via foot.
Murugan Temple on Palamathi Hill

Veraval.x: Veraval-Somnath is a city on the west coast of India in the Junagadh district in the state of Gujarat. The Somnath Temple in the Prabhas Kshetra, near Veraval, is the most sacred of the twelve Jyotirlings (lingas of light) of the God Shiva.

see.d: It is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. Three aartis (ritual) performed daily; at 7AM, at noon and at 7PM.

Vidarbha.x: Vidarbha, also known as Berar, is the easternmost region of Maharashtra, India. Although Maharashtra as a whole is considered a western state, geographically Vidarbha is very much at the centre of the country, on the Deccan Plateau.

Vijayawada.x: Vijayawada or Bezawada, the second-largest city in Andhra Pradesh, is the state's major commercial hub, on the upper banks of the Krishna River, opposite the state capital Amaravati. Famous for the Kanaka Durga Temple that attracts millions every year, Vijayawada is a part of the "Capital Region" (CR) of Andhra Pradesh, with almost all the amenities a traveller might need.

see.d: This temple is on a hill (Indrakeeladri) overlooking the city and the River Krishna. One can either motor up the ghat road or take the steps on foot.
The first Gandhi Memorial with seven stupas in the country was constructed on this hill at a height of 500 ft (150 m). The 52 ft (16 m) stupa was unveiled on 6 October 1968 by Dr.
Bhavani Island is on Krishna River close to the city. AP Tourism is converting this 133-acre (54-hectare) island into a tourist spot and a river-front resort.
Built across the river Krishna connecting this city with Amaravati, Prakasam Barrage has created a panoramic lake. Its three canals that run through the city give Vijayawada a Venetian look.
Created by the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation with great care, this park is at the entrance of the city and features an impressive horticultural network.
A group of 7th-century rock-cut caves dedicated to Shiva.

Virudhaachalam.x: Virudhaachalam is a town in the Cuddalore to Salem Highway next to Neyveli in Tamil Nadu state in India. It is primarily a pilgrimage centre with an enormous Shiva temple, the Viruthagiriswarar temple, from which the name arose. The town is a good travel planning centre because it is linked to all the cities in Tamil Nadu by broad gauge railway network and good wide access roads.

see.d: A Shiva temple.
Built for Lord Murugan. You can give grievance to God for fulfilling your wishes, and once your wishes get fulfilled you can withdraw it. The temple has peacocks and deer.
Built for Lord Muruga.
Palamalai Nathar Temple east 5 km near Veddeper Kovil.

Virudhunagar.x: Virudhunagar is a district of southern Tamil Nadu.

Visakhapatnam.x: Visakhapatnam, popularly known as Vizag (vigh-ZAG), is the largest city in Andhra Pradesh. It is primarily an industrial city, but also attracts tourists due to its unspoilt sandy beaches, well built and maintained parks, Buddhist sites and nearby scenic areas, such as Araku Valley. The city has a population of about 2 million.

see.d: A lighthouse providing an aerial view of the port and the city.
The ride to this hill offers a spectacular view of the sea. There is a park atop the hill, with a beautiful view of the city, the sea and Eastern Ghats merging into the sea.
A crafts village showcasing and preserving the old, including woodwork, jewellery, clothes and local crafts of rural India.
A summer residential palace of the royal family of Jeypore, and one of the most iconic historical buildings of the city.
A museum in a decommissioned submarine of the Indian Navy. This is the first of its kind in South Asia. This submarine is one of the earliest submarines procured from Russia.
It has marine and freshwater fish. The exit gate of the aquarium resembles the open mouth of a huge white tipped shark. 'Kala Shrusti', a handicrafts shop, is atop the aquarium.

do.d: The most popular beach of Visakhapatnam where you can find the locals hanging out during the hot summers, and relatively less hot winters.
11 km away from the city, this has become a popular tourist spot that even the locals frequent. A lot safer to wade into than the R.K.
It is perceived as a private beach but actually it is not. Tourists can visit the beach directly or through the village. Yarada is the village behind the dolphin's nose.
The zoo is home to native mammals like elephants, one-horned rhinos, tigers, lions, leopards, striped hyenas, dholes, sloth bears, gaurs, sambar deer and rhesus macaques, as well as exotic…
A gorgeous nature preserve that many people in Vizag itself seem to be unaware of. Kambalakonda is uncrowded and peaceful and within 20-25 minutes drive from the city centre.

Vrindavan.x: Vrindavan, also spelled Brindavan, is a holy town at the banks of the Yamuna River, in the Braj region of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

see.d: The best-known temple in Vrindavan, home to a Krishna idol known as Thakur-ji. The idol's eyes are said to be so powerful that it is kept hidden from view behind a curtain, which is opened…
It resembles the Tajmahal, built with white marble. It is a unique temple in that you are prohibited from donating if you are a non-vegetarian.
Better known as the ISKCON Temple. A major draw for Hare Krishna (ISKCON) pilgrims to India, and uniquely among Vrindavan's temples well equipped to deal with foreign visitors.
The temple was constructed in 2012. There are fantastic light shows and designs. The light show closes at 7:30PM in the winter days, and at 8PM in the summer.
A very well-known ancient temple of Vrindavan, founded by Shri Hith Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Sri Radhavallabh Lal's idol resemble Sri Radha and Sri Krishna to be embodied in it together: "One…
The single largest temple in Vrindavan, built in 1851 in a South Indian style, complete with intricate seven-story gopuram (gateway) at the entrance.

do.d: Krishna rested with His beloved Sri Radha. The shrine inside has a bed, which is decorated with flowers by the priest every evening.

Walayar.x: Walayar is a small developing town, in the Ernakulam District of Kerala, India. It is near the border between the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu on NH 47 where the sales tax, motor vehicles check post, and excise check posts are. Due to the high traffic on this route (most of the goods import into Kerala happens through road and predominantly through this road), the place has also become notorious for the traffic jams.

Warangal.x: Warangal is in East Telangana in Southern India. Historically known as Orugallu and also Ekashila Nagaram (City carved in single stone). Warangal is part of a tertiary city including Kazipet and Hanamkonda cities.

see.d: One of the oldest temples for Goddess Bhadrakali, believed to be built in 625 AD by King Pulakeshin II of Chalukya dynasty.
Built in the 18th century.
Built in the 3rd century.
Renovated in 2004.

Wazirpur.x: Wazirpur is a village in the Bharatpur Division of Rajasthan.

Virpur.x: Virpur is a village 53 km from Rajkot reached through highway NH-8b.

Vatakara.x: Vatakara, Badagara or Vadagara is a town in the Kozhikode District of the Malabar region, in the state of Kerala, India.

see.d: Established in 1864
Famous for the Dhwaja Prathishta
Rock-cut caves, murals and carvings. 1500 years old. Very famous temple in Malabar side, associated with the famous Kerala Ballards (Vakkum Pattu) and with the heroic deeds of the Thacholi…
Scenic hill top ideal to watch the sunset.
The dam site is open for visitors from 8:30AM to 5:00PM.
Beautiful sunsets

Vidisha.x: Vidisha is a historic city in Madhya Pradesh, India. Known for its ancient temples, archaeological sites, and cultural heritage, Vidisha is a must-visit destination for history enthusiasts and travellers exploring central India. Located about 60 km northeast of Bhopal, Vidisha is often overshadowed by the nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sanchi, but it holds its own as a treasure trove of ancient history and architecture.

Vizianagaram.x: Vizianagaram is a city 40 km (25 mi) north-northeast of Visakhapatnam in northern Andhra Pradesh.

see.d: An early 18th-century square-shaped fort, built by Maharaja Vijaya Rama Raju in 1713. It has two main gates, of which the main entrance is elaborately decorated.
The iconic octagonal clock tower of Vizianagaram. Built in 1885, the tower was partly inspired by the Big Ben in London.
The central lake of Vizianagaram.
Despite being newer than the Vizianagaram Raj era, Ramanarayanam is one of the most-visited attractions in and around the city, attracting millions of pilgrims.

Yelagiri.x: Yelagiri (also spelt Elagiri on some signboards) is a town in Tamil Nadu, a state in the south of India. Yelagiri, at a height of 920 metres above sea level, stands majestically amidst four mountains. This is a hill station with a salubrious climate prevailing throughout the year so that winters do not keep visitors away.

see.d: Yellagiri Hills. Fr. Guezou, who is the founder of this Don Bosco Center has come from France and has been helping the poor people for many years.

Yadgir.x: Yadgir, also known as Yadagiri, is a town in Karnataka. It is dotted with many historical monuments and has a majestic hill fort with three rounds of fortifications. There are three ancient temples, medieval mosques, tanks and wells on top of the hill.

see.d: Stands on the top of a 100-meter (328 feet) tall monolith

Yadagirigutta.x: Yadagirigutta is a Hindu pilgrimage site near Bhongir in West Telangana. It is often called the "Tirupati of Telangana" for its spiritual significance.

see.d: The hilltop Hindu town that draws pilgrims to the town. The temple is dedicated to the god Narasimha, an Avatar of Vishnu.

VAPI: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
